The first decomposition places data-name-1 exactly when no variable-length member precedes it; when one does, the maximum's fixed run leaves that member too little of the record, so when data-name-1 does not read back the count it was decomposed at, the record is decomposed at the SMALLEST count, from the table's minimum, at which data-name-1 reads that count back (the take step's own preference for the earlier member), and at the first count again when none does. The decomposition is (ii)'s take step, exact for a record with one variable-length member at that count and otherwise giving the earlier member the excess, as (ii) states. The same layout locates an indexed or sort key (at the extent table's count, else at the maximum). **Rejected readings:** refusing the record (the previous loud; no rule forbids it, and every other variable-length record already round-trips); taking the count from the record's length (it has none to give); the maximum alone for a record that carries no table (it splits a one-occurrence record into the wrong positions, where data-name-1 recovers it exactly). **(ix) A record whose OCCURS DEPENDING table of fixed-image elements is counted in BITS** (kb/Work PB3030) — a USAGE BIT item lies beneath it, and §8.5.1.6.3 places a bit item *"at the next bit position in storage"*, so its occurrences share bytes — sends the member that holds the table to the ceiling, in characters, of its bits at the sending count (§15.50.4 rule 9's rounding), and its record layout states the table as the last component in CHARACTERS from the character that holds the table's first bit, one character per unit (`OdoTail.RecordUnit` / `RecordMaxUnits`): the record's length then says the table's character extent, which is all a record of characters can say, since an occurrence that shares a byte has no character boundary of its own. A READ / RETURN takes the record's characters whole, as (ii) takes any trailing component; the bits of the last character past the count are whatever the writer's image held there, as they are past the count of any sending group. A receiving group that uses only part of such a table (§13.18.38.4 GR8 a) keeps its later occurrences at the BIT (`OdoTail.KeepUnused`), its declared struct and its storage cell alike. **Rejected readings:** one element per unit in characters (a bit occurrence is not a character, and the per-occurrence character width rounded up overstates the table); refusing the shape (the previous named stage COBOL1756; no rule forbids it). One producer — `OdoModel.FixedImageTail`, read by `GroupImageCodec` and by a cell-backed group's `VarGroupWindow`. **(x) A LINE SEQUENTIAL file carries no extent table, and what the standard asks of its READ is the contiguous image and nothing finer** (kb/Work PB1563; a record with two or more dynamic-length members, which `"AA" "KEY" "CCCC"` under `LIMIT 9` / `X(3)` / `LIMIT 8` reads back as `"AAKEYC" "CCC" ""`). *The derivation.* **(1) A line is plain text.** §12.4.5.10.3 GR2: *"Each record in a line sequential file is terminated by an implementor-defined line delimiter"*, and §9.1.7.2: *"In line sequential files the length of each record is determined by the number of characters between the preceding line delimiter and the following line delimiter or the end of file if no line delimiter is present"* - every character between two delimiters IS the record, so (v)'s table has nowhere to live, and an encoding written INTO the line (a separator or a length field) would hand a second program that reads the file as `PIC X(n)` characters the writer never wrote, exactly the reading (vi) rejects for a fixed-length file; and the only characters such an encoding could use are the ones below U+0020, which are outside the line sequential character set (A.1 item 115) - a WRITE of a record that holds one is '71' (§14.9.51.4 GR23), so the encoding would also be indistinguishable from data. GR2's *"The range of allowable characters in a line sequential file is implementor-defined"* licenses the SET of characters, never information added beside the record (that licence is §9.1.7.2's, for RECORD sequential files only). **(2) What the READ must deliver.** §14.9.30.4 GR13 c): *"the record is made available in the record area"*, with GR15 padding it on the right with spaces to the record descriptions' minimum size (every dynamic member at zero length, §13.18.43.4 GR8 a)) or truncating it at their maximum ('06'); and §8.5.1.11.2: a variable-length item *"behaves in all respects as though it were in fact contiguous with its neighbors whenever a procedural operation is applied to a group containing it"*. So after the READ the group's contiguous image - what DISPLAY, MOVE, a comparison and `FUNCTION LENGTH` (§15.50.4 rule 7) see - is EXACTLY the line, padded or truncated by GR15. That holds for every line by construction: the take step only ever PARTITIONS the image. **(3) Where one dynamic member ends and the next begins inside that image is stated by no rule**: §8.5.1.12.2's correspondence (*"start at the same relative byte positions within their groups"*) relates two groups' storage, not a medium, and no READ rule speaks of members. It is the implementor's. GnuCOBOL, IBM Enterprise COBOL and Micro Focus do not admit a dynamic-length item in the file section (above), so there is nothing to follow (CLAUDE.md rule 1) and the choice is (ii)'s take step - the one split every medium without a table uses, so a record is decomposed the same way whether it arrives from a line, a block file written by another program or a sort store. It is exact for a record with ONE dynamic member wherever it sits, and for any record whose earlier members were written at their maximum; otherwise the earlier member takes the excess and the member lengths differ from the ones written, with the record itself unchanged. The write side is the same convention as (vi)'s: §14.9.51.4 GR21 does not transfer *"any spaces to the right of the rightmost non-space character"*, so trailing spaces of the last member are padding, not data, and a WRITE, a REWRITE (GR17 sends no table either) and the sort's USING and GIVING transfers to or from a line sequential file all agree. **(4) No diagnostic is required**: no rule of §12.4.5.10.3, §14.9.30.4 or §8.5.1.11 makes the repartitioning an error or asks for a warning, a layout with one dynamic member loses nothing, and the compiler cannot tell which layout the program's lines will hold, so none is issued. A program that needs member-exact round trips uses a file that frames its records (record sequential, relative or indexed: (v)). **Rejected readings:** an in-line encoding (above); a sidecar file holding the table (a second file the standard does not know, lost when the line file is copied or edited); refusing the source (no rule forbids the record; CLAUDE.md rule 3); a different split for lines only (a second rule for the same ambiguity). **The REWRITE sibling** (found with it): §14.9.35.4 GR17 a) refuses a REWRITE only after a READ that transferred PART of the line, and the connector decided "part" against the record area's character window (`RecordWidth`, the fixed run of a variable-length group) where GR15 truncates at the descriptions' MAXIMUM size (`FileConnector.MaxRecordSize`), so a whole 9-character line of a 3-character fixed run made every REWRITE of that record '44'; `SequentialConnector.NextFrame` now asks the one bound the READ's truncation asks. **The READ '09' sibling** (found by the branch review): §14.9.30.4 GR16's *"the record area contains one or more characters not in the implementor-defined character set for a line sequential file"* asks about the DELIVERED record area, which for a variable-length group is the whole contiguous line and not its fixed run, so `SequentialConnector` asks the character set of the delivered line at its own width (a control character in a dynamic member past the fixed run is '09' exactly as the WRITE's GR23 and the REWRITE's GR17 d) answer '71' for it). Witnessed by `conformance:cases/12.4.5.10-ORGANIZATION/pb1563_line_sequential_dynamic_members` (the success paths and the statuses '00', '06', '10', '44', '46', '47', '48', '71', with a USE procedure and FILE STATUS, and with FILE STATUS alone), by `conformance:cases/12.4.5.10-ORGANIZATION/pb1563_line_sequential_dynamic_members_exceptions` (READ '09' past and inside the fixed run and in the remainder of an over-length line; REWRITE '43', '49', '71' and the unchanged line; '51' on a READ, a READ with RETRY and a REWRITE against a record another connector locked, and the REWRITE that succeeds once the lock moved; a SORT whose USING file is absent, '35', and whose GIVING file cannot be created, '30') and, for the exceptions that have neither a FILE STATUS nor a USE procedure and so end the run unit (§9.1.13.1 - '46', '43', '71', and the SORT's '35'), by `LineSequentialDynamicMembersAbnormalTests`; and by the refusal `conformance:cases/12.4.5.10-ORGANIZATION/pb1563-line-sequential-dynamic-members-below-2023`. Implemented once — `FileModel.IsOutOfLineRecord`,
  `DataBinder.LinkImplicitRecordArea`, `SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRecordAreaStore`, `OperandText.RecordSendImage`,
  `CobolVarGroup.FromContiguous`, and for (v) `RecordExtents`, `CobolContiguousLayout.ExtentsOf` / `Decompose`,
  `RecordFraming` (the frame's extent table), `OperandText.RecordAreaExtents` (FILES_DESIGN D27); witnessed
  by `conformance:cases/13.18.33-Level-number/pb981_fd_variable_length_records`, `conformance:cases/13.18.33-Level-number/pb981_fd_pointer_record`,
  `conformance:cases/13.18.22-EXTERNAL/pb1026_external_out_of_line_records`, `conformance:cases/A.1-Implementor-defined-language-element-list/pb1053_dynamic_members_both_sides` and
  `unit:RecordExtentsTests`.
- **D-KWV — the byte positions of a key that follows a variable-length member of its record** (2026-09-22; kb/Work
  PB1025). A SORT/MERGE key (§14.9.40.3 SR6 / §14.9.24.3 SR4) and an indexed RECORD KEY / ALTERNATE RECORD KEY
  (§12.4.5.12 / §12.4.5.6) are byte positions of the record, and a record with a dynamic-length member is sent and
  held as its contiguous image (§8.5.1.11.2; D-FRA (iii)), so a key that such a member PRECEDES sits at a different
  position in each record. The standard bounds it — *"all the data items identified by key data-names shall be
  contained within the first x bytes of the record, where x equals the minimum record size"* (§14.9.40.3 SR6 g);
  the same sentence is §14.9.24.3 SR4 g), §12.4.5.12.3 SR4 and §12.4.5.6.3 SR5) — and says nothing more.
  **WiseOwl COBOL's determination:** (i) the rule holds for ANY record, so a key is measured at its furthest reach —
  its offset with every preceding variable-length member at its maximum size (§13.18.43.4 GR8 b)) plus its length —
  against the file's minimum record size (§13.18.43.4 GR9 when no integer-2 is written, which D-FRA (iv) makes every
  dynamic item at zero length); a key that can reach past it is rejected (COBOL0874 for SORT/MERGE, COBOL0863
  for an indexed key — both rules enforced on every variable-length file, a fixed-position key included); (ii) a
  legal such key — trailing fixed material keeps it within the minimum — is located in each record by D-FRA's own
  split: its position is its offset in the record's fixed run plus what each preceding member takes from that
  record, the same take step the decomposition uses, so a key compares, and an indexed file indexes, exactly the
  bytes a READ / RETURN of that record puts in the key: by the record's own extent table (D-FRA (v)) when it was
  written with one — so a key with variable-length members on BOTH sides is exact too (kb/Work PB1053) — and by
  the take step otherwise, exact whenever no variable-length member follows the key. A key taken from the RECORD
  AREA (a WRITE / REWRITE, a random READ, a START, a DELETE) is located by the area's own table the same way.
  **Rejected readings:** refusing the key by name (the previous posture — it rejected legal source); slicing it at
  its fixed-run offset (the previous indexed behaviour — a READ … KEY returned a different record); a length-
  prefixed image (rejected under D-FRA). Implemented once — `RecordLayout.KeyWindowOf`, `CobolContiguousLayout`
  (FILES_DESIGN D27); witnessed by `conformance:cases/12.4.5.6-ALTERNATE-RECORD-KEY/pb1025_key_after_dynamic_member`,
  `conformance:cases/12.4.5.12-RECORD-KEY/pb1025-indexed-key-beyond-minimum` and
  `conformance:cases/14.9.24-MERGE/pb1025-sort-key-after-dynamic-beyond-minimum`.
- **D-ODO2 — a READ of a record made variable by OCCURS DEPENDING ON is judged AFTER the record lands, against the
  file's maximum record size** (2026-09-30; kb/Work PB1513, row `GR-9.1.13.6-4`). §9.1.13.6 item 4 b): *"A READ
  statement is unsuccessfully executed because the records are variable in length because of an OCCURS DEPENDING ON
  clause in the record in the associated record description entry and the associated DEPENDING ON item contains a
  value that makes the number of bytes in the record exceed the value specified or implied by the file description
  entry"* — '34'. **WiseOwl COBOL's determination:** (i) the record's size at a count n is §13.18.43.4 GR13 c)'s —
  the fixed portion plus the table at n occurrences — and "the value specified or implied by the file description
  entry" is the file's maximum record size (the largest description, or integer-1 / integer-3 of an explicit RECORD
  clause), so the test is a compile-time LIMIT on the count, the largest n whose record still fits, compared with the
  DEPENDING ON item (`SequentialIoEmitter.OdoRecordExceedsMaximum`); (ii) the DEPENDING ON item is read AFTER the
  record has landed in the record area, the only moment a count carried in the record has a value — so after a '34'
  the area holds the over-long record, which §14.9.30.4 GR18 makes undefined anyway; the READ is unsuccessful, so it
  runs no NOT AT END and no INTO, stores no length and no relative key, invalidates the file position (GR18), and —
  the connector being open — begins the permanent error of §9.1.13.1 (A.1 item 105); (iii) it applies to the READ
  statement of every organization (sequential, and the relative / indexed arm) and to the implicit READ of a SORT or
  MERGE USING transfer, which lands the record in the file's area for the purpose so the statement terminates under
  the same fatal-status table as any other as-if READ; (iv) **the rule is asked of a file with exactly ONE record
  description.** It speaks of *"the record in the associated record description entry"*; a file description with
  several record descriptions (implicit redefinitions of one area, §13.18.33.4 GR3) has no one description a READ is
  associated with, and judging a description's count over bytes that belong to another record type would reject
  every legal record of the other types. **Rejected readings:** a bound at the table's own maximum occurrence count
  (ignores an integer-1 / integer-3 larger than the largest description — `RECORD CONTAINS 20` over a 12-byte record
  admits counts up to 18); judging every description of a multi-record file; an emit-time snapshot of the count taken
  before the record lands (a count carried in the record would be the previous record's).
  Witnessed by `conformance:cases/9.1.13.6-Permanent-error-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb1513_read_odo_record_exceeds_maximum`
  (the implied value), `…/pb1880_odo_read_explicit_record_clause` (the SPECIFIED value: RECORD CONTAINS 14 and 16, and
  RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 2 TO 16, so counts past the table's own maximum are judged by the clause's bytes),
  `…/pb1880_odo_read_bit_table` (the unit is the byte and a last item that ends inside a byte takes the whole byte,
  §13.18.43.4 GR4: a count of 24 over a 1 TO 20 bit table is still five bytes and succeeds, 25 is six and is '34'),
  `…/pb1880_odo_read_depending_item_outside_record` (a WORKING-STORAGE DEPENDING ON item) and
  `…/pb1880_odo_read_34_exception_paths` (the '34' with a USE procedure only, with FILE STATUS and a USE procedure, on
  the relative arm, and uncovered, where the run unit terminates, Annex A.1 item 103).
- **D-RANGE-KNOWN — when "the runtime collating sequence is known" for a level-88 THROUGH range** (2026-10-07;
  kb/Work PB552, rows `SR-13.18.63.3-26`, `SR-13.18.63.3-27`). §13.18.63.3 SR26 b) and SR27 b) apply to an
  alphanumeric or national range only "when … the runtime collating sequence is known", and SR26's NOTE 5 leaves
  knowing it to the implementor ("this is not a requirement of an implementor"); the one sentence the standard does
  fix is "The runtime collating sequence is unknown when the collating sequence is defined by a locale or the
  collating sequence is otherwise determined at runtime" (cite.py OK). **Determination: every sequence this
  processor fixes at compile time is known** — the `IN alphabet-name-1` phrase's alphabet, else the PROGRAM COLLATING
  SEQUENCE, else the native order — and only a LOCALE sequence is not. So an inverted or equal character range in a
  known sequence is refused at compile time (COBOL2961), as a numeric one always is (SR26 a)), and §14.7.8's
  run-time EC-RANGE-INVALID arm is reached by a level-88 range only through a LOCALE alphabet (and by an EVALUATE
  WHEN range, which no syntax rule orders). Survey under the owner's precedence (CLAUDE.md rule 1; the 2026-08-30
  protocol): GnuCOBOL 3.2 has nothing — it accepts `88 C VALUE 5 THRU 1` and `VALUE "Z" THRU "A"` silently at
  `-std=default`, `cobol2014` and `ibm-strict` (measured, wave 1031 C), enforcing neither arm; IBM Enterprise COBOL
  6.4 states the rule for every class with no condition ("When the THROUGH phrase is used, literal-1 must be less than
  literal-2", Language Reference, VALUE clause format 2), i.e. treats its fixed sequences as known. SR27 b)'s screen
  (COBOL2048) already read the same predicate (`DataBinder.ConditionValueOrder.Known`); SR26 now shares it.
  Witnesses: `conformance:cases/13.18.63-VALUE/pb552-value-through-not-ascending`, `conformance:cases/13.18.63-VALUE/ec_range_invalid` (the
  LOCALE arm at run time), `conformance:cases/13.18.63-VALUE/pb502_value_range_in_alphabet` (an ascending range in a reversed alphabet).
- **D-ODO1 — how many occurrences of an occurs-depending table an INITIALIZE statement initializes, when the
  VALUE phrase is what qualifies them** (2026-09-20; kb/Work PB577, row `GR-13.18.63.4-6`). Two rules answer and
  they do not agree. §13.18.63.4 GR6 says *"the initialization of the associated data item behaves as if the
  value of the data item referenced by the DEPENDING phrase … is set to the maximum number of occurrences"*, and
  §13.18.63.4 GR4c makes the execution of an INITIALIZE statement one of the two occasions a VALUE clause takes
  effect on — so read alone it would give the MAXIMUM. §14.9.20.4 GR8 says *"For a variable-occurrence data item,
  the number of occurrences initialized is determined by the rules of the OCCURS clause for a receiving data
  item"*, which reaches §13.18.38.4 GR8a — *"only that part of the table area that is specified by the value of
  the data item referenced by data-name-1 **at the start of the operation** will be used"* — so for a DEPENDING
  item OUTSIDE identifier-1 it gives the CURRENT value. (Inside identifier-1 the two agree: GR8b's *"If the group
  is a receiving operand, the maximum length of the group will be used"* is the maximum.) **WiseOwl COBOL follows
  §14.9.20.4 GR8**: the INITIALIZE statement's own clause is the more specific rule for how many occurrences that
  statement initializes, and §13.18.63.4 GR6's maximum-pretence governs the occasions on which no statement
  supplies a count — the initial-state seeding and the ALLOCATE seeding, where the DEPENDING item has no
  meaningful value yet and which is what GR6 exists to answer. **Rejected reading:** GR6's maximum-pretence
  overriding GR8 at the INITIALIZE occasion, which would make §14.9.20.4 GR8's second sentence inert for every
  `TO VALUE` statement. The difference is observable only by raising the DEPENDING item afterwards and reading an
  occurrence the statement was told was outside the table. Witnessed at all three poles:
  `conformance:cases/13.18.63-VALUE/pb577_odo_value_initial_state` (the initial-state occasion — the maximum, GR6 as written),
  `conformance:cases/13.18.63-VALUE/pb577_odo_value_initialize` lines L1/L2 (the INITIALIZE occasion with the DEPENDING item
  outside — the current value) and L3 (inside — the maximum, plus GR6's last-sentence ordering).
- **D-READ-KEY-ACCESS — a READ with a KEY phrase on a file whose access mode is SEQUENTIAL is refused** (kb/Work
  PB3569; COBOL0864, every edition). *The question:* does ISO bar a Format 2 READ on an indexed file in sequential
  access mode? *The determination, one reading of SR8 and GR19 across the compiler:* §14.9.30.3 SR8 ("If neither the
  NEXT phrase nor the PREVIOUS phrase is specified and ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL is specified in the file control entry
  for file-name-1, the NEXT phrase is implied") supplies the NEXT phrase of a READ on a SEQUENTIAL-access file, with
  §12.4.5.5.3 GR1 assuming sequential access when the ACCESS MODE clause is absent, and §14.9.30.4 GR19 ("An implicit
  or explicit NEXT phrase or a PREVIOUS phrase results in a sequential read: otherwise, the read is a random read and
  the rules for format 2 apply") makes a READ with an implicit NEXT a sequential read. §14.9.30.2 prints the KEY phrase
  in Format 2 only, so a sequential read has no KEY phrase to bind. That is the reading the READ binder already used
  (`KeyedIoBinder.BindRead` binds `ReadKind.Next` for such a file) and the one that refuses INVALID KEY on a READ of a
  sequential-organization file or on a keyed READ that binds sequential (COBOL1720, `DiagnosticCatalog.IoPhraseForbiddenHere`,
  whose rationale names both READ sites and cites SR8, SR9 and GR19: a READ that binds sequential is a Format-1 read);
  the KEY refusal states the same thing and no other. The standard's own way to read by key on a
  keyed file is §12.4.5.5.3 GR3 (RANDOM) or GR4 (DYNAMIC: "accessed sequentially, randomly, or both"). The
  alternative to a refusal is a sequential read that ignores the key; that is GnuCOBOL's ("KEY ignored with sequential
  READ", a warning), and it reads a different record than the program asked for, so it is not taken (CLAUDE.md rule 1:
  GnuCOBOL settles implementor latitude only, and silently changing which record is read is a wrong answer). It is a
  hard error where the INVALID KEY screen is a strict-error/permissive-warning seam, because a dead INVALID KEY arm
  selects no record and a KEY phrase does. The message names the file's access mode (and, when the clause is absent,
  that sequential access is assumed) and the implied NEXT, and no phrase the statement wrote. A KEY phrase beside
  NEXT, PREVIOUS or ADVANCING ON LOCK is a different refusal (Format 2 prints none of them, §14.9.30.2), named with
  exactly the phrases written; AT END and NOT AT END beside KEY are refused by the parser (COBOL2269, kb/Work PB3830).
  `READ f INVALID KEY` with no KEY phrase on a sequential-access keyed file draws COBOL1720 through the same seam as the
  sequential-organization READ (an error under strict, a warning under `--permissive` with the INVALID arm dead). Witnesses
  `conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/pb3569-read-key-sequential-access-default`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/pb3569-read-key-sequential-access-written`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/pb3569-read-next-key`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/pb3569-read-invalid-key-sequential-access`; the legal twin on RANDOM and DYNAMIC files is
  `conformance:cases/12.4.5.6-ALTERNATE-RECORD-KEY/l1_read_key_of_reference`; the messages are pinned by
  `conformance-test:ReadKeyFormatTests`.
- **I-O status '0x' case equivalence** (E.2 item 17): the low-order status digit for a non-'00' successful
  completion is implementor-dependent; WiseOwl COBOL reports the specific '0x' value (e.g. '04', '05', '07') rather
  than collapsing to '00'.
- **I-O status '04' (record-length mismatch, §14.9.30 GR14 / §9.1.13.2 item 3)**: **emitted** on a
  record-sequential READ whose physical record is outside the file's min/max record size (fixed leg: shorter than
  the record width; varying leg: outside [VaryMin, VaryMax]) — the READ is successful, the record is delivered,
  status '04' (VCR 21; golden `2002/io_status_04`). Line-sequential is excluded (§14.9.30 GR15 pads short records
  with trailing spaces — its '06' write path remains unimplemented). The value is version-invariant — the E.2
  item 15 2023 delta only clarifies *when* it is set.
- **I-O status '07' restricted to OPEN/CLOSE (§9.1.13.2 item 6; E.2 item 16)**: **VERIFIED AT 2023, A DETERMINATION
  BELOW IT, THE SAME BEHAVIOUR AT EVERY EDITION** (kb/Work PB1515). *2023:* the '07' setters are exactly the three
  phrases item 6 names on the two statements it names, all reaching `FileStatusCode.PhraseOnNonReelMedium` on a
  non-reel/unit medium: `CLOSE … REEL/UNIT [FOR REMOVAL]` and `CLOSE … WITH NO REWIND` through
  `FileRegistry.CloseByFormat`, and `OPEN … WITH NO REWIND` through `FileRegistry.NoRewindPhraseEffect`. No
  READ/WRITE/START/REWRITE/DELETE path sets it, on any organization, and an unsuccessful OPEN or CLOSE keeps the
  status that made it unsuccessful ('35', '41', '42', '61': `NoRewindPhraseEffect` and `CloseByFormat` test the first
  digit). `IoStatus07SetterDriftTests` holds both facts structurally (the constant is read in those two methods only,
  and the value is spelled nowhere else). *Before 2023:* E.2 item 16 says the setting "is now restricted to the
  execution of the OPEN and CLOSE statements", so an earlier edition let other input-output statements set it, but
  the repository holds no text of the 1985, 2002 or 2014 editions and E.2 names neither the statements nor the
  condition they reported, so there is no prior answer a gate could serve (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE's admission test,
  row 22). Under rule 1's order — the standard has nothing for those editions, then GnuCOBOL — the behaviour stays
  edition-invariant: GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 (probed in WSL, 2026-10-17) answers '07' from `CLOSE … REEL/UNIT/NO REWIND` alone
  (it does not implement `OPEN … WITH NO REWIND`, which ISO §14.9.27.4 GR11 requires to answer '07') and never from a
  READ, WRITE, REWRITE, START or DELETE; IBM Enterprise COBOL and Micro Focus were not consulted, GnuCOBOL having
  answered. If a text of an earlier edition that states a distinct rule is ever obtained, the gate belongs in
  `DialectBehaviors` and row 22 becomes a `behavior:` row. Witnesses: `conformance:cases/9.1.13.2-Successful-completion/pb1515_io_status_07_open_close_only`
  and `…/pb1515_io_status_07_keyed_organizations` (the same output at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023: each statement's
  status on its success and failure paths, with a FILE STATUS clause and a USE declarative),
  `…/pb1515_io_status_07_sharing_conflict` (a refused `OPEN … WITH NO REWIND` answers '61', never '07'; 2002+, the
  file sharing mechanism's edition) and `…/pb1515_io_warning_07_raises_ec` (2023: the '07' is the exception condition
  EC-I-O-WARNING, §9.1.13.1, raised by OPEN and CLOSE alone, with and without a FILE STATUS clause), plus the negative
  `pb1515-io-warning-07-below-2023`. *(This bullet claimed until 2026-09-05 that CLOSE REEL/UNIT was the ONLY
  setter — untrue since kb/Work PB141 added the CLOSE NO REWIND arm, and doubly so since PB317 added the OPEN
  one — and, until PB1515, that "already met at all editions" had been derived from the 2023 text alone; a
  determination that undercounts its own sites, or claims editions it never read, cannot be checked against the
  code.)*
- **I-O status '07' vs '05' on one OPEN (§14.9.27.4 GR11 against §9.1.13.2 item 4 a; kb/Work PB317)**: an
  `OPEN INPUT` of an OPTIONAL file that is not present, written `WITH NO REWIND`, reports **'07'**. Both values
  describe a successful open and the standard does not rank them, so this is a determination: GR11 is an explicit
  ASSIGNMENT in the statement's own general rules (*"the I-O status associated with file-name-1 is set to
  '07'"*), whereas item 4 a) is a DESCRIPTION in the status-value clause, and §14.9.27.4 assigns '05' only in
  GR17 — whose EXTEND and I-O modes §14.9.27.3 SR6 bars from carrying the phrase at all. The information '05'
  would have carried is not lost: the first READ of an absent optional file is the at-end '10' (§9.1.13.4 item
  1 c). Golden `2023/pb317_open_no_rewind` (`OPT-ABSENT=07`).
- **I-O status '37' insufficient authority on OPEN/DELETE FILE (§9.1.13.6 item 6b; E.2 item 18)**: emitted at all
  editions. The spec permits it ("may") and marks detection processor-dependent; E.2 item 18 is a clarification
  that it is allowed, not a 2023 introduction — so it is NOT gated/suppressed below 2023. **Detection is a
  three-state presence probe, not an exception map alone.** `HostFile.Probe` (`Runtime/IO/FileSupport.cs`) asks
  the host with `File.GetAttributes`, whose failures distinguish a missing file
  (`FileNotFoundException`/`DirectoryNotFoundException` → §9.1.13.6 item 5's '35') from a refused one
  (`UnauthorizedAccessException` → GR3's '37'); `File.Exists` collapses both to `false` and is banned throughout
  `Runtime/IO` for that reason (`HostFileProbeDriftTests`). `FileConnector.Open` answers GR3 from the probe
  for INPUT/I-O/EXTEND — OUTPUT is excluded because GR18 makes it a creation that never consults presence, so a
  writable-but-unlistable directory still accepts a new file — and `FileRegistry.DeleteFile` takes the same probe
  for §14.9.10.4 GR14/GR16. Any refusal the probe cannot see still maps from `UnauthorizedAccessException` in
  `Open`'s `catch`. Witnesses: `unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests` (a real DACL/mode denial — the corpus runner has
  no way to express the precondition) and `conformance:cases/9.1.13.6-Permanent-error-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb323_open_presence_arms` for the probe's other two
  answers (kb/Work PB323).
- **I-O status '37' write capability on OPEN (§14.9.27.4 GR16; §9.1.13.6 item 6 a)**: emitted at all editions,
  for every organization. Presence and *capability* are two questions and a file answers them differently: a
  read-only file is `FilePresence.Present` and fully observable, yet GR16 requires '37' when *"the file does not
  support"* the statements the I-O mode permits, and §9.1.13.6 item 6 a) 1. requires the same for EXTEND and
  OUTPUT. **The question is asked once, in the OPEN contract, above the organizations**: `FileConnector.Open`
  calls `HostFile.PermitsWrite` (`Runtime/IO/FileSupport.cs`) for I-O, EXTEND and OUTPUT on a file that is
  Present, before `OpenCore`. The probe is a real write open (`FileMode.Open`, `FileAccess.Write`,
  `FileShare.ReadWrite`, nothing written), because a read-only attribute, a mode bit and a deny-write ACE are
  three mechanisms with one consequence, and GR25 (*"the file is not affected"*) leaves content and timestamp
  untouched either way. INPUT is deliberately excluded — a read-only file supports every statement Table 20
  permits in the input mode, and item 6 a) 3.'s read-capability question is answered by the organization's own
  eager read. Witnesses: `unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests` (the nine cells — three organizations × I-O/EXTEND/
  OUTPUT — plus the INPUT and writable-file over-fire guards) and `unit:HostFileProbeDriftTests`, which keeps
  the call singular (kb/Work PB328: the sequential arm answered '37' by accident because its I-O and EXTEND
  streams are write opens, while the keyed arms only read their store and answered '00', then '00' for READ and
  REWRITE, and surfaced the loss as a '30' at CLOSE on a byte-identical file).
- **I-O status '39' (fixed-file-attribute conflict, §9.1.13.6 item 7; E.3.3 item 35) — TWO DIFFERENT CASES, and
  only one of them is a gap.** '39' is not produced on either statement, but the reasons are not the same and
  collapsing them (as this bullet did until 2026-08-31) hid a conforming determination inside a deferral.
  - **DELETE FILE — CONFORMING, by definition.** §14.9.10.4 GR19 requires the implementor to *define* which
    fixed-file attributes DELETE FILE validates; WiseOwl COBOL's definition is **the empty set** (§7, Annex A.1
    item 50 — see there for the full determination). GR19 nowhere requires the set to be non-empty, so with
    nothing validated GR18 has nothing to compare and its '39' is **unreachable by definition, not by
    omission**. Golden `2023/delete_file_attribute_set_empty`: a DELETE FILE issued through a connector that
    contradicts the physical file in two §9.1.6 attributes (organization and record size) still deletes, '00'.
  - **OPEN — CONFORMING, and its set is NOT empty.** §14.9.27.4 GR10 delegates the validated set the same
    way GR19 does, but the two obligations are not the same question and WiseOwl COBOL answers them differently:
    a DELETE FILE destroys the file, so nothing downstream depends on the connector's description having been
    right, while everything after an OPEN reads the file THROUGH that description. WiseOwl COBOL therefore
    records each physical file's §9.1.6 fixed file attributes when the OPEN statement CREATES it (GR18's
    OUTPUT, GR17's absent OPTIONAL I-O/EXTEND) and compares them on every later OPEN — see §7, Annex A.1
    item 129 for the set and `FixedFileAttributes` for the mechanism. The set is **per organization**, as
    GR10's third sentence allows: the ORGANIZATION for every file; additionally the record type, the record
    sizes and the key descriptors for RELATIVE and INDEXED, whose store's structure IS those attributes.
    A SEQUENTIAL file validates nothing beyond the organization — §9.1.7.2 puts its record lengths in the
    data and in the reading program, and §9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer a re-read disagreement with the
    successful '04', '06' and '09', so a '39' there would reject the legal write-then-read-back idiom. A file
    whose attributes are not recorded — an external tool's, or one written before the catalog existed —
    supplies nothing to compare and opens normally. Goldens `85/open_fixed_attribute_conflict` and
    `2023/open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix`.
- **Transfer of control includes sections (§14.6; E.2 item 26)**: a section is a first-class transfer target at all
  editions — `ProcedureTableBuilder` gives each section a contiguous `[StartPc,EndPc]` pc range, so GO TO / PERFORM
  of a section resolve (§14.9.17 / §14.9.28). The 2023 clarification is met without a gate.
- **WRITE with no END-OF-PAGE phrase (§14.9.51; E.2 item 30)**: when the END-OF-PAGE condition occurs and no
  END-OF-PAGE phrase is present, control falls through to the next statement (the natural code path — no branch is
  emitted for an absent phrase). Version-invariant; met without a gate (no `>>FLAG-14` option exists for it).
- **>>EVALUATE combined-condition end omission (§7.3.13 GR6/GR10; E.2 item 8)**: the preprocessor omits the
  END-EVALUATE text precisely when no WHEN matched AND no WHEN OTHER is present — the corrected 2023 AND-truth rule;
  the compile-time directive is version-invariant.
- **Figurative constant on an unspecified-length item (§8.3.3.6.4 GR3b/c; E.2 item 11)**: a bare figurative VALUE
  fills a single character (GR3b); an `ALL "literal"` fills the literal's own length (GR3c). Both are defined for
  dynamic-length items at all editions, superseding the pre-2023 undefined case.
- **Case mappings (UPPER-CASE / LOWER-CASE, §15.97.4 r4 / §15.57.4)**: absent a locale, the case correspondence is
  **implementor-defined** (§15.97.4 r4). WiseOwl COBOL uses the .NET invariant Unicode case tables. Because the mapping
  is delegated to the implementor, the enumerated 2023 annex changes (E.2 item 14 deletions of DOTLESS I
  `(0131,0069)` and GREEK FINAL SIGMA `(03C2,03C3)`; E.3.3 item 6 additions) are not separately tuned — the invariant
  mapping is the determination (a corner case; the general Latin/basic repertoire matches exactly). Since kb/Work
  PB64 T5 this is the ELSE-arm it is meant to be: a `LOCALE locale-name-1` phrase (r2) or a CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION
  locale in effect for the operand's class (r3) maps through THAT locale's LC_CTYPE instead — see §4 item 5.
- **CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED UTC-offset positions 17–21 — the TRUE offset is reported, out of the rule's
  stated range when the host is (§15.21.3 r1 / §15.99.3 r1; documented per §4.2.6 / §4.2.7).** One determination
  covers both functions because one formatter serves both (`CobolDate.Format21`; the compile-time bake and the
  run-time read are separate seams onto it). §15.21.3 r1 fixes positions 18–19 at "00 through 13" when position 17
  is `+` and "00 through 12" when it is `–`, and §15.99.3 r1 carries that table character for character. **Real
  offsets exceed both bounds.** UTC+14:00 is a shipping zone on both platforms WiseOwl COBOL targets — IANA
  `Pacific/Kiritimati`, Windows `Line Islands Standard Time` ("(UTC+14:00) Kiritimati Island", verified against the
  host zone table, not assumed) — and the `WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK` pin reaches **−14:00** as well, because it parses a
  `DateTimeOffset` directly and that type's offset range is ±14:00. So the departure is **symmetric: both signs**.
  For such a clock **the rule's table offers no in-range value at all**, and every available behaviour departs from
  something: emitting `14` leaves the stated range; clamping to `13` misreports the offset, which §15.21.1 defines
  as "the … local time differential factor provided by the system on which the function is evaluated"; and writing
  `0`/`00`/`00` asserts position 17's "the system … does not have the facility to provide the local time
  differential factor", which is false — the system has it and it is 14 hours.
  **The determination: report the true offset.** It is the only one of the three that does not state something
  untrue, and it keeps the value usable as an offset. The departure is confined to positions 18–19 and to
  |offset| > 13 (`+`) / > 12 (`–`); positions 1–16, 17 and 20–21 conform outright at every offset, which is what
  makes this one bounded determination rather than an open-ended divergence — `CurrentDateOffsetDeterminationTests`
  asserts exactly that scope (the full §15.21.3 r1 position table re-derived from the rule text, with the violation
  set required to be **precisely** `{18-19}` across the whole fixture range and empty for every in-range offset).
  End to end through the clock seam: `CurrentDateOffsetPinTests` (a COBOL program under `WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK` at
  ±14:00, +13:00, +05:45, +00:00 and −09:30). Inventory rows `RV-15.21.3-1` and `RV-15.99.3-1` carry this one
  determination at DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT.
- **STOP RUN / GOBACK termination status (§14.9.42.4 GR5 / §14.9.18.4 GR10 — Annex A required items 192/193)**:
  the status "passed to the operating system" and the ERROR/NORMAL termination indication both map to the single
  observable available on .NET — the process exit code (`Environment.ExitCode`). The constraint on the STATUS
  operand (item 192): the integer value of `literal-1` / `identifier-1` (truncated toward zero) becomes the exit
  code; a **non-numeric** operand — a display/national data item per §14.9.42.3 SR2, **or a non-numeric
  literal-1**, which SR3's conditional ("if literal-1 *is* numeric …") and SR4 (which bars only a zero-length
  literal) together admit — is interpreted numerically: its digit characters decode as an unsigned integer, a
  non-digit position contributing no digit (`CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric`, the same §14.6.13.2 deterministic decode
  an alphanumeric operand takes in any numeric context). ⚠ **A consequence worth stating: an all-non-digit
  literal maps to 0**, so `STOP RUN WITH ERROR STATUS "ABEND"` exits 0 — indistinguishable at the process level
  from NORMAL termination. That follows from this determination rather than from the ERROR/NORMAL indication,
  which GR5's value phrase overrides. ✅ Surveyed 2026-08-31 before being kept (kb/Work PB169): GnuCOBOL 3.2
  binds the phrase to ONE integer and hands the operand's value to `cob_stop_run` → `exit(status)`, with 1/0
  substituted only when the operand is ABSENT — no arm anywhere gives a non-numeric operand a distinguished
  exit — and no vendor documentation reachable in the survey does either. This determination is the consensus
  shape, not an outlier.
  **"NON-NUMERIC LITERAL-1" MEANS EVERY NON-NUMERIC LITERAL FORM**, which the code now implements rather than
  only the quoted one: a FIGURATIVE constant (§8.3.3.6.3 SR1 admits one "whenever 'literal' appears in a format",
  and §8.3.3.6.4 GR3 b + its NOTE 2 — which names the STOP statement — give it a length of ONE character, so
  `STATUS SPACE` exits 0 and `STATUS ZERO` exits 0), `ALL literal-1` (GR3 c gives it literal-1's length, so
  `STATUS ALL "07"` exits 7), `ALL symbolic-character-1`, a BOOLEAN literal and a boolean CONCATENATION (their
  '0'/'1' characters decode, so `STATUS B"01"` exits 1 and `STATUS B"1" & B"0"` exits 10), a NATIONAL literal and
  a HEXADECIMAL alphanumeric literal. ⚠ **NULL is NOT one of them**: §8.3.3.6.2 lists no NULL format, §8.4.3.10.1
  makes it a predefined address / object reference and §8.4.3.10.3 SR1 admits it only in INITIALIZE/SET, a
  prototype argument, or a pointer-or-object-reference relation condition — so `STATUS NULL` is rejected
  (COBOL1704), not mapped. The error-termination mechanism
  (A.1 item 192; item 193, the implementor-defined error-termination mechanism, is recorded in §7 as not provided): when a status phrase specifies `ERROR` with **no** STATUS value, the exit code is 1; `NORMAL` (or
  no phrase) is 0. When a STATUS value is present it wins regardless of ERROR/NORMAL. A main-program GOBACK
  (§14.9.18.4 GR3) uses the same mapping; a status phrase on a GOBACK executed in a **called** program is inert
  (GR2). Programs with no status phrase leave the exit code at 0 (the abnormal-fatal case still forces item 44's
  nonzero exit). The status is the run unit's own `RunUnit.ExitStatus`, written by the STOP statement wherever in the
  run unit it executes (so it crosses assembly boundaries — a separately-compiled module's STOP RUN … WITH STATUS
  reaches the process exit code) and delivered to `Environment.ExitCode` ONCE, when the run unit has ended, by the
  boundary that IS the process (`ProgramTable.RunModule`, the generated `Main`'s statement). A run unit embedded in a host
  (the generated host entry `Cobol.<assembly>.<NAME>.Call`, inside or outside `RunUnit.Run`) never writes the host's exit
  code (kb/Work PB3163; A.1 item 167): a run unit that STOP RUN or a fatal condition ended reaches the host as the
  `RunUnitEndedException` carrying the status, and the host reads a run unit's status still in progress from
  `RunUnit.ExitStatus`. Two host limits apply on top of the value mapping: the exit code is an `Int32`, so a
  status outside [−2,147,483,648, 2,147,483,647] is **clamped** to the nearer end (`CobolNum.Position32`, the one
  saturating narrowing — see "Integer operands and host carriers" below), never wrapped: before kb/Work PB1178
  `STOP RUN WITH ERROR STATUS 4294967296` wrapped to exit 0, a NORMAL termination reported for an ERROR phrase.
  A POSIX host then reports only the low 8 bits of the exit code — outside COBOL's control — so a STATUS ≥ 256
  is reduced modulo 256 there (2,147,483,647 exits 255; a value that clamps to −2,147,483,648, or any multiple of
  256, exits 0). The value-wins-over-ERROR/NORMAL precedence above is the rule-1 precedence applied: §14.9.42.4
  GR5 leaves "any constraints on the value" to the implementor and GnuCOBOL passes the value as given.
- **COLUMN alignment (§13.18.14.4 GR6 c)/d); kb/Work PB1220)**: RIGHT and CENTER derive an item's leftmost column
  from integer-1 and the printable-size ("integer-1 - printable-size + 1", "integer-1 - ((printable-size - 1) / 2)"),
  and the standard states no outcome when that column is before column 1 (GR5's EC-REPORT-PAGE-WIDTH covers only the
  right edge). Determination: the compiler REFUSES the clause (COBOL2712) instead of clamping, because a clamped
  placement would make GR9's horizontal counter — the item's rightmost column — disagree with where the item was
  printed. Both operands are compile-time integers over a compile-time width, so the verdict is a compile-time one.
  The standard being silent, the choice is the implementor's (CLAUDE.md rule 1 precedence); no GnuCOBOL behavior
  was measured for it.
- **RD CODE reference modification (§13.18.12.3 SR2, §13.18.12.4 GR2; kb/Work PB1292)**: identifier-1 is an identifier,
  so it may be subscripted or reference-modified (a reference-modified identifier references the slice, an alphanumeric
  item, §8.4.3.3.4 GR6 c)). GR2 charges the code's characters to the logical record size, which `RECORD CONTAINS` and the
  report's line width need as a NUMBER at compile time, and SR2 excludes the dynamic-length shapes for exactly that
  reason. Determination: a reference-modified CODE identifier whose leftmost-position and length are not both integer
  literals (the length may be omitted) is refused under SR2's "dynamic-length elementary item" (COBOL2713), the same
  literal-position rule the CONTROL operand's reference modification takes (§13.18.16.3 SR4); the standard states no
  outcome for a code whose length varies. The choice is the implementor's (CLAUDE.md rule 1); no GnuCOBOL behavior was
  measured for it.
- **VARYING counters of one clause (§13.18.64.3 SR3, §13.18.64.4 GR3 b); kb/Work PB1306)**: SR3 lets arithmetic-expression-2
  name data-name-1 of the same VARYING clause, and the clause may define several counters (§13.18.64.2). The standard
  does not order the additions of GR3 b) among the counters of one entry. Determination: for each occurrence after the
  first the counters of the entry are advanced IN CLAUSE ORDER, each adding its BY evaluated against the counters as
  the previous addition left them (so a BY naming an earlier counter of the clause sees that counter's new value, and
  one naming a later counter or itself sees the old one). Only a BY that names a counter of its own entry needs
  this; every other counter is FROM + n × BY. The choice is the implementor's (CLAUDE.md rule 1); no GnuCOBOL behavior
  was measured for it.
- **Integer operands and host carriers (§4.5 / §4.6 — the limits of an implementation; kb/Work PB1033, PB1058)**:
  an integer data item or literal holds up to 31 digits (§13.18.40.3 SR14, §8.3.3.3.2), and every rule that
  consumes one asks about its VALUE. Two carrier rules follow, each written in ONE place:
  **(1) an integer-n the compiler binds into its own model** — a table size, a record or block size, a LINAGE or
  PAGE line count, a report LINE or COLUMN, an ordinal — is limited to **2,147,483,647**; a larger literal is
  `COBOL2427` (§4.5: "Translation may be unsuccessful due to factors other than lack of conformance", whose
  NOTE names "the limits of an implementation"), screened once for every `integerLiteral` by
  `Validation/IntegerOperandPass` and read by the binder only through `IntegerOperandRules.HostValue`. The same
  limit meets an integer the binder reaches by another road — an integer constant-name substituted for integer-n
  (§13.10.4 GR1: OCCURS K where K is 77777777777) and a reference-modification literal of a CONTROL, TYPE CF or
  SUM … RESET ON operand (§13.18.16.3 SR4; the prior control is laid out as the slice, §13.18.16.4 GR3) — through
  the one text reader `IntegerOperandRules.TryHostValue`, which reports "integer literal, saturated" rather than
  "not an integer literal", and the one sentence `BeyondLimitMessage` (kb/Work PB1579). Exempt,
  because their value is carried at full width: PERFORM integer-1 TIMES, WRITE ADVANCING integer-1 LINES, and
  the DYNAMIC LENGTH LIMIT (clamped by A.1 item 62's own determination). **(2) a run-time integer value handed to a host
  `int` or `long`** — a GO TO … DEPENDING selector, a reference-modifier position or length, a PERFORM TIMES
  count, a RETRY amount, a STRING / UNSTRING pointer, a RELATIVE KEY, a boolean shift
  count, an OCCURS DEPENDING current count, an ADVANCING or LINAGE line count, a termination status — is
  **saturated**, never wrapped (`CobolNum.Position` / `Position32`, emitted only through `RuntimeApi.HostInt64` /
  `HostInt32`; a CONTINUE AFTER period is saturated inside `CobolTiming.ContinueAfter`, which reads the interval on its own carrier through `CobolNum.PositionOf`, kb/Work PB1529). A wrap maps an out-of-range value back into range; saturation keeps every rule's out-of-range
  answer, because every range those rules test lies strictly inside the carrier: `GO TO … DEPENDING ON` a
  selector of 4,294,967,297 falls through (§14.9.17.4 GR2), a reference-modifier start of 4,294,967,297 raises
  EC-BOUND-REF-MOD (§8.4.3.3.4 GR5 c), a STRING pointer of 2^64 + 3 overflows and stays unchanged (§14.9.43.4 GR6,
  GR8). A subscript's or OCCURS DEPENDING count's saturated `long` still positions every table, and the diagnostic
  names the value the program holds, not the clamp (`CobolTable.Occ` returns an `Occurrence`, kb/Work PB2695); a reference-modifier
  leftmost position or length is the same carrier (`CobolString.RefModPosition`, kb/Work PB2938), and an integer literal past `long`
  keeps its value in the diagnostic too. A repeat count saturates at 2^63 − 1, which no terminating run can tell from a larger one; the
  observable carrier limits are an **ADVANCING line count** above 2,147,483,647 (≈ 4 GiB of line terminators),
  which advances 2,147,483,647 lines, and the termination status (item 192 above). An UNSTRING TALLYING count is
  summed exactly, never narrowed. `semgrep` rules `wiseowl-cobol-integer-value-cast-narrowed` and
  `wiseowl-cobol-integer-n-parsed-outside-host-value` hold both rules to their one place.
- **Return to a NON-COBOL activating runtime element (§14.9.18.4 GR1 a) — "If the activating runtime element is a
  non-COBOL element, execution continues in the activating element in an implementor-defined fashion"; the
  §14.9.14.4 GR3 EXIT PROGRAM twin reads through to the same rule)**: **an ordinary managed return, and no
  exception condition is raised in the activator.** WiseOwl COBOL defines no §7.3.9 call-convention-name (only `>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL`), so a
  non-COBOL element cannot be the TARGET of a CALL (see the A.1 item 19 determination in §7); the only non-COBOL
  ACTIVATOR it can have is a .NET host that activates a program through the program's generated host entry,
  `Cobol.<assembly>.<NAME>.Call(...)` (the program classes themselves are internal) — A.1 items 65 and 141 in §7. For
  that host the activation is a plain method call: the activation catches the `ProgramReturn` the GOBACK throws and
  returns, the PROCEDURE DIVISION header RETURNING item's value becomes `Call`'s return value exactly as it is delivered
  to a COBOL activator (GR2), and the host resumes at its own call site. A RAISING phrase stages its condition and nothing consumes it: a non-COBOL element enables
  checking for nothing, so GR1 b)'s test — "if checking for that exception condition is enabled in the activating
  runtime element" — is false, and the host runs no pickup, so the staged condition is never raised, fatal or
  not (a COBOL pickup takes a staging only in the activation the staging names — kb/Work PB892). No COBOL exception condition, and no .NET exception, crosses into a non-COBOL
  activator. (kb/Work PB408.)
- **A condition PROPAGATED from a called program versus the CALL's NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase (§14.9.4.4 GR3 i) —
  "If an exception condition is propagated from the called program, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1,
  Exception conditions; otherwise, control is transferred to the end of the CALL statement or, if the NOT ON
  EXCEPTION phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2")**: **the two are alternatives — once a propagated
  condition is RAISED in the activator (§14.9.18.4 GR1 b): checking for it enabled THERE), imperative-statement-2
  is never executed**, whatever §14.6.13.1 then does: a fatal condition terminates or runs its declarative; a
  nonfatal one whose declarative completes normally continues after the CALL (§14.6.13.1.4 3) says so outright:
  "the imperative-statement in that phrase is not executed"); a RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT leaves the CALL; and a
  nonfatal one with NO applicable declarative, where §14.6.13.1.4 4) hands back to "the rules for that statement",
  takes GR3 i)'s own first branch again rather than its "otherwise" — the reading that keeps the rule's two outcomes
  exclusive (the rejected reading, which would run imperative-statement-2 for exactly that last case, makes the
  word "otherwise" do nothing). A condition staged by the callee but NOT enabled in the activator is never raised
  (§14.6.13.1.1), so it propagates nothing and NOT ON EXCEPTION runs. An exception OBJECT takes the same
  disposition. The pickup precedes both phrase bodies, so an activation written inside a phrase body can never
  consume the CALL's own staging. (kb/Work PB606; golden `2002/pb606_call_not_on_propagated`.)
- **The SORT/MERGE implicit transfers after an unsuccessful as-if OPEN, READ, WRITE or CLOSE (§14.9.40.4 GR12,
  GR15, GR17; §14.9.24.4 GR7, GR12; §9.1.13.1; §14.6.13.1.3 2))**: the USE procedure runs first, then the verb's
  rule disposes of the status — **terminate the statement, bypass the file, or continue** — from ONE table
  (`SortEmitter.RuleFor`). Four points the standard leaves to a reading: **(a) a FATAL status the verb's rules do
  not name terminates the statement.** §9.1.13.1: if the implementor continues the run unit (WiseOwl COBOL does, with
  checking off, when the file has a FILE STATUS clause or a USE procedure applies — A.1 item 103 in §7; with neither,
  the as-if statement ends the run unit exactly as the explicit one does, before this table is read, kb/Work PB2700), "control is transferred to the end of the statement that produced the fatal exception condition
  unless the rules for that statement define other behavior" — and the statement is the SORT/MERGE, since the
  as-if statement is not one the program wrote (§14.9.33.4 GR2 a) 1.). With EC-I-O checking ON the same holds:
  §14.6.13.1.3 2) ("If the executed statement is a MERGE or SORT statement, then the rules for those statements
  apply") precedes the run-unit termination of 5)/7). So a SORT whose USING file is missing ('35') or whose GIVING
  write fails '48'/'71' ends there, where it used to run every remaining implicit function against a connector that
  was not open. **(b) SORT GR12 b)'s "If a fatal exception condition exists for file-name-1"** reads as the USING
  file (file-name-2): the sort file has no I-O status, and the same paragraph's "at end condition exists for
  file-name-1" has the same slip; the reading agrees with (a) either way. **(c) "an exception condition exists"
  means an UNSUCCESSFUL status** (first character not '0'): a successful '0x' — an OPTIONAL file's '05' — runs no USE
  procedure (§14.9.49.4 GR6) and leaves the connector usable, so it never terminates a transfer. **(d) a terminated
  statement performs NONE of its remaining implicit functions** — "control is transferred to the end of the
  statement" — so a GIVING file whose write terminated the statement is still OPEN afterwards and the program may
  CLOSE it; a file whose OPEN failed was never opened. (Rejected: closing every file the transfer opened at the
  landing — the standard asks for that only for MERGE GR6's sequence error, "all files associated with the MERGE
  statement are closed", which shows it says so when it means it.) The specific rules that override (a) are MERGE
  GR7 a) (a nonfatal USING OPEN terminates unless a USE procedure completes normally), GR12 a) (a fatal GIVING OPEN
  followed by a USE that completes normally BYPASSES that file — the other GIVING files are still written), GR12 b)
  (any WRITE exception continues only after a USE that completes normally) and both verbs' write-boundary paragraph
  (the file is closed and the statement goes on). (kb/Work PB993; golden `2002/pb993_sort_merge_transfer_termination`.)
- **A USE procedure invoked while a SORT is active that does not complete normally — from the SORT's INPUT or OUTPUT
  PROCEDURE, or from a program CALLed or a method INVOKEd in their range (§14.6.13.1.2 1); §14.9.33.4 GR2 a), GR3;
  §14.9.40.4 GR10, GR13, GR17), spec silent on where control lands**: GR17 — "If a USE procedure invoked while a format
  1 SORT statement is active does not complete normally, the SORT statement is terminated" — names every such USE
  procedure, whichever runtime element declares it: GR10/GR13 put in the procedure's range "all statements that are
  executed as the result of a transfer of control in the range" (so a CALLed program's or INVOKEd method's statements)
  and "all statements in declarative procedures that are executed as a result of the execution of statements in the
  range" (so their USE procedures, and a containing program's GLOBAL one, §14.9.49.4 GR4 b)). The rejected narrower
  reading — only the USE procedures of the program instance executing the SORT — has no text behind it. §14.9.33.4
  GR2 a) 1. alone would put a RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT after the raising statement, inside the procedure (or inside the
  CALLed program). **Pinned choice: the SORT ends where it is terminated, and its whole range with it** — nothing more
  of the procedure, of an element the range activated, of the sequence phase or of the output procedure runs, and a
  RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT (or a not-normal fall-off) lands after the SORT statement, as it does for the implicit
  transfers: GR2 a) yields "unless general rules associated with the applicable statement specify otherwise", and the
  next statement of a terminated SORT's range is no longer part of an executing statement (the rejected reading —
  continue the procedure with the SORT ended — runs RELEASE/RETURN statements that GR1 of each then refuses, and the
  procedure's inserted return would hand control back into a statement that has ended). A RESUME AT procedure-name of
  the SORT's OWN program instance is a GO TO (GR3) taken after the SORT has ended, never from inside the procedure with
  the SORT still active; one of ANOTHER element names a procedure of an activation the termination has ended, so it is
  not taken and control lands after the SORT. An activation the range entered ends as the range does: what it stored
  through a BY REFERENCE formal is the activator's (§14.2.3 GR8, "the same storage area as the argument"), and an
  INITIAL program's activation ends with its implicit CANCEL (§14.9.18.4 GR2). An EXIT PROGRAM or GOBACK in another
  element's USE procedure is that element's return (§14.9.14.4, §14.9.18.4): it returns to its activator, and the SORT is
  terminated there once the return is complete, so a CALL's or an INVOKE's RETURNING item (§14.9.4.4 GR4, §14.9.23.4
  GR8) holds the result, and a condition the same USE procedure staged with GOBACK … RAISING has been raised in the
  activator first (§14.9.18.4 GR1 b): "after the result, if any, of the activated element is returned"), so the activator's
  own USE procedure for it runs inside the range before the SORT ends (kb/Work PB3246). A USE procedure invoked by another while the SORT is active is itself one GR17 reaches, so its
  own RESUME terminates the SORT there. **MERGE has no such rule** (§14.9.24.4): a statement of a MERGE output
  procedure is its own applicable statement, and its USE procedure's RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT continues the procedure
  and the MERGE. The ISO text controls; no GnuCOBOL latitude is taken. (kb/Work PB1177; goldens
  `2002/pb1177_sort_procedure_use_not_normal`, `2002/pb1177_sort_called_use_not_normal`,
  `2002/pb1177_invoke_sort_use_not_normal`, `2002/pb1177_sort_called_goback_ec_free`,
  `2002/pb1177_invoke_self_new_raising`, `2002/pb3246_sort_terminated_after_raising_pickup`.)
- **D-SMF — the short-record fill of a SORT/MERGE transfer (§14.9.40.4 GR7, GR16; §14.9.24.4 GR2, GR13)**: three
  readings. **(a) Arm b) cannot arise.** "multiple record description entries … and the descriptions include a SELECT
  WHEN clause" needs the SELECT WHEN clause, which Annex A.4.8 declines by name (COBOL1705), so a file with several
  record descriptions takes c), the alphanumeric space. **(b) SORT GR16 a) / b) print "file-name-2"** where the rule's
  own lead-in (GR16: "If the file referenced by file-name-3 contains only fixed-length records") and its MERGE twin
  (GR13 a), file-name-4) name the GIVING file: a slip of the standard, read against the GIVING file. **(c) A LINE
  SEQUENTIAL or variable-length GIVING file has no fixed record length to fill to**: §14.9.51.4 GR21 strips the
  trailing spaces of a line sequential record on write, and a variable-length file keeps each record at its own size,
  so the connector's own fit-and-trim owns their shape and the rule's fill is applied to fixed-length files only. The
  test of arm a) is one function of the file's own record descriptions (`FileModel.ShortRecordFillNational`), never
  the connector's per-record-area national flag, which is §14.9.30.4 GR15's READ fill. (kb/Work PB1140; golden
  `2002/pb1140_sort_merge_short_record_fill`.)
- **D-SMA — the sort-merge STATEMENT exception conditions (§14.9.40.4 GR9, GR10, GR12 b), GR13; §14.9.24.4 GR6,
  GR7, GR8, GR12; §13.18.43.4 GR14 b), GR19 b); §14.6.13.1.1; §14.6.13.1.3 2))**: three readings. **(a) Which
  condition a statement raises when it detects two.** A RETURN inside an executing input procedure fails both
  §14.9.40.4 GR10 (EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE) and §14.9.34.4 GR1 (EC-FLOW-RETURN, "any other time"); a RELEASE inside an
  output procedure fails GR13 / MERGE GR8 and §14.9.32.4 GR1. §14.6.13.1.1: "if more than one exception is detected
  during the execution of a statement, the one that is set to exist is undefined". WiseOwl COBOL raises
  **EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE** when it is enabled — the rule written for exactly that range — and the EC-FLOW-* name only
  when it is not; a RELEASE's record-range test (EC-SORT-MERGE-RELEASE) comes last. **The survey behind (a)**
  (CLAUDE.md rule 1: ISO, then GnuCOBOL, then IBM / Micro Focus; kb/Work PB1571; measured on `cobc` 3.2.0 and read
  from the pinned 3.2 source, `libcob/fileio.c` and `libcob/exception.def`): **GnuCOBOL** lists all seven EC-SORT-MERGE
  names but raises exactly one, EC-SORT-MERGE-FILE-OPEN (a USING/GIVING file that fails its implicit OPEN with a '4x'
  status); it raises no -ACTIVE, -RELEASE, -RETURN or -SEQUENCE (its source marks the MERGE sequence test a FIXME) and
  no EC-FLOW-RELEASE or EC-FLOW-RETURN, with `-debug` as without. So it has no order to follow. What it does with the
  misplaced statements is a by-product of its sort store with no check behind it: a RETURN in an input procedure takes
  the record the SORT still owes its output procedure (the output procedure then meets end of file at once, a lost
  record), a RELEASE in an output procedure is kept when it comes before the first RETURN and is a run-time error '30'
  after a RETURN, and a nested SORT of another file runs. **IBM Enterprise COBOL** documents the restrictions (an input
  or output procedure must not contain SORT or MERGE; a called program cannot issue SORT, MERGE, RELEASE or RETURN)
  without a condition or a result. **Micro Focus** documents one fatal run-time error, COBRT099 "Illegal operation in
  SORT/MERGE module", for a RELEASE outside the input procedure and a RETURN outside the output procedure alike. Of
  the three, the one that names the condition (Micro Focus) names a single failure for both rules, and none of the
  three orders two conditions (the ISO exception-checking model of §14.6.13 is WiseOwl COBOL's own to realise), so the
  determination stands: -ACTIVE first. The same survey leaves (c) as it is: the answer with checking off is
  "undefined" in every rule, and GnuCOBOL's depends on the state of its store and loses a record or adds one, where
  this compiler's answer (a RETURN in an input procedure answers at end, a RELEASE in an output procedure is not
  kept) is deterministic. Golden
  `conformance:wiseowl/cases/14.9.40-SORT/pb1571_sort_merge_active_vs_flow` pins (a) at source level, with the EC-FLOW names
  raised where -ACTIVE is not enabled and EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN (GR3) unpre-empted. The dispositions with no USE procedure (abnormal termination for a written RETURN/RELEASE, the inner SORT ended and the run unit continuing for a nested SORT) are pinned by `SortMergeActiveUndeclaredDispositionTests`.
  **(b) The disposition when the SORT or MERGE itself raises a condition** (EC-SORT-MERGE-FILE-OPEN,
  -SEQUENCE, -RELEASE of the implicit USING release, -ACTIVE at a nested SORT/MERGE — and any other fatal condition
  its own execution raises, such as an EC-LOCALE-* from a locale-collated key): §14.6.13.1.3 2) hands it to the verb, and
  each verb rule says the statement terminates (MERGE GR6/GR7/GR12, SORT GR12 b)) or its results are undefined (SORT
  GR9, GR10, GR13). The applicable declarative runs, the statement is terminated, and the run unit continues — the
  reading the implicit-transfer determination above applies to I-O statuses. A terminated statement performs none of
  its remaining implicit functions (that determination's (d)), so the USING file of a MERGE terminated by -SEQUENCE is
  still open afterwards (the program's own CLOSE succeeds, golden leg G). The implicit USING release's size test (GR12
  b)) cannot fire from source: §14.9.40.3 SR5 refuses, at compile time, a USING file that describes a record larger
  than the sort file's (kb/Work PB995), so that test is pinned at the unit level
  (`SortMergeStatementEcTests.ImplicitRelease_TestsTheReadSize`). The same names raised by a RELEASE or RETURN statement keep the general fatal
  disposition (§14.6.13.1.3 5)/7)), since the executed statement is not a SORT or MERGE. **(c) With checking off**
  nothing is raised (§14.6.13.1.1) and the statement proceeds: an open USING/GIVING file meets its implicit OPEN's
  '41', an out-of-range record is released as shaped (a DEPENDING ON size slices or space-extends the record area as
  the lenient reference modification `(1:size)` would), an out-of-order MERGE input merges in stream order, and a
  nested SORT/MERGE runs. Every one of those results is "undefined" in its rule. (kb/Work PB1036; golden
  `2002/pb1036_sort_merge_statement_ec`.)
- **D-SKE — a SORT/MERGE key whose length varies, at edition 1985 (§14.9.40.3 SR6 d), §14.9.24.3 SR4 d); kb/Work PB2512)**: the 2023 text refuses a key that is "a variable-length group, an occurs-depending-on data item, a dynamic-length elementary item or an item subordinate to a dynamic-capacity table" (MERGE's copy prints a comma before "or an item subordinate"; the refusal quotes each statement's own copy verbatim). The repository holds no ISO/IEC 1989:1985 text, so whether the 1985 SORT/MERGE rules carry an equivalent is not read from the standard. **Determination: the arm is not edition-gated; a key that is an occurs-depending group is refused at `--std 85` too** (the occurs-depending group is the only varying-length key an 85 program can write: DYNAMIC LENGTH is 2014 and a dynamic-capacity table is 2023). Basis, under CLAUDE.md rule 1's precedence for a latitude the controlling text does not settle (the ISO text read here is silent for 1985, then GnuCOBOL, then IBM or Micro Focus): GnuCOBOL 3.2 was surveyed first (`cobc -fsyntax-only -free` on `pb1173-sort-file-key-odo-group` and `pb1173-merge-key-odo-group`, at `-std=cobol85`, the default, `ibm` and `mf`) and compiles the occurs-depending group key with exit 0 at every one of them, even at its default dialect where the 2023 text forbids the key, so it has no such check and gives no guidance. The next rung, Micro Focus's SORT statement page, prints the prohibition in 1985-shaped words ("The data items identified by KEY data-names must not be variable length items", beside the OCCURS rule that predates it), and the key's "same byte positions" rule (SR6 e) / SR4 e)) has no meaning for a window whose length varies. **Rejected reading:** gating the arm at 2002 and accepting an 85 key that is an occurs-depending group (it would sort on whatever length the first record held, and no text read here permits it). **Open to the standard itself:** a holder of the 1985 text that shows its SORT/MERGE rules carry no such prohibition turns the occurs-depending arm of `SortKeyAdmission` into an edition gate and moves `85` out of the `refuse-at` of `pb1173-sort-file-key-odo-group` and `pb1173-merge-key-odo-group`. (Goldens `14.9.24-MERGE/pb1173-sort-file-key-odo-group`, `pb1173-merge-key-odo-group`.)
- **D-SWK — the sort-merge file's storage: a memory limit and temporary run files (§13.4.6.1; §14.9.40.4 GR3, GR4,
  GR9; §14.9.24.4 GR4, GR6)**: the standard says what a sort-merge file DOES, never where its records are kept — the SD
  entry "furnishes information concerning the physical structure pertaining to a sort or merge file" and nothing
  more — so the storage is the implementor's, and WiseOwl COBOL follows GnuCOBOL 3.2 (CLAUDE.md rule 1: bounded sort
  memory, sorted runs on temporary files, merged) (kb/Work PB3339). **(a) The memory limit** is `WISEOWL_COBOL_SORT_MEMORY`:
  a byte count with an optional `K`, `M` or `G` suffix (powers of 1024, case-insensitive); unset or not a size, it is
  **128 MiB** (GnuCOBOL's `COB_SORT_MEMORY` default); below **64 KiB** it is 64 KiB. It is read once per run unit. A
  SORT or MERGE keeps at most that many bytes of records in memory (the estimate counts each record's UTF-16 image,
  its frame and extent table, and its decoded keys), or one record when a single record is larger; what exceeds it is
  written as sorted RUNS and merged, at most F at a time (F = the limit ÷ 256 KiB, between 2 and 16), and the return
  phase reads F runs through 64 KiB buffers. A SORT or MERGE whose records fit is done wholly in memory and writes
  nothing. **(b) The temporary files** are created in `WISEOWL_COBOL_SORT_TMPDIR`, or in the host's temporary directory
  when it is unset (`TMPDIR` on Linux and macOS, `TMP` / `TEMP` on Windows). Each is deleted when its handle closes
  (Windows) or unlinked as soon as it is created (Linux, macOS), so none survives the statement, the run unit or a
  killed process, and the statement's end closes every one, whether it ends normally or by a failure part-way
  through writing or merging a run (one owner, `SortWork._files`, holds each file from its creation to its close).
  **(c) The ordering does not depend on the limit**: a run
  is a stable sort, and every merge takes the lowest key and, on equal keys, the record of the earliest run, so
  equal keys are returned in input-file and release order (§14.9.40.4 GR3 a), b) DUPLICATES IN ORDER; without the
  phrase the order GR4 leaves undefined is the same one) and a MERGE keeps §14.9.24.4 GR4 a), b). With
  EC-SORT-MERGE-SEQUENCE unchecked an out-of-order MERGE input is merged in stream order when it fits in memory, and in
  groups of F streams when it does not — both within GR6's "undefined". **(d) A failure of a temporary file** — the
  directory missing or not writable, the volume full — stops the run unit with a message naming the directory and the
  host's reason (an implementor-defined fatal stop that raises no exception condition, like `CobolImplementorFatalException`'s
  other uses); no record is dropped silently. **(e) Two undefined results** this storage settles: a RETURN executed
  before the sequence phase, which only unchecked EC-FLOW-RETURN admits (§14.9.34.4 GR1), finds the file at end; a
  RELEASE executed after it, which only unchecked EC-FLOW-RELEASE admits (§14.9.32.4 GR1), releases to no phase and
  the record is not returned. Witnesses: `conformance-test:SortWorkSpillConformanceTests` (a SORT and a MERGE many times
  the limit, run as a separate process, the work directory empty afterwards) and `SortWorkBoundTests` (the measured
  bound, every key class, the extent table and the character repertoire through a run file).
- **D-ADDRNF — a fatal address-resolution condition with checking OFF continues with NULL (§14.6.13.1.3 8);
  §8.4.3.13.4 4); §8.4.3.12.4 4))**: `SET … TO ADDRESS OF PROGRAM` (and `SET … TO ENTRY`) that cannot locate the
  program sets EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND and gives the address-identifier the predefined address NULL (§8.4.3.13.4 4));
  `ADDRESS OF FUNCTION` likewise sets EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND with NULL (§8.4.3.12.4 4)), and its EC-FUNCTION-PTR-INVALID
  twin is handled by the same site. All three are FATAL in Table 13. With checking ENABLED the condition goes through
  the one selection (`EcEmitter.EmitSelection`): the declarative runs, and a run that is not resumed terminates
  abnormally (§14.6.13.1.3 5) / 7); kb/Work PB1549). With checking NOT enabled, §14.6.13.1.3 8) makes it the
  implementor's choice: "the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and
  how any receiving operands are affected". **WiseOwl COBOL continues with the next statement, and the receiving
  pointer holds NULL** — the value GR4 of each clause already assigns, so a program can test the pointer against
  NULL exactly as it would after a handled condition. Rejected: terminating the run unit — GR4 already defines the
  receiving value, so continuing leaves a defined, testable result, and it is the behaviour unchanged since the SET
  surfaces landed.
  Code sites: `PtrEmitter.EmitSetEntry` and `PtrEmitter.EmitSetFunctionAddress` (the `_ = nf` lines); pinned by
  `conformance-test:FatalRaiseSelectionTests` (the checking-off case).
- **Compile-time arithmetic mode (§7.3.6.2 SR2 / §7.3.6.3 GR2 — Annex E.2 item 6; the required §4.2.16 implementor
  documentation)**: this determination is A.1 item 29 in §7 — one evaluator (`CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator`) for
  constant entries and directive operands alike. At COBOL-2023 the mode is .NET `System.Decimal`, an implementor-unique
  mode (not a §8.8.1 standard mode), with intermediate results rounded to nearest, a tie to the even digit (division
  does not truncate) and a diagnosed error on overflow; at COBOL-2002 and 2014 the mode is standard arithmetic
  (34-digit standard-decimal intermediates, NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO). In every edition the final result is truncated
  toward zero to an integer.
- **Recognized-and-ignored compiler directives (§7.3 — the implementor-disposition set)**: the following standard
  directives are RECOGNIZED (consumed during text manipulation so the program compiles unchanged) and carry no
  effect, each because WiseOwl COBOL provides a single behaviour with no alternative to select: **>>CALL-CONVENTION**
  (§7.3.9) — CALL uses the single .NET managed calling convention, so only `>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL` is accepted and
  any other call-convention-name is an error, COBOL1911 (A.1 item 68 in §7; kb/Work PB1383). GnuCOBOL 3.1.2 and 3.2.0 additionally accept EXTERN, STDCALL and STATIC (measured on both, kb/Work PB1945); owner decision 2026-10-03: keep COBOL only, and revisit only if a .NET mapping is added, which may not be required at all; **>>LEAP-SECOND** (§7.3.17) — the REPORTED side only: the .NET clock never reports a 60th second (A.1 item
  111 in §7); the directive's ARGUMENT side (a 60 in a seconds subfield, a time form to 86,400.99 under ON) is honoured —
  `LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor`, kb/Work PB65; **>>LISTING** / **>>PAGE** (§7.3.18 / §7.3.19) — no source listing
  is produced, so listing on/off and page ejects are inert. The **>>DISPLAY** directive (§7.3.12) is NOT in this set:
  §7.3.12.4 GR2 leaves the no-listing result to the implementor, and GnuCOBOL — the precedent CLAUDE.md rule 1 names for
  implementor latitude — writes the operands to its standard output at compile time, so WiseOwl COBOL parses and evaluates
  the operands and writes them at compile time (kb/Work PB807, PB1538; A.1 items 53–55 in §7 state the determination). The **>>FLAG-02 / >>FLAG-14**
  flagging directives (§7.3.14 / §7.3.15) are NOT in this set: they emit the warnings they request (COBOL1620 /
  COBOL1621 — A.1 items 79 and 80 in §7). **Every one of these is edition-GATED**, which is the half that was missing until
  kb/Work PB725: the roster is the `directiveWords` column of `tests/version-matrix/constructs.json`, inverted by
  `CompilerDirectiveCatalog` and checked once, where `ConditionalCompilationProcessor` recognizes a `>>` word
  (`>>SOURCE FORMAT` one stage earlier, in `ReferenceFormatProcessor`, which consumes its line first). Recognizing
  a directive the targeted edition does not have is not a leniency, it is an under-rejection — the `>>` facility
  itself is a COBOL-2002 introduction (VCR Table 7 row 7.21) and `>>FLAG-85` / `>>FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC` were
  REMOVED in 2023 (Annex E.2 item 21), so all three edges are enforced: COBOL0900 below the introducing
  edition, COBOL0903 at an obsoleting one, COBOL0902 at a removing one.

WiseOwl COBOL rejects a type-name argument-1 to CONVERT with a targeted COBOL1514 naming this note (kb/Work PB124 wave 4); every other Table-21 `TypeN` cell (LENGTH, BYTE-LENGTH) has §15.50.4/§15.14.4 semantics and is implemented.
  end of the PERFORM statement includes the statements in a FINALLY phrase", while GR20's fatal branch routes an

  The two cannot both hold. **Pinned choice: FINALLY runs on the NORMAL (and EXIT-PERFORM) fall-through path ONLY, NOT
