  nothing about 2002. So SEND, RECEIVE and END-RECEIVE are reserved at 2002, like the rest of the communication
  facility's vocabulary (CD, DISABLE, ENABLE, PURGE, …), which GnuCOBOL records as obsolete there and removed at 2014;
  an earlier generator cleared their 2002 flag on the wider reading and left one facility half reserved.
  A word's reservation and its construct's availability are TWO facts: nothing in the standard ties a reserved word to
  a construct that spells it, and GnuCOBOL 3.2 at `-std=cobol2002` refuses both the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause ("does not
  conform to COBOL 2002") and `01 SEGMENT-LIMIT` — so SEGMENT-LIMIT stays reserved at 2002 though the clause left
  there (VCR row 7.8), and COBOL stays reserved through 2014 (refused as a data-name by `cobc -std=cobol2014` too),
  a compiler-directive word only at 2023 (§8.3.2.1 2), §8.12). The same source dates the PADDING CHARACTER clause:
  obsolete 2002 (COBOL0903), removed 2014 (VCR row 7.20). ⚠ DETERMINATION (owner may overturn; a 2002 or 2014
  text overturns any flag in one generator run): pinned by the version-matrix rows `receive-as-user-word`,
  `end-receive-as-user-word`, `segment-limit-removed-2002`, `padding-character-removed-2014`, the negatives
  `user-word-receive` / `user-word-end-receive` (85 2002 2023) and
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb656_padding_character_obsolete_2002`.

- **D-DECLREF — the declaratives reference boundary: an SR4 violation is an error, an SR3 violation is a warning
  (kb/Work PB362).** §14.9.49.3 SR3 ("Within a declarative procedure, there shall be no reference to any
  nondeclarative procedures except in a RESUME statement") and SR4 ("Procedure-names within a declarative section
  may be referenced in a different declarative section or in a nondeclarative procedure only with a PERFORM
  statement") are syntax rules. For a syntax rule the standard requires only §4.2.2's "warning mechanism", so the
  standard settles WHETHER a reference violates the boundary, but not the severity. The severity is therefore
  implementor latitude, and the owner's precedence (ISO, then GnuCOBOL, then IBM or Micro Focus) decides it. An
  **SR4** violation is an **ERROR, COBOL2376**. A GO TO, an ALTER, or a SORT/MERGE INPUT or OUTPUT PROCEDURE
  phrase that enters a USE procedure from outside its section has no activating USE for §14.9.49.4 GR7's return,
  and GnuCOBOL refuses a reference into DECLARATIVES from outside them. An **SR3** violation is a **WARNING,
  COBOL2375**, as it is in GnuCOBOL. A PERFORM or GO TO of a nondeclarative procedure from a USE procedure runs
  as written, is common in production source, and IBM Enterprise COBOL and Micro Focus accept it without comment.
  ⚠ The GnuCOBOL postures are recalled, not measured: the implementer host has no GnuCOBOL install, and the
  differential run is where they are confirmed. Both rules are asked of SECTION identity in the one
  procedure-name funnel (`ProcedureTableBuilder.ResolveProcedureOperand` →
  `StatementValidation.CheckDeclarativesBoundary`), so every statement that takes a procedure-name inherits them.
  Only PERFORM and RESUME claim an exemption. Pinned by `unit:DeclarativesStructuralRulesTests`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.49-USE/pb362_declaratives_reference_boundary` and `conformance:cases/14.9.49-USE/pb362-goto-into-declarative`.

- **D-RELCLASS — a relation outside §8.8.4.2.1's "Comparisons are defined for the following:" list is refused
  (kb/Work PB1468).** The list is closed, and two of its limits are class/usage/form facts of the source, so §4.2.2
  ("This warning mechanism shall indicate violations of such rules") reaches them; the severity is ours. **§8.8.4.2.5**
  ("The numeric integer operand shall be an integer literal or an integer numeric data item of usage display or
  national"): a non-integer, COMPUTATIONAL, packed-decimal or floating-point item, a non-integer literal, an arithmetic
  expression or a numeric, integer or index intrinsic function-identifier against an operand of class alphanumeric,
  alphabetic or national is an **ERROR, COBOL2532**, and `--permissive` keeps it as a warning evaluated as the
  character comparison of the value's text — the DA6 disposition every §8.8.1.1 / §15.3 class screen follows. **An
  INTEGER function-identifier is no longer admitted as the integer operand (owner 2026-10-25, kb/Work PB3691; the first
  wave of this determination admitted it as the Table-16 Integer row of the A.1 item 92 determination, which moves such
  a function to an alphanumeric receiver in its literal text form): see D-FNUSE's relation-condition paragraph.**
  **§8.8.4.2.13** ("Relation tests
  may be made only between" two index-names; an index-name and a numeric data item or numeric literal; an index data
  item and an index-name or another index data item) is an **unconditional ERROR, COBOL2533** — the pairs outside
  it have no comparison to keep under `--permissive` (an index-name against an alphanumeric operand aborted the run
  unit). The figurative ZERO opposite an index-name is row 2's numeric literal (§8.3.3.6.4 GR4, "the numeric value
  '0'"); an arithmetic expression opposite an index-name is not "a numeric data item or numeric literal" and is
  refused. **A numeric or integer FUNCTION-IDENTIFIER is row 2's numeric data item, folded or not (kb/Work PB1662):**
  §8.4.3.2.1 — "A function-identifier references the unique data item that results from the evaluation of a function"
  — and §15.2 items 4 and 5 (class and category numeric) make it one, so `IF I1 = FUNCTION LENGTH(X)` (a value the
  binder folds), `IF I1 = FUNCTION INTEGER(3.7)` and `IF FUNCTION SQRT(9) = I1` are all defined; the first wave of this
  determination refused the unfolded function and admitted the folded one, so one rule drew two answers by what the
  optimizer could compute (the fold now keeps its origin, `BoundNumericLiteral.FunctionValue`, and BOTH are the item the
  function references). A COUNTER REGISTER is a numeric data item likewise: LINAGE-COUNTER "references a temporary unsigned integer data item
  of class and category numeric" (§8.4.3.14.4 GR1), and PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER "reference temporary unsigned
  integer data items of class and category numeric" (§8.4.3.15.4 GR1). Implemented in `RelationComparability` at the one relation checkpoint; pinned by
  `conformance:RelationComparabilityTests`, `conformance:wiseowl/cases/8.8.4.2-Simple-relation-conditions/pb1468_relation_defined_pairs`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1662_index_name_against_function`,
  `conformance:cases/8.8.4.2-Simple-relation-conditions/pb1468-relation-numeric-not-integer` and `conformance:cases/8.8.4.2-Simple-relation-conditions/pb1468-relation-index-pair`.

- **D-RELLITERAL — a relation condition of two literals is a WARNING (kb/Work PB1470).** §8.8.4.2.1 closes its
  general rules with "A relation condition shall contain at least one reference to an operand that is not a literal"
  (`cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.1` stamps the unnumbered sentence "13)", PB222). It is neither a general format nor a
  syntax rule, so §4.2.2 settles only that the warning mechanism indicates it ("This warning mechanism shall indicate
  violations of such rules"); the severity is implementor latitude, and the owner's precedence (ISO, then GnuCOBOL,
  then IBM or Micro Focus) decides it. GnuCOBOL 3.2, measured under WSL, compiles `IF 1 = 1`, `IF "A" = "A"` and
  `PERFORM UNTIL 1 = 1` and warns under `-Wall` (`-Wconstant-numlit-expression`, `-Wconstant-expression`). So each such
  relation is **WARNING COBOL3146** at every edition and strictness, and is evaluated as written. A figurative
  constant is a literal (§8.3.3.6 is a clause of §8.3.3 Literals), a symbolic-character is "a user-defined figurative
  constant" (§8.3.2.2.29), and a constant-name's effect "is as if literal-1 … were written where constant-name-1 is
  written" (§13.10.4 GR1), so `IF "A" = SPACE`, `IF ZERO = ZERO`, `IF SB = "B"` and `IF KT = "A"` draw it too; a data
  item, an arithmetic expression (`IF 1 + 1 = 2`) and a function-identifier (`FUNCTION LENGTH(X)`, folded at bind
  time or not, §8.4.3.2.1) do not. It is asked where a relation condition is WRITTEN: IF, PERFORM UNTIL, SEARCH WHEN, a
  boolean relation, an abbreviated relation's inserted subject (`IF 1 = N OR 2` holds `1 = 2`, §8.8.4.12) and an
  EVALUATE partial-expression (§14.9.13.3 SR8: "treated as though it were specified as condition-2"). An EVALUATE
  subject/object pair or range is governed by §14.9.13.3 SR10's Table 15, which refuses a literal object against a
  literal subject and permits a range-expression against one, so it is not asked again. Implemented in
  `ConditionBinder.WrittenRelational` → `StatementValidation.CheckRelationHasNonLiteralOperand`; pinned by
  `conformance:RelationLiteralOperandTests` and `conformance:cases/8.8.4.2-Simple-relation-conditions/pb1470_relation_of_two_literals_runs`.

- **D-RELINDEXEXPR — an index-name inside a relation's arithmetic expression is refused (kb/Work PB2018).**
  **An index-name is not an operand of an arithmetic expression:** §13.18.38.3 SR7 admits it "as an operand in a
  relation condition" and §8.8.4.2.13 says "Relation tests may be made only between" an index-name and "a numeric
  data item or numeric literal", so a relation operand that is itself an arithmetic expression (`IF N < (K + 2)`,
  `IF K + 1 = 4`, `EVALUATE N WHEN K + 1`) holds the index-name as an operand of the EXPRESSION, where §8.8.1.1 names
  only numeric data items, numeric literals and ZERO; it is COBOL1637 (a warning under `--permissive`, the
  occurrence number computes) exactly as `COMPUTE N = K + 2`, and an index data item there is COBOL0844. kb/Work
  R29's golden had read "inside an expression" as legal; that reading was wider than r7 and §8.8.4.2.13 and is
  withdrawn. Pinned by `conformance:cases/8.4.2.3-Subscripts/index_name_r7_windows` and the `pb2018-*` refusals of `conformance-suite/`.

- **D-ARGEXPR — a keyword-less `N + 1` in a CALL, INVOKE or inline-invocation argument list is ONE argument
  (kb/Work PB1135 / PB130, decision R59).** A USING list is juxtaposition, so `USING N + 1` has two grammatical
  readings: the ONE arithmetic-expression-1 argument, or the two arguments `N` and a unary `+ 1`. The format answers
  it: CALL Format 2 (§14.9.4.2) and INVOKE (§14.9.23.2) print `arithmetic-expression-1` and `boolean-expression-1`
  under an OPTIONAL `[ BY CONTENT ]`, and CALL SR20 forbids omitting BY CONTENT only "when identifier-4 is an
  identifier that is permitted as a receiving operand" (`cite.py --check 14.9.4.3 "BY CONTENT shall not be omitted
  when identifier-4 is an identifier that is permitted as a receiving operand"` → OK 20); SR17 makes every identifier
  in it a sending operand. The token-level tie is broken by the text too: a sign "shall appear as the leftmost
  character of the literal" (§8.3.3.3.2 SR2, OK) and an arithmetic operator is "preceded by a space and followed by
  a space" (§8.7.1, OK), so a `+` or `-` after an operand is the BINARY operator. **Determination (the lexer skips
  whitespace, so the parse does not consult spacing; §8.7.1's spacing is then asked of the parsed operator, COBOL2993,
  kb/Work PB2017 — `USING N -1` is the expression `N - 1` and is refused for its missing space):** an argument is the
  LONGEST arithmetic expression that starts at it — `USING N + 1`, `USING N - 1`, `USING 5 + 1`, `USING BY CONTENT N + 1` and
  `O :: "M" (N + 1)` are each one argument, evaluated before the call and passed BY CONTENT (§14.9.4.4 GR9 a) 2,
  §14.9.23.4 GR6 a) 2); an argument that is a SOLE identifier or literal stays an identifier or literal
  (§14.9.4.4 GR8). A second argument that is a signed literal is written first or after a BY phrase — `USING +1 N`,
  `USING N BY CONTENT +1` (`N (+ 1)` is N subscripted). This replaces PB130's earlier "the list reading wins".
  Implemented in the grammar (no bare `dataReference` arm in `callArgument` / `callByContent` / `invokeArgument`, and
  `{!numericLiteralIsLeftOperand()}?` on the literal arms), with the binders recovering the sole identifier;
  pinned by `conformance:cases/14.9.4-CALL/pb130_call_format2_bare` and `conformance:cases/14.9.23-INVOKE/pb1135_invoke_keywordless_expression_argument`.

- **D-DEBUG — the COBOL-85 debug facility's debugging lines (indicator `D`) and `WITH DEBUGGING MODE`** (kb/Work
  PB1705, PB1802, PB1088; owner decisions R56 and R61). ISO/IEC 1989:2023 no longer carries the facility: §6.2.2 lists no
  `D` fixed indicator (`cite.py --check 6.2.2 "The following are fixed indicators:"` → OK), so the earlier-edition
  behavior is X3.23-1985's, taken as owner decisions and not from the 2023 text. **Determination:** a debugging line is
  SOURCE — compiled as if the `D` were absent — when the program's SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph says `WITH DEBUGGING MODE`,
  and a COMMENT line otherwise. The clause is a SOURCE-COMPUTER clause, so it applies to the source unit that specifies
  it and to every source unit contained in it (§12.3.5.4 GR1, `cite.py --check 12.3.5.4` → OK 1), and to nothing else: a
  separate program in the same source does not inherit it. **Edition windows (R61, GnuCOBOL's per-standard dialect
  files, medium confidence on the 2002/2014 edge — the ISO 2002 and 2014 texts are not in the repository):** accepted at
  85; OBSOLETE at 2002 (COBOL0903 on the clause and on the first line); removed from 2014 (COBOL0902, an error
  under strict, a warning under `--permissive`, where the pre-removal behavior above is kept). **Mechanism (R56, the
  pre-parse token rewriter):** the §6.5 logical conversion cannot decide, because the clause is further down the text
  than the line, so it writes the line as `ReferenceFormatProcessor.DebugLineCarrier` plus its program text; COPY
  REPLACING and REPLACE match over that text as if the `D` were absent; the lexer reads the carrier as the hidden
  `DEBUG_LINE` marker and the text as ordinary tokens; and `DebuggingLineRewriter` keeps the line's tokens or moves
  them to the `ABSENT_DEBUG_LINE` channel, per source unit, before any other token pass runs. A continuation line of a
  debugging line is part of it (§6.5 6) joins it to its latest logical line), and the literal state it ends in is
  tracked like any source line's, so a debugging line that opens a continued literal gets that literal's continuation
  (kb/Work PB1914; before, the line's open literal was forgotten and its continuation line was appended as loose text).
  **A debugging line between the parts of a continued literal** (kb/Work PB1914; the 1985 text is not in the repository,
  so the choice follows rule 1's precedence: ISO 2023 has no `D` indicator, then GnuCOBOL): a debugging line is a comment
  line unless the clause says otherwise, and "Comment lines and blank lines may be interspersed among lines containing
  the parts of a literal" (§6.3.5 2), `cite.py --check 6.3.5 "Comment lines and blank lines may be interspersed"` → OK),
  so when the line before it leaves a literal open — an open literal, or a floating literal continuation indicator —
  the debugging line does NOT become the latest logical line: the continuation line after it continues the literal, and
  the debugging line keeps a logical line of its own, after the joined one (GnuCOBOL reads the same program without
  `-fdebugging-line` as the joined literal, and rejects it with `-fdebugging-line`, "continuation character expected").
  Under WITH DEBUGGING MODE the line is source, and a source line between the parts of a literal is outside the
  continuation rule (§6.3.5 2) lets only comment and blank lines stand there); that program is non-conforming and is
  REJECTED (COBOL3473, an error at every edition, kb/Work PB2490), at the debugging line's indicator: the walk
  cannot tell the two modes apart, so it passes the line over as it would a comment and NOTES it to the per-compilation
  reference-format diagnostics, `DebuggingLineRewriter` names the lines it keeps as source, and the front end reports
  the ones that were noted (GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 `-fdebugging-line`: "continuation character expected"; witnesses
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2490-debugging-line-between-literal-parts-source`,
  `unit:LogicalLineBuilderTests.DebuggingLine_PassedOverInALiteral_IsDiagnosedOnlyWhenItIsSource`,
  `unit:DebuggingLineRewriterTests.Rewrite_NamesTheDebuggingLinesThatAreSource_PerUnit`). Any other debugging line is the
  latest logical line, so a continuation line after it continues it ("continuation of debugging lines is permitted"); a
  debugging line of spaces is a blank line (§6.5 2)), never a join target. Witnesses:
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1914_debugging_line_between_literal_parts`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1914_debugging_line_continued_under_clause`,
  `unit:LogicalLineBuilderTests.DebuggingLine_*`. The NIST `S` / `Y` letters are the
  `--nist` dialect, not the `D` indicator: they stay comment lines whatever the clause says. A debugging line that
  stands inside an open PICTURE clause or an open subscript or reference-modification region is decided the same way
  (kb/Work PB1913): the lexer skips its text in those two modes, and when the line's unit declares the mode the frontend
  blanks the line's carrier and lexes the text again, so the line is source under the clause (`MOVE A(1` / `D    + 2` /
  `) TO B` is `A(1 + 2)`; a `D` line holding the PICTURE string supplies it) and a comment without it. `USE FOR
  DEBUGGING` keeps its own row (accepted at 85, rejected from 2002) and its `--std 85` posture is unchanged. Witnesses:
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1913_debugging_lines_in_open_regions`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1913_debugging_lines_in_open_regions_comment`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1705_debugging_lines_compiled`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1705_debugging_lines_per_unit`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1705_debugging_lines_copy_replacing`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1494_debugging_line_85` (no clause: a
  comment), `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1705_debugging_mode_obsolete_2002`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/debugging-mode`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1494-debugging-line-at-2014`, `unit:DebuggingLineRewriterTests`.

- **D-CE1 — where a FREE-form comment-entry ends** (kb/Work PB3245, review finding R1-1; PB1494, PB1758). The
  comment-entry paragraphs (AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, DATE-COMPILED, SECURITY, REMARKS) are COBOL-85's,
  removed by COBOL-2002, the edition that introduced free form, so no edition of the standard says where a free-form
  comment-entry ends: it is accepted only at `--std 85 --source-format free` (WiseOwl's free form at 85) and under
  `--permissive`. **Determination (CLAUDE.md rule 1: the standard is silent, so GnuCOBOL decides):** GnuCOBOL 3.2's
  `-free` reading. Inside an IDENTIFICATION DIVISION, a line whose FIRST word is one of those paragraph words opens the
  paragraph, its period optional, and the entry is the rest of that line; the next line is program text again. GnuCOBOL
  3.2 measured: `AUTHOR. Pat O'Brien.`, `AUTHOR Pat O'Brien.` and `SECURITY. J. Smith.` are accepted, the paragraph
  word part-way along a line is not a header, and a second line of entry text is refused. **Mechanism:** the §6.5 logical
  conversion's free-form classifier (`ReferenceFormatProcessor.FreeFormConverter`) writes the header line as `AUTHOR. .`
  and discards the entry, exactly as the fixed-form classifier does with a COBOL-85 entry that runs to the next Area-A
  word, so no comment-entry character reaches the lexer in either format: an apostrophe in a name is no unclosed literal
  (COBOL5563), and a comma with no space after it is no misplaced separator (COBOL2631). Which division a line stands in
  is the one `DivisionCursor` rule, carried from each SOURCE FORMAT segment to the next in either format. Before this
  determination, free-form entry text ran to the parser's first period token: entries with a period inside or an
  unbalanced quotation mark were refused, and an entry continued on further lines was accepted. Pinned by
  `conformance:wiseowl/cases/6.5-Logical-conversion/pb3245_free_comment_entry_is_commentary`,
  `conformance:wiseowl/cases/6.5-Logical-conversion/pb3245-free-comment-entry-ends-at-line-end`,
  `conformance:cases/6.5-Logical-conversion/pb3245_free_segment_hands_on_its_division` and
  `unit:ReferenceFormatLogicalConversionTests.FreeFormCommentEntry_IsTheRestOfItsHeaderLine_AndIsDiscarded`.

- **D-OOCIRC — the reach of "directly or indirectly references" in §9.3.8.2.3's closing sentence** (kb/Work PB1498;
  owner decision R63). §9.3.8.2.3: "If the description of the returning item of a method in interface-1 directly or
  indirectly references interface-2, the description of the returning item of the corresponding method in interface-2
  shall not directly or indirectly reference interface-1" (cite-checked). The standard defines "indirectly" no further,
  so it carries its ordinary TRANSITIVE meaning. The reference graph: nodes are classes and interfaces, keyed by name;
  a RETURNING item described as an object reference to Y (an object-class-name, an interface-name, or ACTIVE-CLASS —
  the containing class) is an edge to Y, from the class whose methods (instance or factory) or the interface whose
  prototypes (inherited ones included) declare it; a class has edges to the class it INHERITS and to every interface
  in either IMPLEMENTS list; an interface to the interfaces it INHERITS. A universal reference is no edge. The walk is
  breadth-first with a visited set. The sentence is asked only of two DISTINCT interfaces ("If two interfaces are of
  the same interface, they conform to each other"), so a returning item that references its own class or interface is
  legal. It is one of `OoConformance.MethodConformanceMismatches`' rules (`ReturningCircularity`), so every asker
  applies it — IMPLEMENTS (COBOL0841), an override (COBOL0829) and the interface relation GOBACK / EXIT RAISING
  asks. Witnesses: `conformance:cases/9.3.8.2.3-Conformance-between-interfaces/pb1498_self_referencing_returning`,
  `conformance:cases/9.3.8.2.3-Conformance-between-interfaces/pb1498-returning-circularity-direct`, `conformance:cases/9.3.8.2.3-Conformance-between-interfaces/pb1498-returning-circularity-indirect`.

- **D-ALR1 — the length of an ANY LENGTH RETURNING item when the activation has no receiving item** (kb/Work PB1167;
  ISO §13.18.2.3 SR3 b) and §13.18.2.4 GR1 b)). §13.18.2.3 SR3 admits the clause's subject as the RETURNING item of a
  contained program or a method (cite-checked), and §13.18.2.4 GR1 b) fixes its length n as "the length of the
  corresponding argument or returning item of the activating runtime element"; GR1 a) makes it a zero-length item when
  that returning item is zero-length. With a receiver, n is the receiver's length and the standard decides it. The
  standard is silent on the one activation that has NO receiver: a CALL or INVOKE whose RETURNING phrase is absent
  (§14.8.3.1 requires the phrase exactly when the activated element declares a RETURNING item, so only an activation
  the compiler cannot check statically, a dynamic CALL, can reach it). **WiseOwl COBOL gives the item the length its
  PICTURE spells (one position for the one-symbol PICTURE §13.18.2.3 SR1 requires).** Rejected readings: zero length
  (a MOVE into it would silently store nothing, and the value is discarded by GR4 anyway, so the choice cannot change
  the activator's data) and a diagnostic (the activation is legal source). GnuCOBOL has no ANY LENGTH RETURNING item, so
  no vendor behavior applies (rule 1 precedence: ISO, then GnuCOBOL, then IBM / Micro Focus). Written once on each ABI:
  the program ABI seeds the item at activation entry from the receiver's `CobolArg` (`CobolArgAdapt.ReturningSeed`) and
  the method ABI receives n as the trailing `__retLen` parameter that `OoEmitter.OoSignatureOf` appends for exactly the
  methods whose RETURNING item is ANY LENGTH. A universal-receiver INVOKE of such a method sets EC-OO-UNIVERSAL
  (§14.9.23.4 GR7 c)), an inline invocation of it is refused (§8.4.3.4.3 SR4, COBOL2140), and a PROPERTY method may
  not carry it (§13.18.2.3 SR2). Witnesses: `conformance:cases/13.18.2-ANY-LENGTH/pb1167_any_length_returning`,
  `unit:ReturningSeedTests.No_Receiver_Gives_The_Declared_Picture_Length`,
  `unit:ReturningSeedTests.Zero_Length_Receiver_Gives_A_Zero_Length_Item`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1167-inline-invocation-returning-any-length`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1167-any-length-returning-property-method`,
  `conformance:cases/14.8.3.3-Elementary-items/pb1167-returning-fixed-sender-any-length-receiver`.

- **D-INH1 — interface multiple inheritance: what SR5 asks of the inheriting interface, and what "the same interface-name"
  means in SR6** (kb/Work PB1502; ISO §11.6.3 SR5 and SR6, §11.7.3 SR4 b), §9.3.10; all cite-checked). (1) **SR5.** "If a
  given method-name is inherited from more than one interface, the method prototype in each inherited interface shall be
  such that this interface conforms to all inherited interfaces." The inheriting interface has ONE method of that name
  (SR4 b) leaves it no prototype of its own), so the rule holds exactly when ONE inherited prototype conforms to every
  other, by the §9.3.8.2.3 rule set (`OoConformance.MethodConformanceMismatches`): identical prototypes inherited twice,
  and a covariant RETURNING pair (rule 5) through the more specific one. WiseOwl COBOL reads it that way, reports a
  violation on the INHERITING interface (COBOL2762) and records the conforming prototype as the interface's own
  (`OoInterfaceSymbol.ChooseInheritedPrototype`), which the IMPLEMENTS pass, `InterfaceConformsTo` and the emitted C#
  interface (a hiding `new` member, because C# member lookup over two base interfaces declaring one name is ambiguous)
  all read. Rejected reading: pairwise conformance in BOTH directions, which refuses the covariant pair that rule 5 makes
  legal. (2) **SR4 b).** A prototype whose roster key (the method-name; the v1 method resolution signature, kb/Work
  PB1519) matches ANY prototype of the INHERITS closure is refused (COBOL2761): SR2 forbids OVERRIDE in a prototype, so there is no
  legal way to redeclare. (3) **SR6.** The rule is about the WRITTEN interface-name (a case variant is the same
  word, §8.1.3.2 GR3). Two different REPOSITORY names for one externalized interface (§12.3.8.3: `INTERFACE
  ALX AS "EXT-ALI"` and `INTERFACE ALY AS "EXT-ALI"`) are two interface-names, no sentence of the standard forbids them,
  and the inheriting interface has ONE base — the emitted C# base list carries it once. This follows the PB946
  determination for IMPLEMENTS (ISO controls where it states the prohibition; SR6 names the NAME). Witnesses:
  `conformance:cases/11.6-INTERFACE-ID/pb1502_interface_inherits_legal`, `conformance:cases/11.6-INTERFACE-ID/pb1502-interface-inherits-conflicting-prototypes`,
  `conformance:cases/11.7-METHOD-ID/pb1502-interface-prototype-redeclares-inherited`,
  `conformance:cases/11.7-METHOD-ID/pb1502-interface-prototype-contradicts-inherited`,
  `conformance:cases/11.6-INTERFACE-ID/pb1502-interface-inherits-same-name-twice`.
- **D-SR8 — what "with or under a PERFORM statement with the VARYING phrase or either the TEST BEFORE or TEST AFTER
  phrase" reaches (kb/Work PB434, row `SR-14.9.28.3-8`).** §14.9.28.3 SR8: "The UNTIL EXIT phrase shall not be specified
  in a PERFORM statement with or under a PERFORM statement with the VARYING phrase or either the TEST BEFORE or TEST
  AFTER phrase". (1) **A TEST phrase counts only when WRITTEN.** SR1's assumed TEST BEFORE ("If neither the TEST BEFORE
  nor the TEST AFTER phrase is specified, the TEST BEFORE phrase is assumed") governs the until-phrase UNTIL EXIT itself
  is, so counting it would make SR8 forbid every UNTIL EXIT; a TIMES PERFORM and an until-phrase with no TEST written do
  not bar it. (2) **"With" includes the superset spelling** `VARYING … UNTIL EXIT` (and an AFTER level's `UNTIL EXIT`):
  the varying-phrase prints `UNTIL condition-1` only, and SR8's first conjunct is exactly that spelling — refused by name
  (COBOL2954) at every edition rather than as a bare parse error. (3) **"Under" is the PERFORM's range** (§14.9.28.4
  GR1, "The range includes all statements that are executed as the result of a transfer of control in the range of the
  PERFORM statement"), decided statically: an inline PERFORM's imperative-statement-1 at any depth, an out-of-line
  PERFORM's specified set (§14.9.28.4 GR4, both physical orders of a GR6 inverted THRU), closed over every transfer that
  RETURNS — an out-of-line PERFORM, a SORT/MERGE INPUT or OUTPUT PROCEDURE, an exception-checking PERFORM's handler
  (`ProcedureReach`). A GO TO's destination and a declarative are NOT followed: where control goes after a GO TO leaves a
  range, and whether an I/O failure runs a USE procedure, are run-time facts, and following them statically would refuse
  statements no execution reaches under the PERFORM. GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 enforces neither half (measured, wave 1021 C), so no
  vendor behavior informs the reading. Witnesses: `conformance:cases/14.9.28-PERFORM/pb434-until-exit-under-varying`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.28-PERFORM/pb434-varying-until-exit`, `conformance:cases/14.9.28-PERFORM/pb434_until_exit_unbarred`,
  `conformance-test:PerformUntilExitPlacementTests.UntilExit_WithOrUnderAVaryingOrTestPerform_IsRefusedOnce`,
  `conformance-test:PerformUntilExitPlacementTests.UntilExit_InASortInputProcedureUnderAVaryingPerform_IsRefusedOnce`,
  `conformance-test:PerformUntilExitPlacementTests.UntilExit_NotUnderAVaryingOrTestPerform_IsAccepted` (thirteen refused
  shapes, each refused exactly once; four admitted).

- **D-PTHRU — control that runs off the end of the source element inside an out-of-line PERFORM whose return mechanism
  is never reached (kb/Work PB3511, rows `GR-14.6.3-3`, `GR-14.9.28.4-5`).** §14.9.28.4 GR5 b): "If procedure-name-2 is
  specified, the return mechanism is after the last statement of procedure-name-2"; GR6: "There is no necessary
  relationship between procedure-name-1 and procedure-name-2 except that a consecutive sequence of operations is to be
  executed beginning at the procedure named procedure-name-1 and ending with the execution of the procedure named
  procedure-name-2". In `PERFORM P2 THRU P1` with P1 written before P2 and P2 the last paragraph, control runs from P2 off
  the end of the procedure division and never reaches the return mechanism, so the PERFORM does not return under any
  reading. §14.6.3 ("There is also no next executable statement after the last statement in a source element when the
  procedure in which it appears is not being executed under the control of some other COBOL statement … an implicit
  GOBACK statement without any optional phrases is executed") can be read two ways here: P2 IS in the PERFORM's range, so
  the sentence's first case does not literally fire and the standard names no next statement; or running off the source
  element is the implicit GOBACK whatever is active. The standard does not decide, so CLAUDE.md rule 1 takes GnuCOBOL
  3.2, which ends the activation after P2 (measured 2026-10-22 for kb/Work PB3511, `cobc -x -free -std=cobol2014`, with
  its `-Wsuspicious-perform-thru` warning). **Determination:** the implicit GOBACK, the same as when a GO TO has left the range (where §14.6.3 does
  decide): `DispatchEmitter.EmitDispatchMethod`'s end-of-element arm throws the element's return signal from whatever
  nested dispatch reaches it. Witness: `conformance:cases/14.6.3-Explicit-and-implicit-transfers-of-control/pb3511_implicit_goback_perform_thru_inverted`.
  A SORT input or output procedure is the same question: a GO TO that leaves the named procedure for the source
  element's last paragraph stays in the procedure's range (§14.9.40.4 GR13: "The range includes all statements that are
  executed as the result of a transfer of control in the range of the output procedure") but never reaches its return
  mechanism (GR11, GR14), and GnuCOBOL 3.2 ends the activation there too (measured 2026-10-22, `cobc -x -free
  -std=cobol2002`), so the same determination applies; the SORT never passes control to the statement after it.
  Witnesses: `pb3511_implicit_goback_sort_input_procedure` and `pb3511_implicit_goback_sort_output_procedure` in the same
  directory. A MERGE output procedure is the same question again (§14.9.24.4 GR8, GR9), and in a called program the
  implicit GOBACK returns to the CALL with the abandoned MERGE's USING files still open, because GR7 c) terminates them
  only "after control passes the last statement in the output procedure" (GnuCOBOL 3.2 differs on this one point: it
  reads and closes the USING files before the output procedure); witness
  `pb3511_implicit_goback_sort_merge_called_program`. A procedure whose range ENDS at the last paragraph completes there
  and resumes the SORT or MERGE (`pb3511_sort_merge_procedure_ends_at_last_paragraph`, 85 to 2023).

- **D-PROP1 — an object property that a statement stores only IN PART: the GET supplies the kept positions, and a class
  WITH NO GET still compiles (kb/Work PB2618).** §14.9.43.4 GR7: "All other portions of the data item referenced by
  identifier-3 will contain data that was present before this execution of the STRING statement"; §8.4.3.3.4 GR5 makes a
  reference-modified receiver "a unique data item that is a subset of the data item referenced by identifier-1", so a
  store into it leaves the rest of the item as it was. An object property stands in for its data item through a
  conceptual temporary (§8.4.3.9.4 GR2, GR3), and what was "present before" is the property's value. **Determination:**
  a property reference at a position that stores only part of the item (STRING's identifier-3, and any receiver written
  through a reference modifier) runs its GET method first, when the class has one, then the statement, then its SET
  method, so the positions the statement did not reach keep the property's value. The standard does not say whether such
  a position is a SENDING use of the property, which would make §8.4.3.9.3 SR3 demand a get method ("If the object
  property is used as a sending item, a get property method shall exist"); §14.9.43.3 SR10 calls STRING's identifier-3 "the
  receiving operand", and a STRING into a property WITH NO GET was already accepted (kb/Work PB1275). This compiler keeps
  that: the position is a RECEIVING use (SR4 asks for a set method, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2618-string-into-property-no-set`),
  and when the class has no get method the receiving temporary starts as spaces (an alphanumeric property; zeros for a numeric one) at EVERY execution of the statement, reset before it (measured: STRING "Q" gives "Q     ", the second time too; `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2618_no_get_part_store_every_execution`), so
  the positions a partial store does not reach are those, not an error and not a stale value. GnuCOBOL has no object
  properties, so no vendor behavior informs the reading. Witnesses:
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2618_string_into_property_keeps_unreferenced`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2618-string-into-property-no-set`, `conformance:cases/8.4.3.9-Object-property/pb1275_property_set_formats` (the
  WITH NO GET case, filled whole).

- **D-RM1 — a reference-modified argument passed BY REFERENCE to a method, a prototyped program, a program the NESTED phrase activates or a function**
  (kb/Work PB2077; decision PB3098, 2026-10-12). §8.4.3.3.4 GR5/GR6 define the unique data item with class, category,
  usage and no JUSTIFIED clause — and no PICTURE clause; §9.3.6 match rule 3 e) and §14.8.2.3.2 rule 2 require "the
  same … PICTURE … clauses". So BY REFERENCE the slice matches and conforms only to an alphanumeric group formal of no
  more bytes (3 c), §14.8.2.2 rule 1), on the typed lane (a compile-time refusal, COBOL0828) and the universal lane
  (EC-OO-METHOD) alike; an elementary formal takes it BY CONTENT (§9.3.6 4 d)). Two readings the text leaves open:
  **(a)** a slice whose length is a run-time value is measured for the compile-time rule 1 by its MAXIMUM extent — the
  model §14.8.2.2 gives an occurs-depending group ("the maximum length is used"): identifier-1's positions from a
  static leftmost position on, or all of them, where identifier-1's positions are at their bound when its own length
  is a run-time value — a DYNAMIC LENGTH item's §8.5.1.10.1 maximum size (so a slice of a `LIMIT 3` item never fits a
  4-byte group formal), and for an ANY LENGTH item, whose description fixes no bound (§13.18.2.4 GR1 b): its length
  is the argument's), the largest character string the run time holds, so every group formal is admitted (kb/Work
  PB3128) — and by its evaluated length at the boundary: the universal lane raises
  EC-OO-UNIVERSAL when it is shorter than the group formal; the typed lane's formal holds the slice padded to the
  formal's width and writes back through the slice, truncated to it. Such a slice states its storage area WITH its
  evaluated length (`CellPointer.Extent`), so a formal is laid over a slice at least as long as itself (§14.2.3 GR8: a
  second argument over the same positions sees its stores, on the CALL lane too) and never reads or writes past a
  shorter one; **(b)** the ANY LENGTH item of match rule 3 e) is read through §14.8.2.3.2
  "Additionally" d)/e) (a formal's ANY LENGTH matches any argument length, every other clause still compared; an ANY
  LENGTH argument needs an ANY LENGTH formal), because the literal reading empties §13.18.2 for methods. One relation
  serves both lanes, so through a universal receiver a `PIC X(4)` argument matches a `PIC X ANY LENGTH` formal and the
  bound method is then refused by §14.9.23.4 GR7 c) (EC-OO-UNIVERSAL, not EC-OO-METHOD); a slice matches no ANY LENGTH
  formal (it has no PICTURE clause). GnuCOBOL 3.2 gives no answer: its prototype conformance check reads identifier-1's
  description and ignores the modifier (measured). Witnesses: `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb480_universal_refmod_evaluated_length`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2077_refmod_argument_both_lanes`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb480_universal_any_length_omitted`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3128_refmod_any_length_argument`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3128_refmod_dynamic_length_argument`; the CALL and function lanes ask the same relation at bind time (kb/Work PB3101): `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3101_activation_lanes_one_relation` and the negatives `pb3101-prototype-call-refmod-by-reference`, `pb3101-function-refmod-by-reference`, `pb3101-nested-refmod-into-any-length`.
- **D-N8 — a group sender into a national DYNAMIC LENGTH receiver** (kb/Work PB546; decision PB3099, 2026-10-12).
  §14.9.25.4 GR4 makes the move a byte copy and §8.5.1.10.4 sets the receiver's new length to the content's. An odd
  byte count cannot be national content (D-N1: two bytes per position), so the last position is completed with the
  alphanumeric space GR4's elementary-move fill supplies, as a fixed national receiver already is: `MOVE G3 TO DN` with
  a three-byte `G3` leaves `DN` two positions long and `FUNCTION LENGTH(DN)` = 4 (§15.50.4 r6 counts bytes). GnuCOBOL
  3.2 has no dynamic-length items. Implementing site: `ReceivingStore.ContentCharacters` over `CobolBits.NatFromStorage`
  (also the READ of an elementary dynamic-length national record). Witness:
  `conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb546_group_into_national_dynamic`.
- **D-VGB — a BY REFERENCE formal's FIXED table stored past the capacity of the argument's dynamic-capacity table
  creates the occurrences the callee stored into (kb/Work PB2690).** §14.2.3 GR8: "the activated runtime element operates
  as if the formal parameter occupies the same storage area as the argument". A formal table of a fixed (or DEPENDING)
  occurrence count opposite the argument's dynamic-capacity table is legal when the two correspond and match (§8.5.1.12.1,
  §8.5.1.12.2; §8.5.1.12.3 sentence 3: the dynamic-capacity table "is considered to be the same length as the
  corresponding table"), and the callee may subscript it up to its own count. A store to an occurrence past the
  argument's current capacity is therefore a receiving reference to the dynamic-capacity table whose subscript "exceeds
  the current capacity of the table", and §8.5.1.9.3 says what that does: "a new element is automatically created and the
  capacity of the table is increased to the value given by the subscript" (intermediate occurrences too). Until
  kb/Work PB2690 the store was dropped silently and the argument kept its capacity. The occurrences it creates are
  initialized: §8.5.1.9.5, with INITIALIZED, "any elementary items not referenced as receiving operands in a statement
  that creates new elements in that table are first initialized as though they had been the subject of a statement of the
  form INITIALIZE ... WITH FILLER ALL TO VALUE THEN TO DEFAULT", so the intermediate occurrences and every item of a
  created one the callee did not store hold the element's VALUE, exactly as the same store made in the caller leaves them
  (until the second PB2690 landing they came back space filled). **Determination (the latitude the standard leaves):** a
  copy of the argument crosses the boundary and only the finished view comes back, so (i) the formal VIEWS an occurrence
  the argument lacks, when the table writes INITIALIZED, as the occurrence the table creates, the §8.5.1.9.5 NOTE's
  "functionally identical to one where the intermediate occurrences are physically allocated and, if specified,
  initialized": the INITIALIZED recipe, the seed a receiving subscript past the capacity grows the table with
  (`CobolDynTable.CreatedAs`); without the phrase, whose created contents §8.5.1.9.5 leaves "undefined", the view shows
  the space fill, chosen because no numeric store matches it, so a store of the element's own VALUE (a zero) is still
  seen; and (ii) a store past the capacity is the callee's RECEIVING REFERENCE, recorded where it is made: the formal's
  fresh area records the window of every store through a view of it (`StorageCell.Received`, emitted after each store
  through a LINKAGE or BASED view), from the moment the area is filled (`ManagedPointer.Watch`), and the store back
  (`ManagedPointer.OverStorage` → `CobolVarGroup.Overlay`) raises the capacity to the highest occurrence the callee
  referenced as a receiving item, whatever it stored there: the INITIALIZED default, SPACES, the element's VALUE. A callee
  that only reads such an occurrence creates nothing (§8.5.1.9.3 acts on a receiving reference only). A store that reaches
  the area only through a further activation's boundary copy of the whole group (the copy covers every occurrence, so it
  records none, whatever the group's shape and whether the further activation is a CALL, a typed INVOKE or a universal
  one: `CallEmitter.BoundaryCopyWrite`) is recognised by its effect, an occurrence whose image differs from the
  one the view showed. The creation travels on the argument's
  carrier only for a BY REFERENCE crossing (`CobolVarGroup.Created`, stated by `AsVarImage(__byReference: true)` and
  `StorageCell.VarGroupAt(byReference: true)`): a BY CONTENT formal is a record "allocated by the activating runtime element"
  that does "not occupy the same storage area as the argument" (§14.2.3 GR9), filled as by a MOVE, so past the sending
  capacity its fixed table holds the MOVE's space fill (§14.6.9.2 2)) and nothing returns. The same law holds one level
  down for a dynamic-capacity table nested in an element (a created element is the table's created element, its own inner
  table at its creation, with the formal's element stored over it, whichever of the pair's outer tables is the variable
  one), including a fixed table nested in an occurrence of the formal's OWN dynamic-capacity table, whose stores are
  recorded by their subscript path, and across an INVOKE, the universal lane included
  (`CobolVarGroup.Reshape` / `Overlay`'s `OverlaidTable` / `GrownCount` / `OverlaidOccurrences`, shared by the CALL and
  INVOKE boundaries). A fixed-length ARGUMENT cannot grow (it has no more occurrences). The ISO text decides the arm that
  matters, so no vendor behavior was consulted (CLAUDE.md rule 1). Witnesses:
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690_fixed_table_formal_grows_dynamic_argument_call`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690_fixed_table_formal_grows_vlg_element_table_call`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690_fixed_table_formal_grows_dynamic_argument_invoke`, `conformance:cases/14.2-Procedure-division-structure/pb965_vlg_into_fixed_invoke`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690_initialized_created_occurrences_call`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690_initialized_created_occurrences_invoke`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690_store_of_shown_image_grows_capacity_call`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690_store_of_shown_image_grows_capacity_invoke`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690-fixed-table-formal-grows-dynamic-argument-below-2014`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690-initialized-created-occurrences-below-2014`,
  `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb2690-store-of-shown-image-grows-capacity-below-2014`.

- **D-SRCH-DYN — which enclosing occurrence bounds a SEARCH of a dynamic-capacity table nested under other tables**
  (kb/Work PB3365). The scan of a SEARCH or SEARCH ALL ends at the table's "highest permissible occurrence number"
  (§14.9.37.4 GR4, GR9), which for a dynamic-capacity table is its current capacity (§8.5.1.9.1), and each occurrence of an
  enclosing table holds a capacity of its own (§8.5.1.9.2). The standard names the enclosing occurrence only by §14.9.37.4
  GR1 ("The subscript that is used to determine the occurrence of each superordinate table to search is specified by the
  user in the WHEN phrases") and by §14.9.37.3 SR2, which lets identifier-1 write the enclosing subscripts. **WiseOwl COBOL
  bounds the scan by the occurrence identifier-1 names when it writes every enclosing subscript, otherwise by the
  occurrence the FIRST WHEN-phrase reference to the table (or to an item within it), in source order, subscripts; a
  nested dynamic-capacity table that neither names is refused (COBOL2075).** The enclosing subscripts are evaluated
  once, when the statement begins; the standard leaves a table referenced at two different enclosing occurrences in its
  WHEN phrases undefined. A fixed or occurs-depending table needs no such choice: its bound is the same for every
  occurrence of its enclosing tables. Witnesses: `conformance:cases/14.9.37-SEARCH/pb3365_search_nested_dynamic_table`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.37-SEARCH/pb3365_search_nested_dynamic_property`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.37-SEARCH/pb3365-search-nested-dynamic-no-occurrence`.

- **D-R3 — which function a REPOSITORY `FUNCTION F` specifier names when its externalized name and its word name two
  different functions** (kb/Work PB989, PB2102; owner decision 2026-10-05; `docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-external-repository.md`
  §8.3). §12.3.8.4 GR11 takes the details by EXTERNALIZED name: a) "if the externalized name of the function prototype
  is the externalized name of a function definition specified previously in the same compilation group" (11) a)), b) a
  function prototype definition of that externalized name, c) the external repository (GR11 NOTE 2: the externalized
  name is literal-5, or the word itself without AS). §12.3.8.3 SR10 states LEGALITY with alternatives one of which is the
  WORD — "the name of a function definition specified previously in this compilation group" and "the name of a function
  prototype specified in this compilation group" (10)) — and §8.4.6.7 lets the user-function-name be referenced "in the
  REPOSITORY paragraph of any source element that follows that function definition". With `FUNCTION-ID. FX AS "F"` and
  `FUNCTION-ID. F AS "G"` both ahead of `FUNCTION F`, the two clauses name different functions and the standard does
  not rank them; CLAUDE.md rule 1's order settles it by GnuCOBOL, whose 3.2.0 resolves by externalized name only
  (measured 2026-10-05). **WiseOwl COBOL:** (1) GR11 a) then b) by externalized name; whichever hits names the
  function. (2) When both miss, the function the WORD names: the definition specified before the referencing element
  whose user-function-name is F (its externalized name, "G", is what is activated), else the function prototype of that
  name. (3) Whenever step 1 selects a function and a DIFFERENT function carries the word F and is visible to the element,
  the externalized name is used, as GnuCOBOL does, and the compiler warns **COBOL2969** naming both. Legal source is
  never rejected: a specifier legal only by SR10's word alternative or §8.4.6.7 takes step 2. GR11 c) — the external
  repository — is not yet implemented (kb/Work PB1086; design slice 7, kb/Work PB2103), so a specifier that steps 1 and
  2 miss has no details today; slice 7 adds the repository entry recorded under the word as the last step-2 alternative
  and extends step 3 to a function in the repository. Witnesses:
  `conformance:cases/11.5-FUNCTION-ID/pb989_function_externalized_name_wins`,
  `conformance:cases/11.5-FUNCTION-ID/pb989_function_prototype_externalized_name`,
  `conformance:cases/8.3.2.2-User-defined-words/pb303_as_externalized_name`,
  `conformance-test:RepositoryDetailsOrderTests.ExternalizedNameWins_AndTheFunctionThatOnlyTheWordNamesIsReported`,
  `conformance-test:RepositoryDetailsOrderTests.AnAsLiteralThatNamesTheOtherFunction_SelectsItWithoutAWarning`,
  `conformance-test:RepositoryDetailsOrderTests.APrototypeAndItsDefinition_AreOneFunction_AndDrawNoWarning`,
  `unit:GroupRepositoryOrderDriftTests`.

- **D-EXPECT — a syntax error names what the parse expects at the token (kb/Work PB3428, PB3861).** §4.2.2 requires a
  compile-time indication of "violations of the general formats" and leaves its wording to the implementor. Where the
  token written is of a kind the parse does not take at its position, **COBOL5506** names the element written (a
  word, a literal by its §8.3.3.1 category — "alphanumeric, boolean, national, or numeric", the integer literal of
  §8.3.3.3.2 among the numeric ones — a figurative constant, or the separator period) and what is expected there:
  every keyword, context word and literal category, where all of it can be named (`OBJECT-COMPUTER. XYZ MEMORY SIZE
  12 FOO.` expects CHARACTERS, MODULES or WORDS; `SEGMENT-LIMIT IS.` an integer literal; `OPEN F` EXTEND, I-O, INPUT
  or OUTPUT), and otherwise the literal categories expected (`SET IX TO "A"`: of the literals, only a numeric
  literal). Context words that are no lexer token are named by running the predicate that recognizes them. The
  figurative constant ZERO is named only where a ZERO written at the token would parse: the parse takes the
  arithmetic ZERO that the token rewriter makes of a ZERO beside an arithmetic operator (`COMPUTE W-N = 1 + "A"`
  names it), and naming it after `SET IX TO`, where the parse refuses a sole ZERO, would direct the user to a rewrite
  the compiler refuses. **What is expected is the compiler's parse, a superset of the
  general format** wherever a later check names the departure better (INSPECT's tallying phrase is parsed with FIRST
  and TRAILING so COBOL2269 refuses them by name; the parse takes a later edition's words at every edition), so the
  message says "expected", never "the general format admits". It is not given where a statement may begin (the
  imperative-statement and statement-shape diagnostics own those positions), where a forgotten separator period
  would let the next sentence or entry follow (COBOL0307), or at a closed format's residue (COBOL1941 / 1970 / 1971).
  Witnesses: `conformance:cases/12.3.6-OBJECT-COMPUTER/pb3428-memory-size-unit-word`,
  `conformance:cases/12.3.6-OBJECT-COMPUTER/pb3428-segment-limit-integer-omitted`,
  `conformance:cases/12.3.6-OBJECT-COMPUTER/pb3428_memory_size_modules_85`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb3861-set-index-to-alphanumeric-literal`,
  `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb3861_set_index_to_integer_literal`, `unit:WrittenKindRefusalTests`.

### 3.1 Implementor behavior in Annex A.2 undefined cases (kb/Work PB1907)

Annex A.2 lists situations whose results the standard leaves undefined, and §4.4 2) says that "A COBOL run unit that
allows these situations to happen is a conforming run unit, although the resultant execution is not defined by
standard COBOL" (`cite.py --check 4.4 "A COBOL run unit that allows these situations to happen is a conforming run
unit"` → OK 2)). This is NOT a §8 "no observable obligation" derivation: for each case below the owner decided
(2026-10-01) to DOCUMENT what WiseOwl COBOL does, align it with GnuCOBOL where GnuCOBOL measurably differs (CLAUDE.md
rule 1: the standard where it controls, otherwise GnuCOBOL; IBM Enterprise COBOL and Micro Focus are consulted only
where GnuCOBOL has nothing, and here GnuCOBOL 3.2 was built and run on every repro), and pin the documented behavior
with a golden so it cannot drift. The documented behavior is a promise about THIS compiler, never a statement about
what the standard requires. For the overlapping-operand cases IBM Enterprise COBOL 6.4 calls the result
"unpredictable" (Language Reference, "Overlapping operands") and Micro Focus calls it "undefined"; neither documents
a result, so GnuCOBOL 3.2 (libcob, measured on every case below) is the comparator.

- **D-INS1 — an INSPECT TALLYING counter in the storage of identifier-1, a pattern or a delimiter (§14.9.22.4 GR13,
  Annex A.2 item 21 d)).** `cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 "If identifier-1, identifier-3, or identifier-4 occupies the same
  storage area as identifier-2, the result of the execution of this statement is undefined"` → OK 13); `cite.py --check
  A.2 "occupies the same storage area as the TALLYING identifier"` → OK 21) d). **Determination:** the operands of
  one TALLYING phrase list are taken in source order, and each operand's count is computed from the state of the
  statement AFTER the operands before it have stored theirs (GR11 still ADDS each count to its counter). The counter's
  new value is therefore visible to identifier-1's image, to a later operand's pattern and to its BEFORE/AFTER
  delimiter: `INSPECT G TALLYING T FOR ALL "A" T FOR ALL "2"` with T inside G counts the "2" the first operand
  stored (D2 = `31A1A1`, not `21A1A1`). A single-operand statement is unaffected (the counter is stored after the
  scan). The mechanism is one rule in `InspectEmitter.EmitBody`: before each operand after the first, when the
  previous counter MAY share storage with identifier-1 or any operand the cycle reads, the image is read again and
  the one comparison cycle re-run (`StorageOverlap.MayShareStorage` is a conservative declaration-level proof of
  disjointness: containment, REDEFINES, LINKAGE and BASED storage answer "may"; a false "may" costs one re-run and
  changes no result). **A statement whose counters overlap nothing it reads is the single shared comparison cycle of
  GR8, unchanged** — so two non-overlapping phrases still compete for characters in source order at each position
  (`ALL "BC"` then `ALL "AB"` over "ABCABC" counts BC=0, AB=2, §14.9.22.4 GR8 a), b)); GnuCOBOL runs every phrase as
  its own pass and counts BC=2, AB=0 there, a divergence from the standard on a case with no overlap, which this
  compiler does not follow because the standard controls). Measured against GnuCOBOL 3.2: D2, D3, D5 and the
  reference-modified case agree. Pinned by `conformance:cases/14.9.22-INSPECT/pb1907_inspect_tally_overlap` (D1-D5, RM, and controls C1
  and C2: C1 a statement that overlaps nothing, C2 one the compiler cannot prove disjoint although it is).
- **D-INS2 — a FORMAT 3 INSPECT whose counter is in the storage of identifier-1 or of a REPLACING operand (§14.9.22.4
  GR13 with GR19).** `cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 "A format 3 INSPECT statement is interpreted and executed as though two
  successive INSPECT statements specifying the same identifier-1 had been written"` → OK 19). **Determination:** the
  statement runs as GR19 words it: item identification once, then the whole tallying statement (counters stored), then
  the whole replacing statement over identifier-1 and operand values as they stand when it starts. A counter inside
  identifier-1 therefore keeps its tallied value (`INSPECT G5 TALLYING G5T FOR ALL "A" REPLACING ALL "A" BY "B"` over
  `0AAA` gives `3BBB`; before this entry the replacing half wrote back the pre-tally image and the counter was lost,
  `0BBB`), and a replacing operand that is the counter reads the counter's new value. The re-read is the same
  `StorageOverlap` test as D-INS1, applied between the two halves. GnuCOBOL 3.2 emits the two statements separately
  and gives the same lines. Pinned by `conformance:cases/14.9.22-INSPECT/pb1907_inspect_format3_counter_overlap`.
- **D-INS3 — an INSPECT REPLACING pattern, replacement or delimiter in the storage of identifier-1 (§14.9.22.4 GR18,
  Annex A.2 item 21 e)).** `cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 "If identifier-3, identifier-4, or identifier-5 occupies the same
  storage area as identifier-1, the result of the execution of this statement is undefined"` → OK 18); `cite.py
  --check A.2 "occupies the same storage area as the INSPECT identifier"` → OK 21) e). **Determination:** every
  operand value and identifier-1's image are read when the REPLACING pass starts (GR6, GR9), the comparison cycle
  matches that image, and the single store at the end is the only write, so an operand never observes a replacement
  of its own statement (`REPLACING ALL "Q" BY "R" ALL "S" BY X1(1:1)` over `QS` gives `RQ`). This was already the
  behavior and GnuCOBOL 3.2 gives the same results on every probe; no code changed. Pinned by
  `conformance:cases/14.9.22-INSPECT/pb1907_inspect_replacing_overlap`.
- **D-INS4 — an INSPECT CONVERTING from-set, to-set or delimiter in the storage of identifier-1 (§14.9.22.4 GR21,
  Annex A.2 item 21 f)).** `cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 "If identifier-4, identifier-6, or identifier-7 occupies the same
  storage area as identifier-1, the result of the execution of this statement is undefined"` → OK 21); `cite.py
  --check A.2 "the CONVERTING identifier, TO identifier, AFTER identifier, or BEFORE identifier occupies the same
  storage area as the INSPECT identifier"` → OK 21) f). **Determination:** as D-INS3 — the sets and the delimiters are
  the values at the start of the statement, a repeated from-set character maps by its first occurrence (GR23, `cite.py
  --check 14.9.22.4 "the first occurrence of the character is used for replacement"` → OK 23)), and the one store at
  the end is the only write (`CONVERTING X5 TO "WXYZ"` over `ABCA` gives `WXYW`). Already the behavior; GnuCOBOL 3.2
  agrees on every probe; no code changed. Pinned by `conformance:cases/14.9.22-INSPECT/pb1907_inspect_converting_overlap`.
- **D-WRT1 — the bytes a WRITE or REWRITE sends past the end of record-name-1** (kb/Work PB1907; Annex A.2 items 64
  and 49). §14.9.51.4 GR13: *"When record-name-1 is specified, if the number of bytes to be written to the file is
  greater than the number of bytes in record-name-1, the content of the bytes that extend outside the end of
  record-name-1 are undefined"* (`cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 "the content of the bytes that extend outside the end of
  record-name-1 are undefined"` → OK 13)); §14.9.35.4 GR15 says the same of REWRITE (`cite.py --check 14.9.35.4
  "the content of the bytes that extend outside the end of record-name-1 are undefined"` → OK 15)). **The NUMBER of
  bytes is not latitude, and WiseOwl COBOL writes exactly the standard's count:** §13.18.43.4 GR13 a) takes it from
  the DEPENDING ON item (`--check 13.18.43.4 "If data-name-1 is specified, by the content of the data item referenced
  by data-name-1"` → OK 13) a)), GR6 makes every record of a Format 1 file integer-1 bytes (`--check 13.18.43.4
  "Integer-1 specifies the number of bytes contained in each record in the file"` → OK 6)), and the status stays
  `'00'` with GR14's `'44'` for a count outside the bounds. **The CONTENT is this compiler's determination: position
  n of the record sent, for n past the end of record-name-1, is position n of the record area, and a position that
  no record description of the file occupies is a space** (a national space in a national area). The area is the
  storage every level-1 entry under the FD implicitly redefines (§13.18.33.4 GR3, `--check 13.18.33.4 "Multiple
  level 1 entries subordinate to a FD or SD entry represent implicit redefinitions of the same area"` → OK 3)), so a
  program that fills the long record and then writes a shorter one writes the shorter one followed by the rest of
  the long one. WRITE FROM and REWRITE FROM are the same case: GR5 a) / §14.9.35.4 GR7 a) MOVE into record-name-1
  and then run the statement without FROM (`--check 14.9.51.4 "The result of the execution of a WRITE statement
  specifying record-name-1 and the FROM phrase is equivalent"` → OK 5)). One rule serves WRITE and REWRITE, fixed and
  variable-length records, record sequential, relative and indexed files; a REWRITE needs no second determination
  because §14.9.35.4 GR15 is GR13's twin and the same predicate answers both. On a NATIONAL record area the space is
  the national space, the two bytes 00 20, in record sequential and relative files alike, and the short tail of a
  variable-length record read into a larger area is padded the same way (witness
  `conformance:wiseowl/cases/14.9.51-WRITE/pb1880_national_pad_record_sequential_and_relative`; the LINE SEQUENTIAL
  fill is the standard's own, §14.9.30.4 GR15, `…/12.4.5.10-ORGANIZATION/pb327_national_line_sequential_fill`).
  **Where the rule does not apply, because nothing is left undefined:** (1) a variable-length file WITHOUT a
  DEPENDING ON item transfers record-name-1 itself (§13.18.43.4 GR13 b)/c)); (2) a LINE SEQUENTIAL file's transfer
  is defined outright — a WRITE drops the spaces right of the rightmost non-space character (§14.9.51.4 GR21,
  `--check 14.9.51.4 "any spaces to the right of the rightmost non-space character are not transferred to
  file-name-1"` → OK 21)) or, with DEPENDING ON, fills with spaces (GR22, `--check 14.9.51.4 "the record area is,
  if necessary, filled to the right of the rightmost non-space character with one or more space characters"` → OK
  22)), and a REWRITE appends spaces (§14.9.35.4 GR17 c), `--check 14.9.35.4 "then a sufficient number of the space
  character is appended"` → OK 17) c)); (3) a record sequential REWRITE whose record-name-1 is shorter than the
  record it replaces is unsuccessful, `'44'` (§14.9.35.4 GR16, PB1168), so no byte is sent; (4) an out-of-line
  record-name-1 (D-FRA: a variable-length group, a dynamic-length or pointer-class record) has no window over the
  area, so it is sent at its own image and the positions past it are spaces. The predicate is
  `FileModel.TransfersPastRecord`, asked by the one image helper `SequentialIoEmitter.SentRecordImage` for the
  sequential and the keyed WRITE and REWRITE emitters; the runtime's `FileConnector.Stored` cuts the image to the
  transferred length or pads it, unchanged.
  **Survey (CLAUDE.md rule 1).** GnuCOBOL 3.2 writes from the file's record area, but `cob_write` clamps the
  DEPENDING ON length to record-name-1's size, and a RECORD CONTAINS file with a shorter 01 becomes variable-length
  (`libcob/fileio.c` `cob_write`, `cobc/tree.c` `finalize_file`; measured with a 3.2.0 build: the variable records
  are 5 bytes, the fixed records carry the area content). That departs from §13.18.43.4 GR13 a)/GR6, which control
  the length, so the length is NOT adopted from GnuCOBOL (owner decision 2026-10-01); its use of the shared area
  for the content agrees with this rule. IBM Enterprise COBOL 6.4 documents the length as ISO does and is silent on
  the content. Micro Focus Visual COBOL 7.0, WRITE statement, Format 1 general rules: *"When the file contains
  fixed-length records, the entire record area is written to the file"*, the rule extended here to
  variable-length records so that one rule decides both. Before PB1907 the bytes past record-name-1 were spaces.
  **A file with no RECORD clause** is the implied Format 1 of D-FRA (`--check 13.18.43.4 "If format 1 is implied,
  integer-1 shall be the record size of the largest record description entry in this file description entry"` → OK
  5) a)), so a short record of a multi-01 FD of fixed shape is sent at the largest record's length too; the NIST
  program RL106A's INFO-ONLY REL-TEST-10 line, which reports whether such a file wrote fixed-length records, therefore
  now reads `FIXED LENGTH RECORDS` (its golden is re-baselined: the line is informational, and §13.18.43.4 GR5 leaves
  the implied format to the implementor).
  Pinned by `conformance:cases/14.9.51-WRITE/pb1907_write_past_record`, `conformance:cases/14.9.35-REWRITE/pb1907_keyed_rewrite_past_record` (relative,
  indexed, REWRITE, WRITE FROM and REWRITE FROM) and `conformance:cases/14.9.35-REWRITE/pb1907_past_record_whole_record` (the cases
  above where nothing is left undefined).
  **RELEASE is the same case** (§14.9.32.4 GR6, Annex A.2 item 45; kb/Work PB322 F): `cite.py --check 14.9.32.4 "If the
  number of bytes to be released to the sort operation is greater than the number of bytes in record-name-1, the
  content of the bytes that extend beyond the end of record-name-1 are undefined."` → OK 6). The sort-merge file with no
  RECORD clause is the implied Format 1 of D-FRA, whose integer-1 is the largest record description entry's size
  (§13.18.43.4 GR5 a)), so `RELEASE A` of a 4-byte description A beside a 10-byte B releases 10 bytes — A's four
  followed by the area's last six, which are B's — through the same helper (`SequentialIoEmitter.SentRecordImage`) and the
  same predicate (`FileModel.TransfersPastRecord`); an SD with a DEPENDING ON item releases that many bytes of the same
  image. Before PB322 F a RELEASE sent record-name-1's own size, so ONE SD held records of two sizes and a GIVING file
  received `AAAA` followed by spaces. Pinned by `conformance:cases/13.18.43-RECORD/pb322_release_short_record_fixed_sd`.
- **D-OVL1 — operands that overlap: a MOVE (and an arithmetic statement) reads its sender in full, then writes
  its receiver** (kb/Work PB1907; Annex A.2 item 36; `GR-14.6.10-1`). §14.6.10 1): "When the data items are not
  described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is undefined" (`cite.py --check 14.6.10
  "When the data items are not described by the same data description entry"` → OK, 1)); 2): "When the data items
  are described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is the same as if the data items
  shared no part of their respective storage areas" (OK, 2)); Annex A.2 item 36 lists both the entries that do not
  share a description (a) and "one or more of the operands is reference-modified" (b) (`cite.py --check A.2 "When
  one or more of the operands is reference-modified"` → OK, 36) b)). **WiseOwl COBOL's behavior is the snapshot:**
  the sending operand is evaluated completely before any part of the receiving operand changes, whatever the two
  share, so `MOVE X(1:5) TO X(2:5)` of `ABCDEF` gives `AABCDE` (the characters 1 to 5 are copied as they stood),
  the backward move `MOVE X(2:5) TO X(1:5)` gives `BCDEFF`, a REDEFINES view gives the same, and a group sent into
  its own subordinate item, or the reverse, copies the image it held when the statement began. A shorter sender
  space-fills the receiver after the copy (`MOVE Y(1:3) TO Y(2:5)` gives `AABC  `). `ADD M2 TO M1`, where `M2`
  redefines the last three digits of `M1`, reads both operands before it stores: `1234 + 234` gives `1468`. This is
  what GnuCOBOL does for every one of these shapes (GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 built and run on each; its `memmove`-based
  alphanumeric moves and its digit-extracting numeric moves are snapshots). Witness: `conformance:cases/14.6.10-Overlapping-operands/pb1907_overlap_move` (the `RM-*`, `RD-*`, `GRP-SUB`, `SUB-GRP`,
  `RM-PAD`, `NUM-ADD`, `JUST-EQ` and `NUM-SAME` lines).

- **D-OVL2 — an overlapping MOVE writes its receiver while it reads its sender: GnuCOBOL's order** (kb/Work PB1907,
  PB1910; Annex A.2 item 36; `GR-14.6.10-1`). GnuCOBOL's `libcob` differs from the snapshot of D-OVL1 in five
  families, all because the library prepares or writes the receiver while it is still reading the sender, and the
  owner chose to follow it (2026-10-01). **(a) A JUSTIFIED RIGHT receiver with a shorter alphanumeric sender:**
  §13.18.32.4 2) aligns the data "at the rightmost character position" of a receiver "larger than the sending operand"
  (`cite.py --check 13.18.32.4 "the receiving data item is described with the JUSTIFIED clause and it is larger than
  the sending operand"` → OK, 2)); WiseOwl COBOL writes the leading pad positions (receiver size minus sender size,
  space-filled) FIRST, then moves the sender, so a sender that overlaps those positions reads spaces: with `J1 PIC
  X(4)` holding `ABCD` and `J2 PIC X(3) JUSTIFIED RIGHT` redefining its last three characters, `MOVE J1(1:2) TO J2`
  gives `A A ` (the snapshot `A AB` is not produced). A sender of the same size or larger is a plain `memmove` and
  stays the snapshot (`JUST-EQ`, `AABC`). The sender may be an alphanumeric or alphabetic item, a group, or a
  reference-modified slice; a numeric sender keeps the snapshot. **(b) Conversion into a numeric DISPLAY or a
  PACKED-DECIMAL receiver is IN PLACE** (`cob_move_display_to_display`, `cob_move_alphanum_to_display`,
  `cob_move_display_to_packed`, `cob_move_packed_to_display`): the library clears the receiver and then writes it one
  digit (one digit pair, for PACKED-DECIMAL), left to right, taking each from the sender's bytes AS THE STORAGE THEN
  HOLDS THEM. A position the receiver has already written is read back as the receiver's content. WiseOwl COBOL runs
  the same algorithm (`OverlappingMove` in the runtime, one method per family) on the two storage images laid over
  each other, for a sending numeric DISPLAY item whose description differs from the receiver's (GnuCOBOL's compiler
  copies identical descriptions byte for byte, and so does this: the snapshot, `NUM-SAME`), for an alphanumeric
  sending item or slice, and for a PACKED-DECIMAL sending item into a numeric DISPLAY receiver; a group sender is a
  group move (§14.9.25.4 GR4, `cite.py --check 14.9.25.4 "alphanumeric to alphanumeric elementary move"` → OK, 4)) and
  is not touched. Measured results (`9(6)` holding `123456`): `PIC 9(5) PACKED-DECIMAL` over its first three bytes gives
  `00456` (the receiver's cleared bytes are read as zeros); over its last three bytes `23300` — neither the snapshot
  `23456` nor "clear the receiver, then convert" (`23000`), because the second digit pair is formed from the byte the
  first pair has just written; `PIC 9(4)` over bytes 4 to 7 gives `3333` (each digit written is the next one read);
  `PIC 9(3)` over the last three digits of `9(4)` holding `1234` gives `000` (`NUM-MOVE`); an alphanumeric `X(6)`
  sender behaves as the numeric one (`3333`, and `3434` for the receiver over bytes 5 to 8). The sender's operational
  sign is read BEFORE the receiver is written and written back after it, as `libcob` does, so a receiver that covers
  the sender's sign byte ends with the sender's sign punched onto whatever that byte then holds (`MOVE S4 TO S5`, `S4
  PIC S9(4)` holding `-1234` and `S5 PIC S9(5)` over its bytes 2 to 6, gives `01p1p` under the ASCII
  convention and `01}1}` under the IBM one); a PACKED-DECIMAL sender's sign is read from its last byte AFTER the store
  (`P-SIGN`: `S9(7) PACKED-DECIMAL` holding `-1234567` into `S9(4) SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE` over its first five bytes
  gives `+4567`). The IBM and ASCII conventions both follow `libcob` under `-fsign=EBCDIC` and `-fsign=ASCII`
  respectively. **Scope — only where the overlap is a compile-time fact.** The compiler decides at bind time
  (`MoveOverlap.Classify`, carried on `MoveStore.Overlap`): both operands lie in one storage area (a REDEFINES class, or
  one record) and every offset and length is a constant (`StorageExtent`). An operand under OCCURS, a dynamic or
  variable-length item, a NATIONAL or BIT operand and a reference modification with a run-time bound are not provably
  overlapping and keep the snapshot; a MOVE that cannot overlap emits exactly what it always did. A reference-modified
  RECEIVER is never converted in place (§8.4.3.3.4 6), "the unique data item is considered to be an elementary data item
  without the JUSTIFIED clause", `cite.py --check 8.4.3.3.4 "without the JUSTIFIED clause"` → OK, 6)), and a
  reference-modified numeric item is an alphanumeric one (6) c), `cite.py --check 8.4.3.3.4 "numeric-edited are
  considered class and category national if the usage is national; otherwise they are considered class and category
  alphanumeric"` → OK), so no numeric receiver is a slice. Because Annex A.2 36 b) makes any reference-modified
  operand's overlap undefined, a slice of the receiver itself counts: `MOVE JR(1:2) TO JR`, `JR PIC X(4) JUSTIFIED RIGHT`
  holding `ABCD`, gives four spaces; `MOVE NR(1:3) TO NR` is the alphanumeric-to-numeric family. **Measured GnuCOBOL
  differences not adopted:** (i) GnuCOBOL moves a numeric DISPLAY item into a shorter JUSTIFIED RIGHT alphanumeric item
  keeping its LEFTMOST digits (`MOVE 1234 TO X(3) JUSTIFIED RIGHT` gives `123`), which is not an overlap effect and
  contradicts §13.18.32.4's right alignment; WiseOwl COBOL keeps `234` (the ISO text controls). (ii) The sign of a ZERO
  result: GnuCOBOL keeps the sender's sign on a zero result in EVERY MOVE, overlapping or not (`MOVE -1000 TO PIC S9(3)`
  stores `00p`, a negative-signed zero, and DISPLAY shows `+000` and `IF < 0` is false on both compilers), and WiseOwl
  COBOL stores a positive zero (`00{` under the IBM convention). That is a representation of the sign of zero, not an
  overlap effect; it is documented with the SIGN encoding determinations (Annex A.1 items 177 and 178), and the
  in-place conversions above reproduce the library's negative zero only because they reproduce its sign handling.
  (iii) A numeric-edited receiver: `cob_move_display_to_edited` scans the picture while it reads the sender and
  back-patches positions it has already written (floating insertion, sign symbols), so its result for a receiver to the
  right of the sender's digits depends on the order of those steps and is not a rule that can be stated beside the
  editing one; where the receiver does not clobber an unread digit (`3456` for `ZZZ9` over either end of `123456`) it
  agrees with the snapshot, and the shapes that differ are listed in kb/Work/PB1910. (iv) A PACKED-DECIMAL sender into a
  PACKED-DECIMAL receiver: `cob_move_bcd` clears the receiver and then calls `memcpy` over overlapping storage, which the
  C standard leaves undefined and whose result depends on the C library, not on a rule. (v) Under the IBM convention
  only (`-fsign=EBCDIC`), a signed overpunched DISPLAY sender into a BINARY receiver that covers the sender's sign byte:
  the library re-punches that byte after the binary store; the ASCII convention, which is GnuCOBOL's default, has no
  such step and agrees with the snapshot. (vi) A P-scaled operand whose digit positions share no decimal position with the other operand's, in a DISPLAY-to-PACKED-DECIMAL move (`9(6)` into `PP9(3) PACKED-DECIMAL`, `PP9(4)` into `9(5) PACKED-DECIMAL`): `cob_move_display_to_packed` then reads the bytes past the sender (storing their nibbles) or writes past the receiver (corrupting the storage after it). That is not a conversion any rule describes, so the snapshot stands (`MoveOverlap.SharesADigitPosition`; `PP-OUT`, `PP-LOW`). Where the windows do share a position the library counts the STORED digits (a P position stores no byte, it moves the scale), and the in-place algorithm agrees with it (`PP-TAIL`, `PP-SEND`, `PP-PACK`; a 320-case P-scaled matrix, every DISPLAY and PACKED-DECIMAL sender and receiver shape at five offsets, differs from the library only in (iv) and in this disjoint case). Implemented in `MoveOverlap` (classification), `StorageExtent` (the overlap
  fact, on `RecordLayout.OffsetInRecord`'s walk), `MoveEmitter.EmitOverlapStore` (the one rendering) and
  `OverlappingMove` (the four algorithms), held by `MoveOverlapDriftTests` and `OverlappingMoveTests`. Witnesses:
  `conformance:cases/14.6.10-Overlapping-operands/pb1907_overlap_move` (`JUST`, `JUST-SELF`, `JUST-GRP`, `JUST-IN`,
  `JUST-LEAD`, `NUM-MOVE`, `NUM-SELF`, `ALNUM-NUM`, `SLICE-NUM`, `NUM-NUM`, `NUM-SCALE`) and
  `conformance:cases/14.6.10-Overlapping-operands/pb1910_overlap_in_place_move` (`PK-HEAD`, `PK-TAIL`, `SMEAR-N`,
  `SMEAR-X`, `SMEAR-X4`, `P-SIGN`, `PP-TAIL`, `PP-SEND`, `PP-PACK`, `PP-OUT`, `PP-LOW`). Every line of those goldens, and a matrix of 1,260 sender-by-receiver-by-offset
  cases over unsigned, signed, separate-sign, scaled, PACKED-DECIMAL and alphanumeric senders and DISPLAY, PACKED-DECIMAL
  and BINARY receivers, was also run through GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 (`cobc -std=cobol2014`, ASCII and `-fsign=EBCDIC`), and the
  outputs are identical except for the families (iii) to (v) and three pairs whose NON-overlapping control already differs in representation.
- **D-UNS1 — UNSTRING runs in place: the SENDING item is read live (kb/Work PB1907, row `GR-14.9.48.4-18`).**
  §14.9.48.4 GR18 — *"If identifier-1, identifier-2, or identifier-3, occupies the same storage area as identifier-4,
  identifier-5, identifier-6, identifier-7, or identifier-8, … the result of the execution of this statement is
  undefined, even if they are defined by the same data description entry"* (`cite.py --check 14.9.48.4 "the result of the
  execution of this statement is undefined, even if they are defined by the same data description entry"` → OK, 18)) —
  and Annex A.2 item 61 (`cite.py --check A.2 "UNSTRING statement. If the UNSTRING identifier, DELIMITED BY identifier,
  or OR identifier, occupies the same storage area as the INTO identifier"` → OK, 61)) leave the case open; GR18 widens
  §14.6.10 rule 2 (*"When the data items are described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is
  the same as if the data items shared no part of their respective storage areas"*, OK) so the overlap is undefined even
  then. **WiseOwl COBOL examines identifier-1 as it stands before each receiving area:** the characters of the sending
  item are read from storage again before every receiving area after the first, so an earlier area's INTO, DELIMITER IN
  and COUNT IN stores into the sender's storage (the same record, a REDEFINES view, a level-66 alias, a BASED item or a
  LINKAGE item passed twice by reference) change what the later areas see. Nothing is snapshotted at initiation except
  the pointer's starting value and, for a fixed-length sender, its size; a variable-length sender is re-read at its current
  extent, and a subscript or reference modifier inside the sender is evaluated again with the re-read. No diagnostic is
  issued. This is libcob `cob_unstring_into`, which scans `unstring_src->data` on every call. Measured (cobc 3.2.0 and
  this build agree): `UNSTRING REC DELIMITED BY "," INTO F2 B C TALLYING IN T`, with `F2` the second 4-byte field of
  `REC = "AAA,BBB,CCC"`, gives `REC=[AAA,AAA CCC] B=[AAA CCC] C=[zzz] T=02` (a snapshot would give `B=[BBB    ] C=[CCC]
