> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — the OPTIONS INITIALIZE background reaches NUMERIC storage too (§11.9.10 / §14.6.2.3.2
> action 1)** (2026-09-02, kb/Work PB152; re-derived 2026-09-30 by owner decision kb/Work R53, kb/Work PB1134).
> §11.9.10.4 GR5 makes the specified-fill-character a CHARACTER, and §14.6.2.3.2 action 1 sets "the storage
> allocated for the implied or associated sections" to it — with no exception for numeric items; §13.18.63.4
> GR4 c)'s "undefined and set to a value that may or may not be allowed" is the baseline §11.9.10.4 GR6 scopes to
> "If the INITIALIZE clause is not specified". **The realization:** character-formed storage takes the fill
> (alphanumeric, national, numeric-edited, DISPLAY-form boolean — D-B1 — including every such member of a Tier-B
> REDEFINES backing); a VALUE-less fixed-point NUMERIC item of a governed section is given image storage at bind
> time and takes the fill as its storage — USAGE DISPLAY the fill characters, BINARY / COMP-5 / PACKED the fill
> byte in every byte (HIGH-VALUES is the byte 0xFF, A.1 item 31), so `INITIALIZE ALL TO X"5A"` leaves a `PIC 9(4)`
> item holding `ZZZZ` and a `PIC 9(4) COMP` item holding X'5A5A'; a floating-point item takes the value its fill
> bytes encode; a USAGE INDEX item's eight bytes each take the fill byte, a NATIONAL-usage numeric item is promoted
> like any other, and an OO method's LOCAL-STORAGE is walked under the method's own effective OPTIONS clause (kb/Work
> PB1134 — no residual remains). **Two carve-outs, each from a RULE and not from convenience:** class
> object / message-tag / pointer take NULL, because GR4 c) states that as a positive requirement in the same
> sentence; and USAGE BIT keeps its packed ceil(n/8) zero seed (D19 / kb/Work PB43), because its storage is
> packed bytes laid out by the §8.5.1.6.3 walk rather than a run of character positions.
> **Scope:** the clause is COBOL-2023 (Annex E.3.3 item 33), so below 2023 it cannot be written and the
> unchanged space/zero seed remains the conformant realization of §11.9.10.4 GR6's "undefined or specified by
> the implementor" there. **§11.9.10.4 GR3 (the SCREEN arm)** has no data items to reach, and since
> 2026-09-02 it is not reached at all: the SCREEN SECTION is a §4.2.7 optional facility documented as
> unsupported in §4 below, so the
> explicit `INITIALIZE … SCREEN …` target is REFUSED by name (COBOL1560,
> `negative/a42-options-initialize-screen`) — it was the module's seventh source shape, parsed into an
> `OptionsSections.Screen` flag that nothing read. ⛔ Only the EXPLICIT leg: GR1 makes `ALL` imply
> LOCAL-STORAGE, SCREEN and WORKING-STORAGE and two of those three are supported, so `INITIALIZE ALL` stays
> legal source. Pinned by `2023/pb152_options_initialize_background`,
> `_sections`, `_local_storage`, `_tier_b`, `_external`, `_figurative` and `_arm_agreement`.
> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — §11.9.10.3 SR1's "one-byte hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal" is §8.3.3.2.2 FORMAT 2, and
> nothing else** (2026-09-02; kb/Work PB152, COBOL1727). "Hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal" is a defined
> term: §8.3.3.2.2 gives the alphanumeric literal exactly two general formats — format 1 (`"…"` / `'…'`) and
> format 2 (`X"…"` / `X'…'`) — and the term names format 2. `INITIALIZE ALL TO "Z"` is therefore **not** a
> conforming spelling however short the literal is; `X"5A"` is, and one byte is exactly two hexadecimal digits
> (§8.3.3.2.3 SR5). This is recorded as a determination because the natural reading of SR1 diverges from its
> letter here, and because the previous decoder took the literal's first character for ANY shape — so
> `INITIALIZE ALL TO "AB"` silently filled with `A`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — the §8.8.1.5.4 r2e development of a non-integer (and past-loop-bound integer) power**
> (2026-08-29, REPLACED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB145 + PB167). r2e leaves the equivalent
> arithmetic expression to the implementor and constrains the DEVELOPMENT: "Operands used in the development of
> that value shall be in SDIDI form. All additions, subtractions, multiplications and divisions performed in the
> development of the result shall be performed in accordance with the corresponding rules in ISO/IEC 60559:2020."
> **WiseOwl COBOL's equivalent expression is `exp(operand-2 × ln operand-1)`, developed entirely on SDIDI operands —
> no binary64 anywhere in it** (`CobolDec.PowCore` / `Ln` / `LnReduced` / `Exponential`: the ln decomposition
> splits the decimal exponent, then takes the atanh series over one of TWO argument reductions — three exact
> square roots to m^(1/8) away from 1, and ln(1+δ) over δ = m − 1 directly inside |m − 1| ≤ ¼, where the roots
> would cancel the difference away; the exp reduction takes out `n × ln 10` so the `10^n` factor is an EXACT
> decimal exponent shift, then runs the Taylor series). **One chosen special case: at operand-2 = ½ the
> equivalent expression is `FUNCTION SQRT(operand-1)`**, whose standard-decimal value §15.84.4 r2 fixes EXACTLY —
> so `b ** 0.5` and `FUNCTION SQRT(b)` agree digit-for-digit by construction rather than by luck. They disagreed
> before, from the 17th significant digit.
> ⛔ **r3 IS NOT PART OF THAT LATITUDE AND IS WRITTEN ONCE.** r2's latitude is scoped "When the value of
> operand-2 is greater than zero"; for a NEGATIVE operand-2 r3 fixes the result as the evaluation of
> `(1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS (operand-2)))`, which under per-operation 34-digit rounding is a different
> value from `exp(-|p| × ln b)`. `CobolDec.Pow` reciprocates at the top, over the same development at
> |operand-2|, so every arm below is r3-correct by construction. One visible consequence: an out-of-range
> negative exponent takes its EC name from r3's own expression, because the operation that leaves the range is
> the INNER power — `2 ** -600000` is EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW and `0.5 ** -600000` EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW (kb/Work PB266).
> ⚠ **What is claimed is an r2e-conforming SDIDI development, NOT 34 correct digits.** §8.8.1.5.2 rounds every
> operation to 34 digits, so a development of N operations carries the accumulated rounding of all N. MEASURED
> (an independent 34-digit emulation of the development checked against 120-digit truth, not estimated):
> **≈33 correct significant digits** for a moderate exponent — 33.00–33.58 over the six
> `CobolDecPowDevelopmentTests` rows and 30.87 as the floor over a 400-case randomized in-range sweep (the
> binary64 predecessor reached ≈17) — **degrading as ≈ 33 − log₁₀|operand-2 × ln operand-1|** once that product
> passes 1 (32.15 digits at 7.1, 31.12 at 69, 30.11 at 693, 28.78 at 13 863). THAT driver is inherent to the
> equivalent expression: an exp development turns ABSOLUTE error in its argument into RELATIVE error in its
> result.
> ⛔ **This determination previously read "≈31 … degrading as |operand-2 × ln operand-1| grows and for a base
> very near 1 — … inherent to the equivalent expression", and the near-unit half of that was NOT inherent — it
> was this coding of it** (kb/Work PB269). The three-square-root reduction carried m^(1/8) at 34 SIGNIFICANT
> digits about 1, so `Sub(u, One)` cancelled away the whole of b−1: 17.05 correct digits at the worst point of
> |m−1| ≤ ¼, and EXACTLY ZERO at m = 1 + 10⁻³³, where `(1 + 10⁻³³) ** 10³⁰` answered a flat 1 against a true
> 1.0010005. The δ arm removes it — the same three cases now measure 32.4, 29.1 and 33.2 — so the near-unit
> driver is gone rather than reduced, and only the |operand-2 × ln operand-1| one remains.
> The range dispositions PB145 established are unchanged: the out-of-decimal128 directions carry their own
> §8.8.1.5.2 r2 names (too large = EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, too small = EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW), and no SDIDI-range operand
> collapses to a silent zero or raises a spurious range error. The past-loop-bound INTEGER escape now enters the
> SAME development — it used to be a SECOND, different binary64 one, which also dropped the sign of a negative
> base raised to an odd exponent — **with the exponent OPERAND, never the loop-bound probe.** That probe clamps
> at `long.MaxValue`, and the escape used to rebuild the exponent from it, so every exponent past 2⁶³−1 was
> silently replaced by 9223372036854775807: `(1 + 10⁻³³) ** 1.0E+20` answered 1.0000000000000 where
> 1.0000000000001 is owed and `0.9999999999999999 ** 1.0E+25` answered a silent 0 where the value is below the
> decimal128 range and EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW is owed (kb/Work PB267). ⚠ The disposition is NOT "a clamped exponent
> with |base| ≠ 1 is out of range": the closest SDIDI value to one is 1 ± 10⁻³³ and `(1 + 10⁻³³) ** 10²⁰` is in
> range, so that screen would be PB145's spurious size error again. GR-8.8.1.5.4-2/-3 are CONFORMS. Pinned by `2023/pb167_sdidi_exponentiation`,
> `2023/exp_standard_decimal_eae` and `CobolDecPowDevelopmentTests`, whose drift leg fails if any binary64
> transcendental returns to `CobolDec`.
> ⚠ **Consequence under INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING IS PROHIBITED, and it is the standard's:** §11.9.11.2 rule 3 d —
> "If the PROHIBITED phrase is specified and an intermediate value cannot be represented exactly in SDIDI form,
> the EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION exception condition is set to exist and the results of the operation are undefined."
> The r2e development is a chain of inexact 34-digit operations over an irrational result, so under PROHIBITED a
> NON-INTEGER power now raises, exactly as `FUNCTION SQRT` already did for an inexact root. The binary64
> predecessor did NOT raise — it computed in IEEE double and entered the SDIDI through one conversion of the double,
> so the prohibition never saw the inexactness it exists to report. An INTEGER power still computes (r2a–r2d is
> exact multiplication). Pinned by `2023/pb167_sdidi_exponentiation_prohibited`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — §8.8.1.5.2 r2's "too small" is the round-to-zero test, and gradual underflow sets no
> exception** (2026-08-29; kb/Work PB145). A value below 10⁻⁶¹⁷⁶ re-rounds onto the 10⁻⁶¹⁷⁶ quantum under the
> INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING mode (genuine gradual underflow — reduced precision, not a flush); only a value that
> rounds to ZERO there raises EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW. A tiny-and-inexact value landing on a NONZERO quantum
> (1.5E−6176 → 2E−6176) sets nothing — r2's "too small … to be contained in an item in decimal128 format"
> reads as the round-to-zero test, and IEC 60559's tiny∧inexact underflow SIGNAL (which the "exception
> conditions … shall be the same as … decimal128 format" paragraph could be read to import) is not modelled.
> Under INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING IS PROHIBITED a below-range landing keeps the too-small name EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW —
> never §14.7.4.3 r7's inexact-transfer EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION: one physical condition, one name.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — the DELETE FILE statement's GR20/GR21 are internally contradictory in the printed
> standard (§14.9.10.4)** (2026-08-29; kb/Work PB141). Both general rules open "If the execution of the DELETE
> FILE statement is successful" (verified against the PDF text layer, page 638 — not a transcription error),
> yet GR20 c) transfers control to the ON EXCEPTION phrase while GR21 b) says "The ON EXCEPTION phrase is
> ignored" — two contradictory outcomes for one successful execution. GR20's CONTENT is plainly the
> UNSUCCESSFUL-execution rule: its d) invokes §9.1.12 "Input-output exception processing" (the unsuccessful-I-O
> machinery), it is the only home for the unsuccessful case (the GR list ends at GR21), and the twin Format-1
> rules pair success/failure the same way. WiseOwl COBOL reads GR20 as governing an UNSUCCESSFUL execution (a
> non-'0x' status: EC per §9.1.13.1 set when enabled, then ON EXCEPTION as the handler, else exception
> processing) and GR21 as the successful case (NOT ON EXCEPTION; ON EXCEPTION ignored) — the reading every
> surveyed implementation takes. Pinned by `2023/pb141_delete_file_ec` and `2023/pb140_delete_file_gate`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — the §14.9.51.4 GR26 a)/b) boundary at LINAGE-COUNTER = page size** (2026-09-05; kb/Work
> PB686). GR26's two arms cannot both be honoured at that one counter value. Arm a) fires when the counter "is
> equal to or exceeds the page size"; arm b) is clamped to "equal to or exceeds the current value of the footing
> start **and is less than the page size**". Both were verified against the PDF text layer (printed page 792) —
> **this is the standard's own text, not a transcription defect.** Read literally, a WRITE landing the counter
> exactly ON the page size is arm a): page overflow, the record pushed to the first line of the next logical page,
> the counter reset to one. **WiseOwl COBOL rejects that reading.** Both arms are evaluated on the counter the write's
> advancing operation produces, and the boundary is STRICT: `counter > page size` is arm a); `footing start ≤
> counter ≤ page size` is arm b). Three other rules force it. §13.18.34.4 GR2 — the page size is "the number of
> lines that may be written or spaced on the logical page" — and under the literal reading the line NUMBERED page
> size can never receive a record from an AFTER-advancing write, so an N-line body would hold at most N−1 written
> lines on every page, forever; that is also true of a file with NO FOOTING phrase, which is the arm a
> FOOTING-only fixture cannot see. §13.18.34.4 GR3 puts that same line INSIDE the footing area ("between the
> footing start and the page size, **inclusive**"), which arm b)'s clamp then excludes. And GR26's own lead
> sentence conditions the whole rule on lines that "do not fit within the current page body" — a line landing on
> the last body line fits. §13.18.34.4 GR7 c) 1 corroborates the strict boundary from the other side: the
> standard's way of making arm a) fire for ADVANCING PAGE is to say the counter "is implicitly incremented to
> **exceed** the value specified by integer-1" — equality would have sufficed had equality been the trigger.
> **The survey does not split** (the 2026-08-30 standing answer): IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.3 states the
> footing END-OF-PAGE as the counter reaching a value that "equal[s] or exceed[s] the value specified in the WITH
> FOOTING phrase" with **no upper clamp**, and page overflow as a write that "would cause the value in the
> LINAGE-COUNTER to **exceed** the number of lines for the page body"; Micro Focus Visual COBOL documents the
> footing area as "the area between footing-line and page-lines, **inclusive**"; and GnuCOBOL passes the NIST
> CCVS-85 suite, whose SQ201M is decisive on its own — `LINAGE IS 50 LINES WITH FOOTING AT 45` with the canonical
> golden printing **six** footing lines reading LINAGE-COUNTER 45, 46, 47, 48, 49 and **50**. Under the literal
> reading the fifth of those writes would overflow and reset the counter, and the sixth would report 1 against a
> required 50. That golden is `tests/nist/valid/SQ201M.txt` and it is green in this tree. Pinned by
> `2023/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary` and its `85/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary_85` edition twin (the discriminating
> lines are `F3 EOP / LC=004` and `N3 NO-EOP / LC=004`), and by
> `LinageConformanceTests.Gr26ab_CounterEqualsBody_IsFootingEopNotOverflow`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — WRITE ADVANCING PAGE on a logical page is a page overflow** (2026-10-16; kb/Work PB578). The
> standard's text decides it, so CLAUDE.md rule 1's precedence never reaches the implementations. §13.18.34.4 GR7 c) 1
> resets the counter to one and says how: "During the resetting of LINAGE-COUNTER to the value one, the value of
> LINAGE-COUNTER is implicitly incremented to exceed the value specified by integer-1 or the data item referenced by
> data-name-1." A counter past the page size is §14.9.51.4 GR26 a)'s trigger ("This occurs when the associated
> LINAGE-COUNTER is equal to or exceeds the page size"), and GR27 a) names the condition it causes: "If the
> end-of-page condition was caused by the action in General rule 26a, the EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW exception condition is
> set to exist." So a WRITE with ADVANCING PAGE on a file whose logical page is established is SUCCESSFUL, takes the
> one overflow transition (GR25 g)'s destination is GR26 a)'s, "the first line that may be written on the next
> logical page"), leaves the counter at one, sets EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW to exist (an applicable USE declarative, an
> exception-checking PERFORM's WHEN phrase and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS see it, GR27 c)/d)), and does not run a
> NOT END-OF-PAGE imperative (GR28: only "the end-of-page condition does not occur"). The PB686 determination
> above reads GR7 c) 1 the same way, as "the standard's own device for making arm a) fire on ADVANCING PAGE".
> **SR18 bars only the END-OF-PAGE phrase beside ADVANCING PAGE.** "The phrases ADVANCING PAGE and END-OF-PAGE shall
> not both be specified in a single WRITE statement" names GR27 b)'s imperative-statement-1 phrase; SR19 ("If the
> END-OF-PAGE or the NOT END-OF-PAGE phrase is specified") and GR28 name the NOT END-OF-PAGE phrase separately, so a
> NOT-only phrase beside ADVANCING PAGE is legal source (its imperative never runs) and the AT phrase is refused
> whichever phrase is written first (COBOL0861). **The surveyed implementation does not split this from the
> text:** GnuCOBOL 3.2 accepts the NOT-only form and runs its imperative after ADVANCING PAGE, but it also runs a NOT
> END-OF-PAGE imperative after an `ADVANCING 9 LINES` write that overflows a 5-line page with no FOOTING phrase, a
> case no reading of GR26 a) allows, so its end-of-page signal is not a witness here (probe 2026-10-16). **What a
> declarative reads mid-statement:** when GR6 b) 2's re-evaluation during the ADVANCING PAGE write violates GR6 b)'s
> value rules, the write is unsuccessful (no end-of-page condition) and the USE procedure, run "after completion of
> the standard input-output exception routine" (§14.9.49.4 GR6), reads GR6 b) 2's counter value 0, never the
> transient value GR7 c) 1 passes through; the overflow arm's twin is pinned by `2023/pb526_linage_ec_condition`.
> Pinned by `85/pb578_advancing_page_overflow_85`, `2002/pb578_advancing_page_eop_overflow`, the negative
> `pb578-write-advancing-page-at-and-not-eop`, and `LinageConformanceTests.Sr18_AdvancingPageWithNotEopOnly_IsLegalAndTheEndOfPageConditionOccurs`
> / `Sr18_AdvancingPageWithNotFirstEopPair_IsRejected`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — ADVANCING 0 is an overprint, represented by a bare carriage return** (2026-09-30; owner
> decision kb/Work R54; kb/Work PB1667). §14.9.51.4 GR25 c): "If integer-1 or the value of the data item referenced
> by identifier-2 is zero, no repositioning of the representation of the printed page is performed." The NEXT line is
> therefore presented at the SAME vertical position as the line the device stands on — an overprint, never a
> continuation of that line's text. The standard leaves the device REPRESENTATION to the implementor, so CLAUDE.md
> rule 1's precedence decides (ISO -> GnuCOBOL -> IBM/MF), and GnuCOBOL 3.2 (`libcob/fileio.c`,
> `cob_seq_write_opt` / `cob_file_write_opt`) writes a **bare carriage return (CR, no line feed)** for AFTER/BEFORE
> ADVANCING 0. WiseOwl COBOL does the same, at the advance's own placement: AFTER writes the return and then the
> record; BEFORE writes the record and then the return (`SequentialConnector.WriteTravel`, reached by the one
> non-LINAGE travel and the one logical-page travel, so a file with a LINAGE clause counts the zero — the counter
> stays — and writes the return too). **Two points are the implementor's and are fixed here.** (1) The return is
> written only while a line IS open — the device stands on a line a presentation wrote and no travel has ended
> (`SequentialConnector.DeviceOnOpenLine`). With none open the device is already at the start of a line, there is
> nothing to overprint and nothing is written (GnuCOBOL writes the return there too; it is a no-op on a line
> start, and the report writer's zero advance on an empty page depends on it being nothing). (2) The return is a
> line CONTROL and not a line end, so it is the same byte on every file shape; the line END of the shape it
> overprints is A.1 item 146 (c′)'s three-way mapping (a record sequential print file without LINAGE: LF, so a
> return followed by the next line's LF reads as a CR LF pair; a LINE SEQUENTIAL file, a LINAGE file and a
> report file: the host newline). **The report writer's line state follows from the same representation.** A report file that stays open
> after a TERMINATE (§14.9.46.4 GR6) stands on that run's last line, and INITIATE (§14.9.21.4 GR1 b) resets the
> report's page model, not the device: the first line of the next run belongs on the line BELOW that one, because
> the only overlap a report may print is a relative line of integer-2 zero inside a report group (§13.18.35.4 GR3),
> and a zero advance is an overprint. `CobolReport.PresentLine` therefore treats its empty page as "the device is at
> page line 1" only while `CobolFile.DeviceOnOpenLine` is false; with the device on an open line it stands at line 0
> and the first line travels to its own number. Pinned by `2023/pb1667_advancing_zero_overprint` and
> `2002/pb1667_reinitiate_open_report_file`.
>
> **A line presented onto an open line is the same overprint (kb/Work PB1840).** §14.9.51.4 GR25 e): a BEFORE
> write's "line is presented before the representation of the printed page is advanced", and GR25 f): an AFTER write's
> line is presented after its advance. So when an earlier write left its line open (an AFTER write's record, a plain
> WRITE's - an AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE - or a BEFORE ADVANCING 0's), no advance lies between the two lines and the new
> one is at the SAME vertical position as the open one, which is GR25 c)'s zero advance by another route. The
> standard states the position and does not leave it to the implementor, so ISO controls and GnuCOBOL does not:
> GnuCOBOL appends the BEFORE record to the open line's text (`AB`), a continuation the standard's "same vertical
> position" does not describe, and WiseOwl COBOL does not follow it. The device representation is the one above: a
> bare carriage return, written by the ONE presentation (`SequentialConnector.Present`) before the record's
> characters, so every arm that presents gets it by construction - a BEFORE write of any amount (a positive count, 0,
> or PAGE: GR25 g) and h) change the advance and not the place the line is presented), on a file with or without a
> LINAGE clause, record sequential or line sequential. Three points are fixed here. (1) The return is written only
> while a line is open AND the device is not already at its start: after a zero advance's own return
> (`SequentialConnector.DeviceLine.Returned`) the next presentation writes none, so AFTER 1 "A", BEFORE 0 "B",
> BEFORE 1 "C" is `A` CR `B` CR `C` and never two returns in a row. (2) A record with no characters to print (a line
> of spaces, the report writer's page-feed carrier) overprints nothing and writes no return; a blank line presented
> with no line open is itself an open line, with the device at its START (`DeviceLine.Returned`), so the record
> presented onto it next, or an AFTER 0, finds nothing to return over and writes none (a stray return there would
> become data of the next record on a line sequential file, kb/Work PB1540). (3) A WRITE that is
> refused - '44' outside the RECORD IS VARYING bounds, '71' for a character outside the line sequential character
> set, '91', a lock refusal - presents nothing, so it neither writes the return nor closes the open line; a BEFORE
> write whose page transition then fails (§13.18.34.4 GR6 b) 2) HAS presented, so its overprint stands. Pinned by
> `14.9.51-WRITE/pb1840_before_after_open_line` (all four editions) and `OpenLineOverprintTests`, which covers the
> refusals (with a declarative, with a FILE STATUS item, with both, with neither: the run ends at the refused
> write), the blank lines and the end-of-page conditions of a write that overprints.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — a WRITE without the ADVANCING phrase is an explicit `AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE` in every state
> of the device, and a file supports vertical positioning when its description carries a LINAGE clause or once an
> ADVANCING phrase has been written to it** (2026-10-07; kb/Work PB1027, adjudicated in wave 1033, implemented in
> wave 1037). §14.9.51.4 GR25: "If the ADVANCING phrase is not used, automatic advancing shall be provided by the
> implementor to act as if the user has specified AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE" (`cite.py --check 14.9.51.4` OK, 25). The
> standard names no implementor choice of PLACEMENT, so the two spellings are ONE path (`SequentialConnector.WriteRecord`
> reroutes the omitted phrase to `WriteAdvancingRecord(lines: 1, before: false)`), whatever the device holds: after a
> BEFORE write, whose own advance already ended the line, a plain WRITE advances AGAIN (one empty line, as AFTER
> does); on a LINAGE page the first plain WRITE after OPEN presents on body line 2 (§13.18.34.4 GR7 d) puts the
> counter at 1, and the AFTER advance makes it 2, GR7 c) 3), and an overflowing plain WRITE presents ON line 1 of the
> next page (GR26 a) with the AFTER phrase implied); a line sequential file no longer travels twice around an AFTER
> write. Before PB1027 the omitted phrase took BEFORE's placement whenever no line was open, so each of those was one
> line off the file the spelled-out phrase writes. Pinned by `PlainWriteAdvancingConformanceTests` (every
> three-write mix of plain, AFTER and BEFORE over record sequential and line sequential files, with and without
> LINAGE, written both ways and compared byte for byte) and by `85/pb1027_plain_write_is_after_advancing_85` and
> `2023/pb1027_plain_write_is_after_advancing`.
> **The latitude, and where this determination departs from the wave-1033 adjudication.** GR25's own first
> sentences — "If the physical file does not support vertical positioning, the ADVANCING and END-OF-PAGE phrases are
> ignored" — leave to the implementor which physical files support it (Annex A.3 item 37 is claimed in §2, but the
> claim is that the PHRASES work; a text file on disk that no program ever asked to position is not a device that
> has a page). WiseOwl COBOL's determination: a file supports vertical positioning when (a) its description has a
> LINAGE clause (positioned from OPEN: GR7 d), or (b) a WRITE to it has carried an ADVANCING phrase since the OPEN
> (`SequentialConnector.SupportsVerticalPositioning`; a report file reaches the medium only through such a WRITE).
> A file for which neither holds — an ordinary text file or fixed-block data file written with plain WRITEs only —
> has nothing to position, so its plain WRITE is the record and its own line end (a line sequential delimiter, or
> nothing for a record sequential block): NO leading empty line, the shape GnuCOBOL 3.2 writes by default. The
> wave-1033 decision read every sequential file as positioned and would have given such a file a leading empty line,
> citing GnuCOBOL's `-fwrite-after`; that flag is NOT the default (default `cobc` writes `AAAAA` LF `BBBBB` LF for two
> plain WRITEs and treats a plain WRITE as a BEFORE write on every file), so the precedence ISO, then GnuCOBOL does
> not select it, and the operator's caveat of 2026-10-07 asked for the default probe before any output moved. No
> output of a plain-only file changes. **Two consequences stated openly:** a plain WRITE that PRECEDES the first
> ADVANCING write of a non-LINAGE file was written before the file was known to be positioned and is a complete line
> (a plain `A` followed by `AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE` `B` is `A` LF LF `B` LF, where a file positioned from OPEN would
> be LF `A` LF `B` LF: the same number of empty lines, one position apart); and the capability is read at run time,
> so an EXTERNAL file shared by programs inherits it from whichever wrote an ADVANCING phrase first. Whether the
> capability should instead be a compile-time property of the file (any ADVANCING write in the compilation unit) is
> an owner question recorded with the PB1027 note, not decided here.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — an unchecked out-of-range reference modification ends the run unit** (2026-09-30; owner
> decision kb/Work R60; kb/Work PB1707). §8.4.3.3.4 5) b)/c) (cite-checked) make the position ranges a `shall`
> — leftmost-position a position of the item, and "The sum of leftmost-position and length minus the value one shall
> be less than or equal to the number of positions in the data item referenced by identifier-1" — and a violation is
> the fatal EC-BOUND-REF-MOD (Table 13). With checking enabled the condition is raised (USE declarative, else the
> run unit ends, §14.6.13.1.3 5)/7)). With checking NOT enabled the standard names no outcome for the violated
> `shall`, so the owner's standing rule of 2026-07-28 decides — lenient wherever the standard names the outcome,
> LOUD ABORT wherever it names none — and WiseOwl COBOL **terminates the run unit with a runtime error**
> ("abnormal run-unit termination: EC-BOUND-REF-MOD (fatal): reference modification (1:10) out of range for a
> 5-position item", exit 1): it never clamps the slice or pads it with spaces, because a reference modification that
> addresses positions no item owns has no result to return (GnuCOBOL, IBM and Micro Focus addressed the storage that
> follows the item, for which there is no memory-safe behaviour to follow; before this determination the read
> padded with spaces and the write clamped, so `DISPLAY CX(1:77777777777)` ended with "Out of memory."). The test is
> ONE predicate for the read and the write (`CobolString.RefModOutOfRange`, through `CobolString.RefMod` and
> `CobolString.SpliceInto`), it also covers a non-integer position (§8.4.3.3.4 5) c), which is the same
> violation), and a LITERAL violation against a fixed-size item is refused at compile time before it can run (A.1 item 69).
> Slices the COMPILER chooses — a REDEFINES view, an occurs-depending group's current extent, an INVOKE/CALL
> boundary prefix, the current record of a READ … INTO — are not reference modifications the program wrote, go through
> `CobolString.Window` / `WindowInto` (`RuntimeApi.StrWindow` / `StrWindowInto`), and keep their lenient
> space-extending semantics; `RuntimeApiWindowDriftTests` keeps the two lists apart. Pinned by
> `RefModUncheckedTerminationTests`, `negative:pb1707-refmod-literal-out-of-range`, and the checked arm by
> `2023/l1_fatal_ec_runtime_detection`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — a RETURNING result whose description does not conform, with EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH checking
> off in either element** (2026-10-02; kb/Work PB1040). §14.8.3.3 (cite-checked) gives a conforming RETURNING receiver
> "the same ALIGN, BLANK WHEN ZERO, DYNAMIC LENGTH, JUSTIFIED, PICTURE, SIGN, and USAGE clauses" as the sender, and
> §14.9.4.4 GR3 d) makes a violation EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH "if checking for it is enabled in both the activated
> program and activating runtime element", the call "not successful" (the callee never runs; GR3 h) 1. sends it to
> ON EXCEPTION). Checked in both, WiseOwl COBOL raises it at call initiation: at a CALL whose activated program the
> activating element holds no signature for, over both returning items' whole descriptions (§14.8.3 entire,
> `BoundaryItem.ReturningViolation`; kb/Work PB165), elsewhere over the numeric item's PICTURE, SIGN and USAGE and a
> text-carried item's character length. The standard names no outcome when checking is off in either element, and WiseOwl COBOL
> follows the posture it already documents for the unchecked argument COUNT (`ProgramTable.CallProgram`: a missing
> argument behaves as omitted, an excess one is ignored): the call proceeds and the result is stored in the
> RECEIVER'S OWN width — a text receiver by the alphanumeric alignment of §14.6.8.5 ("aligned at the leftmost
> character position in the data item with space fill or truncation to the right"), a numeric receiver as the value
> the sender held under the receiver's own PICTURE and USAGE — so an item's image never changes width (before this
> determination a 3-character result left a PIC X(5) item displaying `[ABC]` with FUNCTION LENGTH 5). This is
> implementor latitude settled by the project's own existing posture for the same rule, not by a survey of other
> compilers. Pinned by `2002/pb1040_returning_length_conformance`. **The same gate and the same unchecked posture govern an
> ARGUMENT's description on the dynamic Format-1 lane** (kb/Work PB165): checked in both elements, a formal of a different

> proceeds and the formal's window fits the argument as it always did. Pinned by `2002/pb165_dynamic_call_description_check`.

> PB957). **(1) When WITH RESET resets PAGE-COUNTER.** §8.4.3.15.4 GR2 says PAGE-COUNTER "is reset to 1 when a

> "immediately after the page feed caused by the next page advance, chronologically between the printing of any page
> footing and the printing of any page heading", and §14.9.16.4 GR6 d) makes it the PAGE-COUNTER step of that page
> advance. WiseOwl COBOL follows GR6 and §14.9.16.4: the clause ARMS the reset and the next page advance performs it, so
> the page footing still prints the old page number. **(2) A relative body-group NEXT GROUP in a report that is not
> divided into pages.** §13.18.37.4 GR4 b) compares against "the FOOTING integer", and such a report has no FOOTING.
> WiseOwl COBOL adds integer-2 to LINE-COUNTER; it does not clamp to a FOOTING of 0. **(3) "no effect at all if a
> TERMINATE is next executed" (GR4 a)).** WiseOwl COBOL's TERMINATE discards the save location and restores
> LINE-COUNTER to the group's last line. Leaving LINE-COUNTER at FOOTING would force a page advance before the
> control footings print, and that is an effect. Pinned by `85/pb957_next_group_forms` and
> `85/pb957_next_group_control`. The mechanism is in `docs/REPORT_WRITER_DESIGN.md` (the NEXT GROUP row).

> as a relative clause (GR4c's "relative … without the NEXT PAGE phrase" names the combination) whose integer-2 is
> never read where the phrase applies. A body group advances (GR4a) and is then the first body group on its page,
> so it begins at the FIRST DETAIL integer (GR5b3). A report footing is on a page by itself, so it begins at that
> footing's upper limit, the HEADING integer (§13.18.57.4 GR7f). A later occurrence of a REPEATED bare clause
> advances one line. **(2) The bare operand in a report that is not divided into pages.** §13.18.35.3 SR5 requires

> integer-2`, so the bare operand is refused there (COBOL2199). This is the reading §13.18.37.3 SR3 gives NEXT
> GROUP ("only the relative form of the clause may be specified"), and a report of one page of indefinite length
> (§13.18.39.4 GR2a) has no next page to begin. **(3) GR4a 2 of the NEXT GROUP clause.** §13.18.37.4 GR4a 2 says
> that a next body group opening with an absolute LINE … NEXT PAGE takes "a page advance". WiseOwl COBOL takes the ONE
> advance the save location already forces, then proceeds as GR4a 1 does. Where §13.18.37.4 means a second advance
> it says so (GR4a 3: "a second page advance takes place, resulting in a page devoid of body groups"). A second
> advance here would leave a page with no report group on it. GnuCOBOL 3.2 parses the phrase but gives it no

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — the compile-time screens of the report layout rules refuse what no presentation can excuse
> (§13.18.14.3 SR7/SR8, §13.18.35.3 SR6, §13.18.57.4 GR7/GR8)** (2026-10-04; kb/Work PB1222, PB1270). Several of these
> rules are stated over a condition only the run can settle, and the standard leaves how a compiler judges them to
> the implementor. WiseOwl COBOL screens a rule only where **every presentation of the program breaks it**, and leaves
> the remainder to the run-time condition the standard pairs with it (EC-REPORT-COLUMN-OVERLAP §13.18.14.4 GR4,
> EC-REPORT-PAGE-WIDTH GR5, EC-REPORT-LINE-OVERLAP §13.18.35.4 GR3, EC-REPORT-PAGE-LIMIT GR2). (1) **"Each subject to a
> different PRESENT WHEN clause"** (SR7, SR8 a), SR6 a)–e)) means each of the two items carries a clause the other does
> not — the entry's own or an enclosing entry's, or a GROUP INDICATE clause, which has "the same effect as a PRESENT
> WHEN clause" (§13.18.28.4 GR1). The standard does not require the clauses to exclude each other, and the
> conditions of two different clauses may both hold: that is how a conforming program reaches the run-time
> conditions above (`2002/pb1059_page_columns_width`, `2002/pb1188_report_nonfatal_raise`). (2) **The limits of a
> report group (GR7, GR8) that depend on the run** — whether a report heading shares its page with a page heading, whether
> a report heading or footing stands on a page by itself, how far the OR PAGE control headings reach — are taken at the
> WIDEST region they allow: a report heading, page heading and report footing at the HEADING integer and a body group at
> FIRST DETAIL for the upper limit; a report heading, page footing and report footing at the page limit for the lower.
> The limits that do not depend on the run are exact: a page heading's lower limit FIRST DETAIL − 1, a control heading's
> LAST CONTROL HEADING, a detail's LAST DETAIL, a control footing's FOOTING, a page footing's upper limit FOOTING + 1.
> (3) **SR8 c) and SR6 d)** ("shall not cause the page width / the lower limit to be exceeded unless each of them is
> subject to a different PRESENT WHEN clause, in which case this rule applies only to the largest of them") are read
> literally over the tail of the line or group — the relative items after the last absolute one. The tail is judged as
> a whole, every item present, unless EACH item of it carries a clause every other lacks; then only the largest is
> judged, the one that ends furthest right (or lowest) when it alone of the tail is present, after everything before the
> tail. An item subject to no clause excuses nothing. SR6 d) is asked of a group whose last absolute line is
> unconditional, as its text says ("one or more absolute lines, not subject to any PRESENT WHEN clause"). (4) **The default FIRST DETAIL** (§13.18.39.4 GR3 b: the HEADING integer, 1 when HEADING is
> omitted) is the integer the page heading's lower limit and the body groups' upper limit read, so `PAGE LIMIT 10 LINES`
> with `TYPE PH LINE 1` is refused: the page heading must terminate before FIRST DETAIL (GR2 d), and with the default
> there is no line before it. (5) **The FIRST line of a relative heading or footing, and the reach of a relative page or
> report footing** (§13.18.39.4 GR2 a), c), g); kb/Work PB1270): where §13.18.35.4 GR5 b puts a relative first line is a
> number the description fixes (HEADING + integer-2 − 1 for a report heading and a page heading with no report heading
> before it; FOOTING + integer-2 for a page footing and a report footing with no page footing before it; the previous
> line plus integer-2 otherwise, which only moves it LOWER), so a first line that GR5 b prints above the HEADING integer
> or not after the FOOTING integer — in practice a `LINE PLUS 0` — and a relative page or report footing whose last line
> is past the page limit are refused: they leave the region on every page. A report footing whose first LINE clause is
> the bare `ON NEXT PAGE` is on a page by itself and starts at the HEADING integer (GR7 f), as the run-time engine
> places it. Pinned by `negative/pb1270-*-relative-*`, `85/pb1270_report_relative_first_boundaries`,
> `negative/pb1222-*`, `negative/pb1270-*`, `85/pb1270_report_page_region_boundaries`
> and `2002/pb1222_report_arrangement_present_when`. The mechanism is in `docs/REPORT_WRITER_DESIGN.md` (the
> ARRANGEMENT rules bullet).

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — a SUM entry's category is judged against the INTEGER numeric row of Table 16 (§13.18.54.3 SR2)**
> (2026-10-04; kb/Work PB1295). SR2 requires "the category of the subject of the entry" to be "valid as the category of a
> receiving operand in a MOVE statement for a sending operand of the category numeric", and Table 16 (§14.9.25.3 SR10)
> splits the numeric sender into an Integer and a Noninteger row. The category of the entry's PICTURE does not say
> whether the sum has a decimal point, so the screen refuses only what the INTEGER row refuses — a numeric operand does
> not move to an alphabetic or a boolean item — and admits the alphanumeric and national categories the integer row
> allows; the noninteger row only adds "No" cells, and a compiler that rejected the alphanumeric entry would refuse a
> program some sums fill legally. Neither ISO nor GnuCOBOL (which checks no such category) offers a narrower reading.
> Pinned by `negative/pb1295-sum-entry-*`. In the same change §8.4.2.3.3 SR8 ("neither a sum counter nor the LINE-COUNTER
> and PAGE-COUNTER identifiers may be used as a subscript") is screened once per written entry over every clause that
> carries a subscript (COBOL2751), and a report section item that is neither is the clause's own rule
> (§13.18.54.3 SR6, §13.18.53.3 SR4); a PRESENT WHEN condition is §13.15.3 SR16's. Pinned by `negative/pb1474-*` and
> `85/pb1474_report_subscripts_legal`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — a sequential READ whose I-O status is '46' takes neither the AT END nor the NOT AT END
> phrase (§14.9.30.4 GR21 → GR24)** (2026-09-22; kb/Work PB810). GR21 sets '46' when "the previous READ or START
> statement for the file connector was unsuccessful" and says execution "proceeds as indicated in General rule 24".
> Read as "all of GR24", the pointer would run the AT END imperative and also overwrite GR21's own '46' with GR24
> a)'s '10'. **WiseOwl COBOL does not read it that way.** GR24's actions are conditioned on its own first words — "If,
> during the execution of the READ statement, the at end condition exists" — and '46' is not the at end condition:
> §9.1.13.7 6) makes it a LOGIC ERROR, which §9.1.13.1 defines as an unsuccessful execution "as a result of an
> improper sequence of input-output operations", while the at end condition is §9.1.13.4's '10'/'14'. So the rule
> that governs is GR13 — "If neither an at end nor an invalid key condition occurs during the execution of a READ
> statement, the AT END phrase or the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored" — and GR13 b) transfers control through
> §9.1.12's input-output exception processing (a USE declarative, then the end of the READ). GnuCOBOL and IBM
> Enterprise COBOL take the AT END phrase for the at end condition only. The status→condition table is written
> once, in `CodeGen/Verbs/IoStatusClass.cs` (guarded by `IoStatusClassDriftTests`), and the determination is
> pinned on all three organizations — both emitter arms — by `85/pb810_read_46_takes_no_at_end`.

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION`'s third part, "an implementor-defined identifier of the source
> line that contains the beginning of the statement" (§15.30.3 r2b3 / §15.31.3 r2b3)** (2026-08-18; kb/Work PB63,
> RV-15.31.3-2 r2b3; revised 2026-08-18 by kb/Work PB82). **The identifier is the line number of the statement's
> first token in the source file that PHYSICALLY holds it, counted from 1** — the line the user edits, recovered
> through the preprocessing chain's origin map (§7.2 text manipulation changes the resultant line count: COPY
> incorporates lines, REPLACE statements vanish, fixed-form continuations join). For a statement in the main source
> file the identifier is the bare number (`PB63LOC; IN-PARA OF ONLY-SECT; 42`); for a statement inside
> COPY-incorporated library text it is the copybook's file name (no directory) followed by the line in parentheses
> (`PB82LOC; ; pb82loc_proc.cpy(2)`), the same `file(line)` shape the compiler's own diagnostics print. The
> clause's NOTE disclaims stability across compilations; WiseOwl COBOL's value is stable for one compiler version and
> one set of source files. Pinned by `2023/pb63_exception_location_procedure_field` (no COPY) and
> `2023/pb82_exception_location_source_line` (a COPY, a REPLACE and a continuation before each RAISE; a RAISE
> inside a procedure copybook).

> ⚖ **DETERMINATION — a level-66 RENAMES THRU alias whose data-name-2 / data-name-3 is (or lies under) a
> REDEFINES entry (§13.18.45.4 GR2)** (2026-08-18; kb/Work PB96). GR2 says the alias "defines an alphanumeric group
> item that includes all elementary items starting with data-name-2 … and concluding with data-name-3"; a
> redefinition adds no storage (§13.18.44), so the elementary items named can overlap. WiseOwl COBOL's alias is the
> record's STORAGE WINDOW from the leftmost character position of data-name-2 to the rightmost character position
> of data-name-3 — a REDEFINES view inside the range contributes nothing beyond the storage it overlays, a
> data-name-2 / data-name-3 that is itself a redefinition maps to the area it overlays, and when data-name-3 is a
> SHORTER redefinition of a LATER item (its end still follows data-name-2's end) the alias ends at data-name-3's last
> character, a partial view of the underlying leaf. A data-name-3 that is a shorter redefinition of an EARLIER item —
> `RENAMES A THRU B`, B redefining A's first two characters — is not legal source: §13.18.45.3 SR11 says "the end of the
> storage area described by data-name-3 shall follow the end of the storage area described by data-name-2" (`cite.py
> --check` OK 11)), and the offset arithmetic GnuCOBOL and IBM apply there is a vendor leniency the standard's syntax
> rule controls over (kb/Work PB1283; `negative/pb1283-renames-thru-redefinition`). Pinned by
> `2023/pb96_renames_span_over_redefines`.

## 5. Annex A.4 optional-element disposition (§4.2.7)

One row per A.4 optional module. **Claimed** = support is claimed (§4.2.7/A.4.1); **Partial** = the supported /
not-supported split is itemized (the §4.2.7 second-sentence requirement); **Not claimed** = the module's syntax
is not accepted (per A.4.1, optional-element syntax is accepted only when support is claimed — so a parse error
or a named error is the conforming posture). This section is the user-documentation face; §1's conformance
summary claims only what is Claimed/Partial here. A row's `derived-verdicts.<selector>` names the inventory rows the
decline covers; the selector in `tests/version-matrix/inventory-schema.json` IS that set, so this table carries no
row counts (they drifted from the selectors three times); `python scripts/spec/derive_verdict_batch.py --list` prints
each selector's live count.

| A.4 § | Module | Disposition | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| A.4.2 | ACCEPT/DISPLAY screen handling | Not claimed | The SCREEN facility (§4 item 4). **REFUSED BY NAME, uniformly, since 2026-09-02 (kb/Work PB260)** — the row used to record a measured NON-uniform accept-and-warn posture, and the measurement that produced it is what refuted it. Annex A.4.1 admits an optional element's syntax "only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor", so an unclaimed module is not accepted at all: all SEVEN source shapes now draw a named **Error** through the single funnel `src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/ScreenFacility.cs` — **COBOL1560** for the SCREEN SECTION header (§13.9), every screen description entry clause (§13.17 / §13.18.x, one message per clause KIND naming the clause and its ISO §), the SPECIAL-NAMES `CURSOR` / `CRT STATUS` clauses (§12.3.7) and the OPTIONS `INITIALIZE … SCREEN` target (§11.9.10.4 GR3 — the seventh shape, which parsed into a flag nothing read; GR1's `ALL` stays legal), and **COBOL1707** for ACCEPT format 3 (§14.9.1), DISPLAY format 2 (§14.9.11) and SET format 6 ATTRIBUTE (§14.9.39 — whose printed format has no `TO`) plus every EC-SCREEN exception-name in the six item-10 positions. Two codes, split at the DIVISION boundary, because a statement witness must declare a SCREEN SECTION to have a screen-name and would otherwise pass on the section's diagnostic. Declining the module costs the user none of its WORDS: the fifteen §8.10 screen words are reserved at no edition and the seven §8.9 ones only where §8.9 says (all but `COLUMN` from 2002), so all 22 are legal user words exactly where the standard leaves them so — and the population is DERIVED from `CobolScreen.g4` plus the two SPECIAL-NAMES screen clauses, so the next screen token added without a `cobol-words.json` `nameSlot` row fails a gate (kb/Work PB301). Witnesses: 43 negative-corpus programs `conformance-suite/wiseowl/cases/*/a42-*` (each `wiseowl/diagnostics/<id>.json` file carrying the code AND the named construct; `a42-accept-screen-exception` and `a42-display-screen-exception` are the unpositioned exception-phrase spellings, kb/Work PB1528) plus `ScreenFacilityConstructDriftTests`, which reads `CobolScreen.g4` and fails when a `screenClause` alternative has no row. Every rule the facility conditions carries this row's determination through `inventory-schema.json` `derived-verdicts.screen-handling-only` (ten of its rows are the Annex A.1 items 3, 4, 11, 27, 41, 45, 83, 91, 172 and 199, withdrawn by owner decision R42 through the selector's Annex A.1 arms) |
| A.4.3 | Commit and rollback | **Claimed** | §4 item 2. **Scope of the claim:** complete for SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL files and the print stream, and for RELATIVE and INDEXED files: an OPEN OUTPUT that replaces a RELATIVE or INDEXED file, a DELETE FILE that removes one and an OPEN that creates one are journaled in the same transaction journal (the keyed CAPTURE of DESIGN-runtime-library.md 2.2.2.14, kb/Work PB3492), so a ROLLBACK restores such a file as at the last COMMIT (§14.9.36.4 GR3; the NOTE under §14.9.10.4 GR15) and a DELETE FILE after a CLOSE under commit control proceeds. **Provided for RELATIVE and INDEXED files** (kb/Work PB3337, the keyed store engine's transaction; kb/Work PB3338, the compiler's half): the I-O-CONTROL APPLY COMMIT clause (§12.4.6.3; its syntax rules refused by name, COBOL4709), COMMIT (§14.9.7) and ROLLBACK (§14.9.36) over every active clause of the run unit, the commit of a normal run unit termination and the file-only rollback of an abnormal one (§9.1.18.5), §14.6.13.1.3 item 8's unconditional ROLLBACK after a fatal I-O condition on a file under commit control, and the EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT / EC-FLOW-COMMIT / EC-FLOW-ROLLBACK conditions. **Provided for SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL files and the print stream too** (kb/Work PB3340; DESIGN-runtime-library.md 2.2.2 — the explicit decision for LINE SEQUENTIAL is that it is COVERED with the same journal: its two changes, an append and a same-span overwrite, are the two the journal undoes, 2.2.2.10). **Determinations.** (a) What the program is told: COMMIT and ROLLBACK have no I-O status (§9.1.13.1 sets it only for CLOSE, DELETE, OPEN, READ, REWRITE, START, UNLOCK and WRITE), so a COMMIT or ROLLBACK the medium refuses raises the fatal EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR for the refused file, with '30' in that file's FILE STATUS item and the file in permanent error until its CLOSE, and with checking off item 8's ROLLBACK follows. A refused file of another element's clause, which the executing element does not describe, raises the condition there under the checking of a directive that names no file or, for a containing element's GLOBAL file the element can name, names that file (§7.3.25.4 GR6, GR8: checking is enabled "only for exception conditions associated with that file-name"), and otherwise the run unit continues exactly when an element gives the file a FILE STATUS item (A.1 item 103). The executing element's format 1 USE procedures apply to another element's refused file as they do to any input-output statement's file, with or without checking (§14.9.49.4 GR4, GR6 a)-e)): the file-name tier when the element names the file (a containing element's GLOBAL file) and the open-mode tier by the file's open mode. The run unit then continues when a declarative ran or an element gives the file a FILE STATUS item (kb/Work PB3554). (b) Files are committed one at a time in the order of the run unit's open files (a keyed file's store when it became the run unit's, a sequential file's transaction when it began): a COMMIT refused at file i leaves the files before i committed and the files from i on at the previous COMMIT (cross-file atomicity is per file, owner decision kb/Work PB3454). (c) COMMIT and ROLLBACK touch only this run unit's changes; a dead run unit's holdings are rolled back by the next writable statement that meets one, so a connector opened INPUT before that reads the dead run unit's uncommitted records (DESIGN-runtime-library.md 2.2.1.10). (d) EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT, Table 13's name for §12.4.6.3.4 GR3/GR4's "EC-FLOW-APPLY", is checked under the ACTIVATING element's checking (the CALL's), latched before the activated element's scope opens; with checking off the clause stays inactive. (e) §12.4.6.3.4 GR6's change of address (detection processor dependent) has no cause to detect: SET ADDRESS OF requires a BASED item (§14.9.39.3 SR18) and §12.4.6.3.3 SR10 keeps a BASED item out of the clause. (f) "Under the control of a recursive runtime element" (§14.9.7.4 GR2, §14.9.36.4 GR2, §12.4.6.3.4 GR3, §9.1.18.7) is one question to the run unit's module stack, which marks the frame of every RECURSIVE program, function and method (§8.6.6: "Functions and methods are always recursive."): a program a method CALLs that executes COMMIT or ROLLBACK, or activates an APPLY COMMIT clause, raises the condition (kb/Work PB3540); a COMMIT or ROLLBACK written in a method is refused at translation (§14.9.7.3 SR1, COBOL1690). (g) A SEQUENTIAL file's transaction (2.2.2): the committed length L read at its first append and every rewritten record's first image are journaled, each synced before the change it precedes, and the first OPEN OUTPUT of an existing file or DELETE FILE copies the file whole into a before file first; the journal is three transient files in the file's lock directory (`txn-<id>.live`, `.journal`, `.before`), which exist only while the transaction is open, so a copy of the file taken without them is the file as it stands, committed (the owner's decision of 2026-10-19, kb/Work PB3340). A file not under commit control pays one directory listing per writable OPEN. A transaction holds the END of the file, so while one lives another connector's WRITE on the file answers '51' under `SHARING WITH ALL OTHER`, a REWRITE of a record it holds '51', an OPEN OUTPUT '61' and a DELETE FILE '62' (§9.1.13.9 2)); a run unit killed or lost to a power failure is rolled back by the next writable OPEN or DELETE FILE of the file in any run unit (§9.1.18.5). A covered file's posture with no SHARING clause is `SHARING WITH NO OTHER` for every open mode (the one handle serves every mode of the transaction). After a ROLLBACK the connector keeps its open mode: a writer's next WRITE lands at the restored end, or creates the file again when the ROLLBACK removed it (a creation undone: the state at the last COMMIT was "no file"); a reader keeps its file position indicator; a LINAGE file's page state is the one the last COMMIT or the OPEN left. A DELETE FILE after a CLOSE under commit control proceeds (the NOTE under §14.9.10.4 GR15: *"Such files can still be deleted, however if they are, then in the event of a rollback they will be restored"*). Known gaps, kb/Work notes: PB3492 (above, the keyed CAPTURE); §12.4.6.4.4 GR3, two files of one SAME clause both under commit and rollback, is not enforced (PB3539, an owner question). Witnesses: `conformance:cases/14.9.36-ROLLBACK/pb3338_apply_commit_rollback`, `conformance:cases/14.9.36-ROLLBACK/pb3340_sequential_file_under_apply_commit`, `conformance:cases/14.7.9-RETRY/pb3340_sequential_holding_exception_paths` (the holdings' 51, 52, 61 and 62 with and without a USE declarative), `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb695-apply-commit-no-on`, `unit:SequentialCommitControlTests` and `unit:SequentialJournalTests` (2.2.2.12's rows through the registry and the journal, every operation refused, made the point of a death and of a power loss through the fault-injecting medium), `conformance:cases/12.4.6-I-O-CONTROL/pb3338_apply_commit_external_two_elements`, `conformance:cases/14.9.7-COMMIT/pb3338_commit_rollback_under_recursive_element`, the `pb3338_apply_commit_sr*` refusals, `unit:TransactionControlTests` (the refused COMMIT and ROLLBACK at every region of 2.2.1.10 through the refusing medium), `unit:CommitRollbackRefusalWitnessTests` (the same refusals and item 8 through a compiled program), the `pb3542_item8_*`, `pb3543_item8_*` and `pb3544_item8_*` goldens (item 8's one rule, kb/Work PB3542-PB3544: only with checking for the condition not enabled, after the declarative and before a RESUME transfers control, never on a SORT or MERGE implicit transfer or after an ON EXCEPTION phrase that processes the condition, and as a ROLLBACK statement, so EC-FLOW-ROLLBACK in a SORT input or output procedure), `conformance:cases/12.4.6-I-O-CONTROL/pb3338_ec_flow_apply_commit_under_sort`, `conformance:cases/12.4.6-I-O-CONTROL/pb3338_ec_flow_apply_commit_under_recursive_element`, the method arm of the same rules (`conformance:cases/14.9.7-COMMIT/pb3540_commit_rollback_under_method`, `conformance:cases/14.9.7-COMMIT/pb3540_commit_under_factory_method_unchecked`, `conformance:cases/12.4.6-I-O-CONTROL/pb3540_ec_flow_apply_commit_under_method`, the refusals `pb3540_commit_in_object_method` and `pb3540_rollback_in_factory_method`) and `unit:CommitRollbackRuntimeTests` |
| A.4.4 | Dynamic capacity tables | **Claimed** | All three items. Item 2, OCCURS format 4 (P12 §8.5.1.9); item 3, SET format 14 (§14.9.39.4 GR29–GR31); item 1, the four exception conditions, each with a LIVE raise site: EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW (an IMPLICIT capacity change past the expected capacity — a receiving subscript, §8.5.1.9.3, and the recreation of a receiving table by a variable-length group MOVE or boundary transfer, §14.6.9.2 — first crossing only, §8.5.1.9.6 1); the one raise is `CobolDynTable.RaiseImplicitOverflow`, kb/Work PB1144), EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT (a new capacity above the implementor maximum OR beyond what the runtime can allocate, capacity unchanged — §8.5.1.9.6 2) and GR30 first arm, `GrowTo`; kb/Work PB1410), EC-FLOW-SEARCH (a capacity SET during a SEARCH of the same table — GR31, `SetCapacity`) and **EC-BOUND-SET** (a SET whose NEW capacity exceeds the expected maximum capacity — GR30 second arm, `SetCapacity`; kb/Work PB460 — before it the condition had a catalog row and no raise site while this row read Claimed). ⚖ Two determinations ride EC-BOUND-SET: (1) the explicit SET raises EC-BOUND-SET, the name its own statement rule gives, and NOT also EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW, although §8.5.1.9.6 GR1's first sentence is worded broadly enough to reach an explicit change — GR1's exemption is written for implicit changes only, and GR30 names the explicit case; (2) EC-BOUND-SET is raised on EVERY such SET (GR30 has no first-crossing exemption), and it is raised BEFORE the capacity changes — the shape of its implicit twin — so a USE declarative sees the capacity the table had, a declarative that completes normally lets the change proceed, and a RESUME that leaves the statement abandons it. ⚖ A third, for EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW (kb/Work PB1269): a declarative that executes RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT does NOT abandon the implicit change — §8.5.1.9.6 1) names that case outright (“the operation shall be allowed to continue, thus exceeding the receiving table's specified expected capacity”), so the raise site returns as for a declarative that completed normally, the statement finishes (the growth and the store both happen) and control then reaches the next statement; RESUME AT procedure-name still transfers out of the statement. §14.6.13.2 rule 6 (EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE for a table whose internal format does not agree with "the corresponding OCCURS clause") is reachable only where a table is shared across descriptions — a cell-backed area such as an EXTERNAL record (kb/Work PB1042) — and is asked there on every reference (`StorageCell.DynTableAt`, against the referencing description's FROM minimum and element width; `conformance:cases/14.6.13.2-Incompatible-data/pb1042_dyn_table_agreement`); every other table is built from its own description. | A.4.11 | Report Writer | Partial | **The LINAGE clause (item 10, §13.18.34) is CLAIMED and implemented whole** (kb/Work PB2503): Annex A.4.11 lists it with the Report Writer elements, and A.4.1 makes its syntax, general rules, exception conditions and I-O statuses optional with it, so the claim covers all of them, not the clause alone. It needs no report description: it is the print file's logical page of §13.18.34.4 (page size, FOOTING and the top and bottom margins, the LINAGE-COUNTER register of §8.4.3.14.4, and the §14.9.51.4 ADVANCING, end-of-page and GR26 page-transition rules), including the exception conditions EC-I-O-LINAGE and the implementor-defined I-O status `'90'` (A.1 item 110), at every `--std` on a sequential file (a LINE SEQUENTIAL file is one, §9.1.7.2, and exists from 2023). The claim is bounded by the file description entry's own general formats (§13.4.5.2), not by A.4.1's licence: a LINAGE clause on a Format 2 (relative or indexed) or Format 3 (report) entry is refused COBOL2604, because those formats print no linage-clause (§13.4.5.3 SR5/SR7/SR8; kb/Work PB1238, PB865; `FileDescriptionFormats`). Witnesses: `conformance-suite/cases/13.18.34-LINAGE/`, `13.4.5-File-description/pb1238-fd-linage-relative`, `pb1238-report-fd-linage`; `FileDescriptionFormatDriftTests.TheLinageClaim_AgreesWithTheFileDescriptionFormatTable` holds this sentence to the table. Implemented, the rest of the module: the RW nucleus incl. PRESENT WHEN + VARYING (P10 RW-2002) and the SUPPRESS statement (§14.9.45 — inhibits the current instance's printing/page-advance/NEXT GROUP/LINE-COUNTER but not sum accumulation or the end-of-group reset; SR1/GR1 resolve the enclosing USE BEFORE REPORTING group at bind, COBOL1581 rejects a misplaced SUPPRESS). A report group description entry REPEATS ON EITHER AXIS (kb/Work PB565): the multiple LINE clause is bound as §13.18.35.4 GR9's own reduction to a LINE clause with one operand plus a simple OCCURS clause, so it and §13.18.38 format 3 are ONE mechanism, and the entry's axis decides whether integer-3 displaces vertically (GR10c/GR10d, GR12c/GR12d) or horizontally (GR10a/GR10b, GR12a/GR12b). Both COBOL0899 report-repetition stages are retired; the syntax rules now report through the family code that owns them (COBOL2021 for the OCCURS clause, COBOL2199 for the LINE clause). The NEXT GROUP clause is LIVE in all three forms, WITH RESET included (§13.18.37; kb/Work PB957 — the engine applies §13.18.37.4 GR1–GR6 after the group's last line, and COBOL2284 screens §13.18.37.3 SR1/SR3–SR7 and §13.15.3 SR6), and every report-writer relative operand — LINE, COLUMN and NEXT GROUP — admits both PLUS and + (§13.18.35.3 SR1 / §13.18.14.3 SR2 / §13.18.37.3 SR2; kb/Work PB951). The LINE clause's NEXT PAGE phrase is LIVE in both operand forms (§13.18.35; kb/Work PB1001 — §13.18.35.4 GR4a/GR5a, and COBOL2199 screens §13.18.35.3 SR3/SR5/SR7/SR8 — kb/Work PB1002). The RD CODE clause is LIVE (§13.18.12; kb/Work PB1129): literal-1 or identifier-1 prefixes every record the report writes (GR1), the code is not part of the line description but is part of the logical record size (GR2, `RECORD CONTAINS` = code + line), an identifier is evaluated per body group — at the page advance's step c) or, when none is performed, at the group's start (GR3, §14.9.16.4 GR6 c)) — and COBOL2713 reports SR1 (an alphanumeric literal), SR2 (an alphanumeric item that is no ODO group, variable-length group or dynamic-length item) and SR3 (every report of a file or none). It is not edition-gated: the 2023 text does not say which edition introduced the identifier form (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE has no row for it), and an unverified gate would reject legal source; a subscripted or reference-modified identifier is LIVE (kb/Work PB1292; see §3 "RD CODE reference modification"). The SOURCE clause's identifier-1 is bound as §13.18.53.4 GR1's implicit MOVE sender by the ONE operand binder a MOVE takes (kb/Work PB1292, PB1316, PB1456), so a subscripted or reference-modified identifier, a sum counter of the current report (§13.18.53.3 SR4; a name two reports share is that of the current one), a numeric constant-name (§13.10.3 SR2: arithmetic-expression-1 with one operand), a report counter of ANOTHER report qualified by its report-name (§8.4.2.2.3 SR9/SR10) and a VARYING counter are all SOURCE operands; an unqualified counter in the report section is qualified implicitly by the enclosing RD, and a counter qualified by a name that is no report is COBOL2729 (the same code the procedure division's SR9/SR10 violations take, kb/Work PB1049). A VARYING counter is the data item of its ENTRY (§13.18.64.4 GR1), in scope within that entry and its subordinate entries (§13.18.64.3 SR2): a group entry's counter is referable by its subordinates' SOURCE, subscripts, FROM and BY, a BY may name a counter of its own clause (the running recurrence of GR3 b); see §3 "VARYING counters of one clause"), and the three arms of SR2's "not defined elsewhere" (a name twice in one entry, a name an enclosing entry defines, a name defined by a data item or report section item) report as COBOL1559 once per written entry. An FD may name SEVERAL reports (`REPORTS ARE r1 r2`, §13.18.46.4 GR1; kb/Work PB1050): each has its own engine over the one file connector and the records reach the file in GENERATE order, told apart by their CODE; COBOL2714 reports the REPORT clause's name-correspondence rules (§13.18.46.3 SR1/SR2, §13.14.3 SR1; kb/Work PB1285). Staged LOUD (COBOL0899 band): the GLOBAL clause, a FUNCTION reference inside PRESENT WHEN, and GROUP INDICATE on a relative COLUMN operand. A SUM clause's data-name-1 is LIVE (kb/Work PB1294): a report section entry's sum counter, or the operand of its SOURCE or VALUE clause — an UNPRINTABLE SOURCE entry included (§13.18.53.4 GR3) — added when the group that contains it is processed (§13.18.54.4 GR6, GR7 a)/b), GR11), repeating addends mapped onto repeating counters by their innermost levels (GR8, SR4 b)/c)/d)), in the counter's own report or another's (SR4 g)), with SR4's other rules reported as COBOL2730 and the report-type pairings of SR4 f) as COBOL2731; an UPON on a detail of another report is LIVE too (GR7 c) 2)). A report group item may be DISPLAY **or NATIONAL** (§13.18.60.3 SR7, COBOL2198 screens the clause and SR2's group/subordinate agreement; §13.18.60.4 GR1 inherits a group entry's usage — kb/Work PB541), and PAGE-COUNTER is a receiving operand wherever an integer data item may appear (§8.4.3.15.3 SR1; LINE-COUNTER is refused by SR3 as COBOL2197 — kb/Work PB429). The REPORT SECTION's entry grammar is the printed one (§13.8.2, §13.15.2, §13.18.39.2; kb/Work PB1226, PB1059): an RD is followed by `{ constant-entry | report-group-description-entry } …` (a constant entry binds into the compile-time constant table at the point it stands — its value substitutes in a later VALUE operand, PICTURE repetition `X(K)` and the procedure division — and COBOL2708 reports an RD followed by no report group description entry, §13.8.4), the entry-name clause is the data description entry's own `dataName` (so `05 FILLER COLUMN 1 PIC X …` and `01 FILLER TYPE PAGE HEADING` parse, §13.18.20.3 SR3), and the PAGE clause carries all of §13.18.39.2 — `integer-2 {COLS | COLUMNS}` (the page width, 999 when omitted, §13.18.39.4 GR5: it bounds the COLUMN clause's own operands at compile time, COBOL2710 §13.18.14.3 SR6, and the line the engine truncates with EC-REPORT-PAGE-WIDTH, §13.18.14.4 GR5; a width alone leaves the report unpaged, GR2a), `LAST {CONTROL HEADING | CH} IS integer-5` (the control heading's lower limit, §13.18.57.4 GR8 d)) and the `FIRST DE` / `LAST DE` abbreviations (§13.18.39.3 SR1), with COBOL2709 for a phrase written without integer-1 (SR3). Not edition-gated: whether ISO 1989:2002 introduced these PAGE spellings is not derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d), and an unverified gate would reject legal source, so they are accepted at every edition. The TYPE clause carries Format 2 whole (§13.18.57.2; kb/Work PB1298, PB1248): `{CONTROL HEADING | CH} [ [ON | FOR] {data-name-1 | FINAL} [OR PAGE] ]` and the footing without OR PAGE. A control heading written with OR PAGE is reprinted after every page advance, following the page heading, major to minor, as the first body group of the page (§13.18.57.4 GR6 c); the page-advance proviso — not before a control footing at a lower control level — is read with the HEADING's level as the referent of "lower" (kb/Work PB1927; the printed sentence is elliptical and, read with the footing as the referent, contradicts GR7 d) 4., which gives a control footing an upper limit after the lowest OR PAGE heading at its own level or higher; IBM's Report Writer, SC26-4301 section 3.24.4 rule 1.c, states the same outcome: no control heading below the level of the footing is printed): a page advance caused by a control footing at level j reprints the OR PAGE headings at level j and every higher level, FINAL being the highest, and skips those below j, which the footing's own break prints in their turn. The GR7 d) upper limits ARE modelled (`DataBinder.GroupLimits`): a heading below another is placed after it (`HeadingReach`: the last line of a heading is walked from the last line of the nearest OR PAGE heading above it, not from FIRST DETAIL), so an absolute LINE above a d) 2./3./4. limit is COBOL2199, SR6 c) (kb/Work PB2513). **A sum counter is a signed USAGE DISPLAY numeric item** (§13.18.54.4 GR1 gives it a category, a digit count derived from the PICTURE and a sign, and states NO usage; §14.9.1.4 GR7 shows the standard naming a usage where it makes a conceptual item one, so the choice is the implementor's, kb/Work PB1943, PB2520): the profile of `S9(n)V9(m)` DISPLAY with the default operational sign (trailing, not separate: the last digit carries the sign in the processor's overpunch convention, `--sign-encoding`), n+m the PICTURE's digits. Consequences, each the ordinary rule for such an item: §8.4.3.3.3 SR1 admits a reference modifier on the counter (`MOVE CF-T (1:2) TO X`, `CF-U (2) (2:3)` after the subscripts of a repeating counter, in a SOURCE clause, and as a receiver, GR12), a second modifier is SR3's violation (COBOL1630); positions are the digit characters, the last of which is the signed digit; FUNCTION LENGTH of a PIC 9999 counter is 4. The counter keeps the characters stored in it, as a stored item does (§8.4.3.3.4 GR5: the modified item is "a subset of the data item referenced by identifier-1"; kb/Work PB2553): `MOVE "X" TO CF-T (2:1)` leaves `1X3D`, `CF-T IS NUMERIC` is then false, `MOVE SPACE TO CF-T (1:4)` leaves spaces (SPACE into the counter itself is refused at every edition, §14.9.25.3 SR5, kb/Work PB3605), and a reference to such content — a numeric statement, or the GENERATE whose §13.18.54.4 GR3 addition reads it — is §14.6.13.2 rule 2's EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE; a numeric store makes the content valid again. The engine still accumulates in an integer and holds the characters beside it while they are not a numeric image. DISPLAY of a counter shows the signed DISPLAY image (`123D` for +1234 in the default convention). Micro Focus sizes the counter by its PICTURE in character positions; GnuCOBOL has no observation to follow (it binds a reference-modified counter name to the entry's own unsigned storage, never to the counter). COBOL0899 (report-page-type-requires-page) also covers OR PAGE in a report with no page limit (SR12) and COBOL2199 an absolute LINE in an OR PAGE heading (§13.18.35.3 SR9). The COLUMN clause carries its LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT alignment phrase (§13.18.14.2 Format 1; kb/Work PB1220): GR6 b)–d) place the item from integer-1 and the printable-size, GR9's horizontal counter takes the aligned item's rightmost column, COBOL2711 is SR9's absolute-only rule, the phrase gates 2002 with the other COLUMN forms, and COBOL2712 refuses an aligned item whose leftmost column falls before column 1 (a case the standard states no outcome for; see §3 "COLUMN alignment"). The full itemization: `docs/REPORT_WRITER_DESIGN.md` §5 |

## 6. Maintenance

Update this document in the same change set as any change to the supported surface (a new usage, a facility
newly implemented or newly documented as non-support, an I-O status determination). The declined-facility
sites — every one of them routed through `EditionContext.Declined`, whose refuse rule (`EditionContext.Refuses`: the
descriptor's severity, with a `PermissiveInert` refusal accepted under `--permissive`) chooses warn-inert from
refuse — are the code-side counterpart; keep the two in sync. This file is referenced by
`docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md` (the edition-change checklist) and by `docs/DOC_INDEX.md`.

## 7. Annex A.1 — implementor-defined language element register (§4.2.5 / §4.2.16)

> **STATUS: every documentation obligation is discharged (2026-09-25, doc-rows-2) — but a documented determination is
> not always what the compiler does yet: a row whose ⚠ names a kb/Work note states the INTENDED behaviour, and its
> traceability-inventory verdict (DIVERGES / PARTIAL / NOT-IMPLEMENTED) is held open by that note.**
> Annex A.1 lists **222** implementor-defined language elements: **164 required · 30 optional · 27
> conditionally required · 1 whose class the standard states in prose rather than the usual sentence
> (item 176, the SET NaN payload)**, of which **199 carry the obligation "This item shall be documented in the
> implementor's user documentation"** and 23 explicitly do not. §4.2.5 requires the implementor to *specify*
> every element identified as required and to *document* every element identified as requiring documentation;
> D13 makes those 199 part of the definition of done.
> **MEASURED 2026-09-25 — this register discharges 182 of the 182 in scope, and 0 obligations remain**;
> 205 items carry a determination, twenty-three of them (**35**, **60**, **61**, **63**, **69**, **81**, **90**, **92**,
> **104**, **113**, **118**, **119**, **123**, **125**, **138**, **144**, **169**, **170**, **186**, **194**, **200**,
> **201**, **220**) documented voluntarily where A.1 does not require it. ⚙ **The numbers and the item list are `python scripts/spec/audit_annex_a1.py`'s
> output, not a hand count — run it rather than trusting this sentence.** An enumeration of the discharged items
> used to live in this paragraph and it rotted twice: stale by three when item 50 landed, and by three again by
> 2026-09-02. The script prints the list (`--json`'s `filed`), the C# gate `AnnexA1RegisterDriftTests` runs it
> every build, and a list here could only ever be a second answer to a question one artifact already owns.
> The rows below are the register itself, and they are what the script reads. Notable among them are the
> **storage-representation items 205–209, 211 and 215** that V59 pinned (BINARY · the BINARY-CHAR family ·
> COMPUTATIONAL · INDEX · PACKED-DECIMAL: the byte width, the radix, the byte order and a worked example for
> each, since a COBOL developer reading this needs to know what lands on disk).
> ⛔ **SEVENTEEN OF THE 199 CANNOT ARISE, so the denominator is 182** — items **84**,
> **85** (FORMAT clause), **173** (SELECT WHEN clause) and **86** (Format validation, which cites only PICTURE GR15
> and USAGE GR3 *during a VALIDATE statement*), and — by owner decision R42 (2026-09-24) — the eleven items of the
> declined screen-handling and commit/rollback modules: **3**, **4** (ACCEPT screen format), **11**

In a standalone executable a REDIRECTED standard input (a pipe or a file) is decoded as **UTF-8**, without byte-order-mark detection, by the process entry (`StandardStreams.EnsureUtf8`; kb/Work PB3193 — on Windows it was the console's OEM code page, so the bytes C3 A9 reached the receiver as two characters); an **interactive Windows console's** input is read through the console's wide-character interface (`ReadConsoleW`: the same entry sets the console's encoding to UTF-16, which .NET serves that way and which changes no code page), so a character outside the console's input code page arrives as itself (€ U+20AC and 中 U+4E2D typed under code page 437 store as typed, not as `?`; kb/Work PB3294), and the console's end-of-input signal survives that interface (`ConsoleInputReader`: Ctrl+Z as the first character of a line ends the input, as the console's own read ends it, so `ACCEPT` leaves the unfilled remainder as spaces, `AcceptSource.Device`, and a program reading until end-of-input sees the end; Ctrl+Z elsewhere in a line is an ordinary character), and an interactive Unix terminal's input is decoded in the terminal's locale; under a host (item 167) a run unit reads the host's `Console.In` as the host configured it; each receiver shape converts them as follows (`AcceptDisplayEmitter.EmitAcceptDevice`). **Alphanumeric, alphabetic, alphanumeric-edited, numeric-edited, national and national-edited** receivers: **no conversion** — the characters store as-is, one per character position, with no editing applied (a NATIONAL receiver's conversion is the identity on the UTF-16 substrate). A **reference-modified** receiver takes the characters into the slice the same way; a **group** receiver takes them positionally across its character positions. A **fixed-point numeric** receiver of ANY usage (DISPLAY, NATIONAL, COMP, COMP-3, COMP-5, BINARY-\*, …) converts the transferred characters by the form the compile option **`--numeric-display`** selects (kb/Work PB3513; the inverse of DISPLAY's conversion, item 56, and baked into the compiled program the same way, at every `--std`). **`decimal` (the DEFAULT)** reads DISPLAY's own decimal form back, as GnuCOBOL 3.2.0's default configuration does (the precedence tiebreaker of CLAUDE.md rule 1, measured 2026-10-23 with `cobc -x -std=default` over about 1,300 receiver and text pairs, `CobolNum.ParseDeviceDecimal`): (a) the text converted is the receiver's own SIZE in leftmost characters for an item stored as characters (a DISPLAY or NATIONAL item: its digit positions plus one for SIGN SEPARATE, §14.9.1.4 GR3 and GR4 b)) and ONE WHOLE RECORD (item 5) for a binary or packed item, which has no character positions to size a window by; Where WiseOwl COBOL does NOT copy GnuCOBOL: a NATIONAL item reads its own size like a DISPLAY item (ISO GR4 b)'s leftmost characters), where GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 reads the whole line into it and keeps unrelated digits for a line longer than the item (an in-size text converts alike). **`digits`** keeps the digit window of every earlier revision: a window of the receiver's digit count plus one position for SIGN SEPARATE, for every usage, **decoded as that item's display image**: the digit characters, in order, form the value at the PICTURE's implied scale, every non-digit character contributes no digit, and the sign is read where the description puts it (a separate `+`/`-`; an over-punch per the program's §13.18.52.4 GR5 b) sign set; a leading `-` for the binary family); no exception is set.
