Range **[0, 86 400)** — LEAP-SECOND's §7.3.17 default OFF is the only supported mode (§15.5.5), so a value ≥ 86 400 is unreachable. | DOC-A.1-176 | **SET statement — the value in a NaN PAYLOAD**, §14.9.39.4 GR34 and GR35, required + documented | **Quiet NaN: payload ZERO. Signaling NaN: payload ONE.** GR34/GR35 set the content of identifier-14 to "a canonical representation of a quiet NaN / of a signaling NaN, with the payload set to an implementor-defined value, as described in ISO/IEC 60559:2020, Clause 3, for the basic interchange format corresponding to the usage of identifier-14", and A.1 item 176 makes the choice documentable. §14.9.39.3 SR32 confines the receiver to a STANDARD floating-point usage (§3.166 / §3.167), and of those WiseOwl COBOL provides FLOAT-BINARY-32 = IEEE binary32 and FLOAT-BINARY-64 = IEEE binary64 EXACTLY — the other three are Annex A.3 items 17/19 documented non-support (§2 rows 17 and 19), refused at declaration — so the interchange format the rules name IS the .NET carrier and nothing is approximated. **The full encodings, sign bit from GR34/GR35's own last sentence (the SIGN phrase, positive when absent):** binary32 quiet `0x7FC00000` (`0xFFC00000` negative), binary32 signaling `0x7F800001` (`0xFF800001`); binary64 quiet `0x7FF8000000000000` (`0xFFF8000000000000`), binary64 signaling `0x7FF0000000000001` (`0xFFF0000000000001`). The QUIET payload of zero is the canonical NaN every IEEE implementation produces — leading significand bit set, every other significand bit clear; the SIGNALING payload of one is the SMALLEST value that keeps the significand nonzero once ISO/IEC 60559:2020 §6.2.1's quiet bit is cleared, which a signaling NaN requires. **⛔ Written as BIT PATTERNS, never as a CLR constant:** `double.NaN` is `0xFFF8000000000000` — its sign bit is SET — so GR34's "otherwise the sign is positive" would have to be spelled `-double.NaN` and would depend on how a constant negation folds; and the CLR has no signaling-NaN constant at all, because every managed arithmetic path quiets one. **⛔ And delivered to the item with no binary64 anywhere on the way (kb/Work PB961):** a binary32 → binary64 widening QUIETS a signaling NaN, so the value is materialized by an opaque runtime call over the bits (`CobolFloat.FromBinary32Bits` / `FromBinary64Bits` — an inline `BitConverter` reinterpretation of a constant is a JIT floating constant, which the JIT carries as a double, and it stored the binary32 signaling NaN as the QUIET `0x7FC00001`), and a windowed or record-image FLOAT-BINARY-32 encodes and decodes through the binary32 carrier's own lanes (`CobolNum.FormatImageSingle` / `ParseImageSingle`). A same-usage MOVE of the item copies it on its own carrier, as §14.9.25.4 GR6 c) requires ("transferred to the receiving data item without change"), so a copy keeps the payload too. ONE table, `IeeeSpecials.Bits` (`src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IeeeSpecials.cs`), is both the emitted encoding and the documented one; `RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits` spells it. The quiet-versus-signaling distinction is COBOL-observable through §8.8.4.4.4 GR3 j)/k)'s FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-QUIET / -SIGNALING class conditions (kb/Work PB225), decided on the carrier's raw bits by `CobolFloatClass`; `CobolFloatClassTests` pins that every value this table writes classifies as what it was written as. | `unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.EveryCanonicalValue_DecodesToWhatItsGeneralRuleRequires`; `unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits`; `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb452_set_content_float`; `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb961_signaling_nan_binary32`; `unit:CobolFloatClassTests.EverySetFormat15Value_ClassifiesAsWhatItWasWrittenAs` |
| DOC-A.1-174 | **SET statement — the effect of SET on the FUNCTION whose address is being stored in a function-pointer**, §14.9.39.4 GR15, required + documented | **NONE. Storing a function's address does nothing whatever to the function.** GR15 says only that the effect "is implementor-defined", so the whole obligation is to say what this implementation does, and what it does is defined by what a function-pointer IS here: the externalized function-name (§8.4.3.12.4 GR2 — "For a COBOL function, the address is that of the function identified by the externalized function-name in its FUNCTION-ID paragraph"), carried in the managed `FunctionPointer` identity struct. **Taking that address therefore performs no activation, no loading, no linking, no allocation and no initial-state establishment**: §14.6.2.3.2's initial state is established "the first time the function … is activated in a run unit", and a SET is not an activation (§8.4.3.2.4 GR6 is the only thing that activates a function). Concretely: a function's WORKING-STORAGE is untouched, a previously activated function keeps its §13.5.4 GR1 static data exactly as it stood, and a never-activated function stays never-activated — `ProgramTable.FunctionAddressOf` performs a registry LOOKUP only, and its one side effect (the separately-compiled sibling-module probe) is the same module load a CALL would perform and changes no COBOL-visible state. Consequently a function's RESULT cannot depend on whether its address was taken, which is what the witness measures. ⚠ The empty answer is the substantive one: an implementation that (say) pinned or eagerly initialized the function would have to say so here, and a program relying on either would be relying on an implementor definition. **The witness is an OBSERVATION, not a restatement:** `conformance:cases/8.4.3.10-NULL-address-pointer-and-message-tag/pb452_set_function_pointer` activates `FUNCTION PBF8DBL(21)` before the first SET and again after the last, and both activations print `000000042` — so the function's result cannot depend on whether its address was taken. | `conformance:cases/8.4.3.10-NULL-address-pointer-and-message-tag/pb452_set_function_pointer`; `conformance:cases/8.4.3.10-NULL-address-pointer-and-message-tag/pb452_function_address_runtime` |
| DOC-A.1-175 | **SET statement — the effect of SET on the PROGRAM whose address is being stored in a program-pointer**, §14.9.39.4 GR17, required + documented | **NONE. Storing a program's address does nothing whatever to the program.** GR17 says only that the effect "is implementor-defined", so the obligation is to say what this implementation does, and it is fixed by what a program-pointer IS here: the externalized program-name of an OUTERMOST program (§8.4.3.13.4 GR2), carried in the managed `ProgramPointer` identity struct. `SET … TO ENTRY` performs a registry LOOKUP only (`ProgramTable.EntryOf` — its one side effect, the separately-compiled sibling-module probe, is the same module load a CALL would perform and changes no COBOL-visible state), and `SET pp TO pp2` / `TO NULL` is a carrier copy (`SetEmitter.EmitSetProgramPointer`). **So the SET performs no activation, no CANCEL, and no initial-state establishment**: a program already activated keeps its WORKING-STORAGE in its last-used state (§8.6.4), a never-activated program stays never-activated, and a later CALL through the pointer is an ordinary CALL of that program (§14.9.4). ⚠ The empty answer is the substantive one, exactly as for item 174: an implementation that (say) loaded, initialized or cancelled the program would have to say so here. **The witness is an OBSERVATION:** `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb460_set_program_pointer_effect` calls a counting subprogram once (`COUNT=1`), stores its address three times, and calls it through the pointer — `COUNT=2`, where a SET that re-initialized it would print `COUNT=1`; a third program whose address is stored but which is never called prints nothing. | `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb460_set_program_pointer_effect`; `conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/program_pointer` |
| DOC-A.1-210 | **USAGE FUNCTION-POINTER clause — alignment, size and representation of data, and allowable languages**, §13.18.60.4 GR26, required + documented | GR26 leaves four things to the implementor and this determination answers all four. **ALIGNMENT: none** (the item 205 rule). §13.18.60.3 SR14 confines a function-pointer to a level-1/77 elementary item or an elementary item of a STRONG type declaration. Its value rides a MANAGED SLOT (`StorageForm.FunctionPointerRef`), and inside a strongly-typed group it occupies 8 character positions whose character image is the D-SLOT placeholder — eight SPACES, whether the pointer is NULL or not — exactly as a `POINTER` or `PROGRAM-POINTER` leaf does (item 56): `01 G TYPEDEF STRONG` of `PIC X(3)`, a `FUNCTION-POINTER TO` leaf and `PIC X(2)` has `FUNCTION LENGTH` 13 and displays `abc` + eight spaces + `zz` before and after `SET … TO ADDRESS OF FUNCTION`. **SIZE: 8 character positions** wherever a size is asked for (`FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH`, the `ElementaryByteWidth` pin) — the 64-bit managed reference width this implementation reserves for every class-pointer leaf, shared with POINTER / PROGRAM-POINTER / OBJECT REFERENCE / INDEX so the four cannot drift. **REPRESENTATION: the function's EXTERNALIZED FUNCTION-NAME**, held in the readonly record struct `FunctionPointer(string? Name)` (`src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Control/FunctionPointer.cs`) and resolved through the ONE run-unit `ProgramTable`; the predefined address NULL is the null name, which §8.4.3.10.4 GR2's "guaranteed not to represent the address of any function" satisfies because no FUNCTION-ID paragraph can name a function null. It is deliberately a SEPARATE type from `ProgramPointer`, whose representation is the same shape: §8.4.3.10.4 keeps the predefined NULLs apart by category and §14.9.39.3 SR20/SR21 forbid mixing the categories in one SET, so one shared struct would have made the two assignment-compatible in the GENERATED C#, the one place a binder screen cannot reach. **ALLOWABLE LANGUAGES: COBOL only.** GR26's second paragraph admits "another language for which the implementor has declared support for access by function pointers" and this implementation declares none: a non-COBOL function has no run-unit registration to resolve, so §8.4.3.12.4 GR4 — EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND and the predefined address NULL — is the defined answer for one, never an undefined outcome — which the `NF-RAISED` / `B-NULL` pair of `conformance:cases/8.4.3.10-NULL-address-pointer-and-message-tag/pb452_function_address_runtime` measures. | `conformance:cases/8.4.3.10-NULL-address-pointer-and-message-tag/pb452_set_function_pointer`; `conformance:cases/8.4.3.10-NULL-address-pointer-and-message-tag/pb452_function_address_runtime`; `conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb452-function-pointer-without-to` |
| DOC-A.1-177 | **SIGN clause — representation when the picture character-string contains the symbol 'S' and no optional SIGN clause applies**, §13.18.52.4 GR4 + §8.5.1.5, required + documented | **The operational sign is FUSED onto the TRAILING digit position, and WHICH characters it uses is the compile option `--sign-encoding`, default `ibm`** — owner decision kb/Work PB803, 2026-09-09: *"Keep both behind an option with the default being IBM and Micro Focus compatibility."* GR4 grants both halves at once (“Neither the representation nor the position of that operational sign is specified by the symbol 'S'. The implementor shall specify the position and representation of the operational sign”) and §8.5.1.5 repeats the obligation (“if it is not used, operational signs will be represented as defined by the implementor”), so this determination answers both. **POSITION — TRAILING**: an item with no SIGN clause is byte-identical to one that writes `SIGN IS TRAILING`, and different from one that writes `SIGN IS LEADING`. **REPRESENTATION — two conventions, one table pair each, chosen at COMPILE time:** `ibm` (**the default**) fuses positive 0–9 to `{ABCDEFGHI` and negative 0–9 to `}JKLMNOPQR`, so `PIC S9(3)` +123 is `12C`, −123 is `12L` and `SIGN IS LEADING` −123 is `J23`; `ascii` leaves a POSITIVE digit alone and makes a negative digit *digit + 0x40* (`pqrstuvwxy`), so `PIC S9(4)` −1234 is `123t` and `SIGN IS LEADING` −1234 is `q234`. Surveyed rather than invented: `ibm` is what IBM Enterprise COBOL, Micro Focus and GnuCOBOL's `-fsign=ebcdic` write, `ascii` is GnuCOBOL's `-fsign=ascii` (its default on a PC host) — read from that compiler's published test expectations, never its sources. The value is spelled **`ibm`, not “ebcdic”**, because nothing about those characters is EBCDIC-encoded on an ASCII host: they are what an EBCDIC-descended CONVENTION produces after translation, and the misnomer would make the option unreadable. **The fused sign occupies an EXISTING digit position and adds none** (§13.18.52.4 GR5 a, which is normative and not part of the latitude), so `PIC S9(3)` is 3 character positions under either convention. **⚠ THE INTERCHANGE CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than left implicit:** the convention is a property of the **COMPILED PROGRAM** — baked into every emitted `NumProfile` and into every emitted signed class condition, never read from the process environment — so two programs of one run unit compiled under different options each read storage by their OWN convention, exactly as two vendors' programs do. Nothing records the convention of a DATA FILE: it is whatever wrote the file, and a mismatch is undetectable (a record holding `123t` read through a program compiled `ibm` yields +1230, silently). A signed DISPLAY item that must cross a convention boundary should be declared `SIGN IS SEPARATE`, whose characters §13.18.52.4 GR6 b) pins to `+`/`-` with no implementor latitude at all. ONE table pair per convention lives in `ZonedSign` (`src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/ZonedSign.cs`), consulted by the encoder (`CobolNum.FormatDisplaySigned`), the decoder (`CobolNum.ParseDisplay`) and the class condition alike; the option reaches them through `PicInfo.ProfileInitializer(SignEncoding)`, the one place a `NumProfile` is written. | `conformance:cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_default_representation`; `conformance:wiseowl/cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_encoding_ascii`; `conformance:cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_default_representation_85` |
| DOC-A.1-178 | **SIGN clause — what constitutes a valid sign when the SEPARATE CHARACTER phrase is not present**, §13.18.52.4 GR5 b), required + documented | **At the SIGN POSITION: a plain digit `0`–`9`, plus both tables of the program's `--sign-encoding` convention. Every other character position must be a plain digit.** Under the default `ibm` the sign position admits `0`–`9`, `{`, `A`–`I`, `}`, `J`–`R`; under `ascii` it admits `0`–`9` and `p`–`y`. Any other character there makes the item **NOT NUMERIC**. GR5 b) — “The implementor defines what constitutes valid signs for data items” — is the whole of the latitude, and §8.8.4.4.4 GR3 n)1.a delegates the NUMERIC class condition to it by name (“Valid operational signs are defined in 13.18.52, SIGN clause”). **A PLAIN DIGIT IS VALID, and means POSITIVE**: an unseparated sign shares a digit position, so an item whose sign was never punched — what a group MOVE of raw characters deposits, and what the `ascii` convention writes for every positive value — is well formed. **A punched character carries a DIGIT as well as a sign**, so the valid set also fixes the VALUE: under `ibm`, `12C` is +123, `12L` is −123, `12{` is +120 and `12}` is −120, and at the LEADING position `C23` is +**3**23 (the punch contributes digit 3, exactly as it does at the trailing position of `12C`) — a sign-only reading would answer +123 and be wrong. The refused near-misses are worth naming: `+` and `-` are §13.18.52.4 GR6 b)'s SEPARATE characters and are NOT valid here, and neither are a space, a lower-case `l`, or a letter past the end of the run such as `Z`. **The set is DERIVED from the same `ZonedSign` tables the encoder punches with** — `ZonedSign.IsSignCharacter`, reached from `CobolClass.IsNumericZoned` (the class condition, emitted by `ConditionRenderer.RenderClass`) and from `CobolNum.IsNumericImage` (§14.6.13.2 rule 2's checked sending read, which the standard defines BY REFERENCE to the class condition) — never written a second time; it previously stood as a literal character-range pattern beside the tables and could only ever have answered for one convention. **GR5 a) is documented with it because it is NOT latitude:** the sign is *presumed to be associated with* a DIGIT position, so `PIC S9(3) SIGN IS LEADING` and `PIC S9(3) SIGN IS TRAILING` are each **3** character positions, never 4. What a numeric operation makes of a character OUTSIDE the valid set is a different obligation (§14.6.13.2 / EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE) and is not filed here. | `conformance:cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_valid_set`; `conformance:wiseowl/cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_encoding_ascii`; `conformance:cases/13.18.52-SIGN/pb803_sign_default_representation_85` |
| DOC-A.1-22 | **CHAR-NATIONAL function — which one of the multiple characters is returned**, §15.16.4 r2 (second sentence), required + documented | §15.16.4 r2 has TWO branches and only the second is an implementor obligation. **Branch 1 — the order is DEFINED** (an `ALPHABET … FOR NATIONAL` literal phrase with `ALSO`): the standard itself answers — “the character returned is the first character defined for that character position”, and §12.3.7.4 GR7 k)6 fixes which one that is (“Literal-1 is the first character in the sequence of multiple characters defined at that ordinal position”). WiseOwl COBOL obeys it (`NationalCollation.CharAt` reads the emitted `__COLLATE_NAT` table in the alphabet’s own written order), but that is CONFORMANCE, not a determination. **Branch 2 — the order is UNDEFINED, and this is item 22:** an `ALPHABET … FOR NATIONAL IS LOCALE` sequence is an ALGORITHM, not a written order, so every set of characters the locale collates EQUALLY shares one ordinal position with no order among its members. **WiseOwl COBOL returns the LOWEST-CODED member of that rank** — `LocaleCollation.OrderVector.FirstOfRank`, a vector materialized once per collator, so the answer is the same for every invocation at a given implementation, collating sequence and ordinal position, exactly as r2’s third sentence requires. (Position 1 of a locale national sequence is the completely-ignorable rank; its lowest-coded member is U+0000.) Determination **L7** (§4 locale facility) states the position model this refines; `HIGH-VALUE`/`LOW-VALUE` read `LastOfRank`/`FirstOfRank` of the same vector. | `conformance:cases/A.1-Implementor-defined-language-element-list/l1_char_national_locale_tie`; `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/l1_char_national_also_positions` |
| DOC-A.1-180 | **SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC function — usage of the argument when native arithmetic is in effect**, §15.83.3 r4, required + documented | **No restriction beyond the standard's own rules 2 and 3** (kb/Work PB122, 2026-08-29 — supersedes the earlier refusal of floating-point usages, whose rationale — that a smallest increment for an IEEE float is exponent-dependent — confused the ULP of a stored VALUE with the format minimum §15.83.1 actually asks for; r4's latitude also could not license the refusal under the STANDARD modes, where it was an over-rejection). Every numeric usage is accepted. A fixed-point argument returns **10^(−scale)** (§15.83.4 RVR2 — `S999` → +1, `99V9(3)` → 0.001, `S9PP` → +100, `BINARY-CHAR` → +1). A floating-point argument returns **the smallest positive (subnormal) value of the item's CARRIER** — the smallest algebraic difference between two representable values (§15.83.1), a property of the format exactly as 10^(−scale) is of a PICTURE: binary32 carriers (COMP-1 / FLOAT / FLOAT-SHORT / FLOAT-BINARY-32) → 2^−149 = 1.401298464324817070923729583289916E−45, binary64 carriers (COMP-2 / FLOAT-LONG / FLOAT-EXTENDED / FLOAT-BINARY-64) → 2^−1074 = 4.940656458412465441765687928682214E−324 (34 correctly-rounded digits — full decimal128 precision; the HIGHEST/LOWEST max folds keep R10's round-trip grain), the decimal carrier → 1E−28. The §15.83.4 r1 IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE screen on the entry is enforced beside the r2/r3 usage bars (every carrier declarable today passes under both reachable modes; the guard fires automatically if a wider carrier ever lands). Pinned by `2023/pb122_smallest_algebraic_float` and `Algebraic_SmallestFloat_FoldsToCarrierSubnormal`. | `conformance:cases/15.43.3-Argument-rules/pb122_smallest_algebraic_float` |
| DOC-A.1-183 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, code-name-1 - the alphanumeric coded character set and collating sequence, the ordinal number of characters, and the correspondence with the native alphanumeric character set**, ISO 12.3.7.4 GR7 i, **conditionally required** ("conditioned upon the existence of a code-name") + documented | **Two code-names exist, so this item is LIVE** (it was vacuous until owner decision kb/Work PB793 filled the SR15 set; see A.1 item 184). GR7 i asks for three things per name, and Table 6 gives code-name-1 a Y in both the coded-character-set and the collating-sequence column, so each name answers all three.<br>**`ASCII` - the ISO/IEC 646 International Reference Version.** *Coded character set:* the 128 characters of ISO/IEC 646 IRV. *Ordinal number of characters:* 128; ordinal n is the character at ordinal position n of that set. *Correspondence with the native alphanumeric character set:* the IDENTITY on U+0000-U+007F - ordinal n corresponds to native character U+(n-1) - because the first 128 positions of the native alphanumeric character set ARE ISO/IEC 646 IRV (item 188 / determination D-N1). *Collating position of each character:* its native collating position, i.e. the sequence IS the native order, which is what 12.3.7.4 GR7 c already says of the STANDARD-1 keyword ("The collating sequence referenced by both the STANDARD-1 and STANDARD-2 phrases shall be as defined by the order in which characters appear in ISO/IEC 646"). `ASCII` is therefore a supported SPELLING of a set the standard also names; it is provided because other implementations spell it that way and a program that does is not otherwise portable. No runtime carrier is emitted for it.<br>**`EBCDIC` - IBM CCSID 37 (code page 037, "EBCDIC US/Canada").** *Coded character set:* the 256 characters of CCSID 37. *Ordinal number of characters:* 256; ordinal n is the character CCSID 37 assigns to code unit n-1. *Correspondence with the native alphanumeric character set:* the CCSID 37 code page itself - the whole table, derived at compile time from .NET's `Encoding.GetEncoding(37)` and never transcribed (`ImplementorCodeNames.SingleByteCodePage`). It is a bijection of the 256 code units onto exactly the 256 native characters U+0000-U+00FF. *Collating position of each character:* a character the page spells takes the position equal to its CCSID 37 code unit (so X'81' `a` &lt; X'C1' `A` &lt; X'F0' `0`, the reverse of the native order on both pairs). **Every OTHER native character** - the 65,280 UTF-16 code units above U+00FF that CCSID 37 does not spell - **takes a position greater than every specified one, in unchanged native relative order**: this implementation adopts 12.3.7.4 GR7 k3's own rule ("Any characters of the native collating sequence that are not specified in the literal phrase shall assume a position in the collating sequence that is greater than that of the highest character specified in this literal phrase. The relative order within the set of these unspecified characters is unchanged from the native collating sequence") as its GR7 i specification, so every native character has a position and none shares one. Those characters are NOT members of the coded character set: they have no ordinal and no medium representation, so no SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS or CLASS ordinal reaches them and a CODE-SET record containing one cannot be written (13.18.13.4 GR6 b). **HIGH-VALUE / LOW-VALUE under this sequence** (12.3.7.4 GR8/GR9): LOW-VALUE is the native character CCSID 37 puts at code unit X'00'; HIGH-VALUE is U+FFFF, the last character of the unspecified tail the GR7 k3 rule above places after the page's 256 (owner decision kb/Work R52 — the whole native repertoire, not the Latin-1 block, kb/Work PB1093). On a `CODE-SET IS EBCDIC` medium HIGH-VALUE is written as X'FF', the coded character set's highest code unit (owner decision kb/Work R51 item 4; `CodeSetConversion.HighUnit`), and X'FF' reads back as HIGH-VALUE. **Which EBCDIC**, surveyed rather than assumed: CCSID 37 is the canonical registered complete single-byte EBCDIC page and the z/OS default, i.e. the one the compiler whose users write `ALPHABET ... IS EBCDIC` means; GnuCOBOL's own default translation table corresponds to no registered CCSID and its named alternates are CCSID 500 variants, so following its LATITUDE (which names are accepted) does not mean adopting its table - none of its tables or sources are used here. CCSID 500 differs from 37 in five punctuation positions and is the obvious second row for whoever needs it. | `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb793_code_name_alphabets`; `conformance:cases/13.18.13-CODE-SET/pb793_code_set_ebcdic`; `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb793_code_name_alphabets_85` |
| DOC-A.1-184 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, code-name-1 and code-name-2 - the names supported for code-name-1 and code-name-2**, ISO 12.3.7.3 SR15, **optional** + documented-if-provided | **code-name-1: `ASCII` and `EBCDIC`. code-name-2: NONE.** SR15 - "The implementor shall specify the names supported for code-name-1 and code-name-2 in the ALPHABET clause, if any" - leaves the set to this implementation, and "if any" licenses an empty one in either class. The ALPHANUMERIC class is not empty (owner decision kb/Work PB793, following the surveyed model implementations where the standard leaves a point open and the vendors split); what each name MEANS is item **183**. The NATIONAL class IS empty and item **185** is therefore vacuous: the native national character set is the UTF-16 repertoire (determination D-N1) and the standard's own `UCS-4` / `UTF-8` / `UTF-16` keywords already name the ISO/IEC 10646 forms, so no national code-name would name a set that is not already reachable. The OTHER words that may stand alone in an alphabet definition are the general format's own keywords - `NATIVE`, `STANDARD-1`, `STANDARD-2` in the ALPHANUMERIC branch; `NATIVE`, `UCS-4`, `UTF-8`, `UTF-16` in the NATIONAL one; `LOCALE` in either - and the 12.3.7.4 GR10 figurative constants of a one-operand literal phrase. A word the source element declares as a constant-name is literal-1 of a literal phrase (13.10.3 SR2, kb/Work PB1942) and is never read as a code-name: ⚠ DETERMINATION — where one spelling could be both, the program's own declaration of the word wins over the implementor's system-name, the same answer the LOCALE clause's external-locale-name-1 gets (item 181). Any OTHER bare word is a source error, **COBOL1907** `alphabet-code-name`, whose message names the supported set from the table itself. &#x26D4; That refusal closes an under-rejection that was also a WRONG ANSWER: an unrecognized code-name used to be reinterpreted as a LITERAL PHRASE SPELLING OUT ITS OWN LETTERS, so `ALPHABET A-ASC IS ASCII` built an alphabet whose first four positions were A, S, C, I and every downstream reference (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, SORT, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS ... IN, CLASS ... IN, CODE-SET) read that (kb/Work PB770 leg e). The supported set is ONE table (`ImplementorCodeNames`), read by the binder, by the coded-character-set reference sites and by the diagnostic alike, so the names, their meanings and the message can never disagree. Witnesses, ONE PER CLASS plus the acceptance: `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb770-alphabet-unsupported-code-name` refuses a code-name-1 outside the set, `conformance-test:AlphabetLiteralPhraseTests.NationalUnsupportedCodeName_IsSR15` refuses code-name-2 on the empty national class, and `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb793_code_name_alphabets` accepts both supported spellings. | `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb770-alphabet-unsupported-code-name`; `conformance-test:AlphabetLiteralPhraseTests.NationalUnsupportedCodeName_IsSR15`; `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb793_code_name_alphabets`; `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb793_code_name_alphabets_85` |
| DOC-A.1-185 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, code-name-2 - the national coded character set and collating sequence, the ordinal number of characters, and the correspondence with the native national character set**, ISO 12.3.7.4 GR7 j, **conditionally required** ("conditioned upon the existence of a code-name") + documented | **VACUOUS - there is no code-name-2.** A.1 conditions this item "upon the existence of a code-name", and A.1 item 184 records the national half of the SR15 set as empty, so there is no national coded character set, no ordinal numbering and no native correspondence for this item to describe. It is stated rather than omitted because the condition is a DECISION (kb/Work PB793) that could change: the code-name table is keyed by class and the binder asks it for both, so a national row would wake this item without a code change. The refusal that proves the class is empty is the witness. | `conformance-test:AlphabetLiteralPhraseTests.NationalUnsupportedCodeName_IsSR15` |
| DOC-A.1-188 | **SPECIAL-NAMES ALPHABET clause, UCS-4, UTF-8 and UTF-16 phrases — correspondence with the native character set**, §12.3.7.4 GR7, required + documented | The native alphanumeric and national repertoires are **UTF-16, one code unit per character position** (the D-N1 substrate). The UTF-16 phrase's correspondence with the native set is therefore the **BMP identity** — code point = code unit, and §8.5.1.4's denial of surrogate-pair recognition makes the supplementary-plane codepoint/code-unit divergence unreachable. **UTF-8 and UTF-16 name coded character sets ONLY** — Table 6 leaves their collating-sequence column empty, and GR7 g/h give each only a correspondence — so naming one where a collating sequence is required (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, SORT/MERGE, a file COLLATING SEQUENCE) is a syntax-rule violation. **UCS-4 names BOTH** (Table 6 row UCS-4, and GR7 f: “The collating sequence referenced by the UCS-4 phrase shall be defined by the order in which characters appear in ISO/IEC 10646”); on the one-code-unit-per-position D-N1 substrate that ISO/IEC 10646 appearance order over the 65,536 single-position characters **is code-unit order**, i.e. the NATIVE national sequence, and §8.5.1.4’s denial of surrogate-pair recognition puts the only place the two could diverge out of reach. UTF-8’s external form is converted to/from the native UTF-16 form at a codec boundary. `CollatingModel` carries this split (`HasCollatingSequence` false for exactly UTF-8 and UTF-16). **A supplementary character named by a NUMERIC ordinal under a CLASS clause's `IN` phrase** (`CLASS C FOR NATIONAL IS n IN alphabet-name-4`, alphabet-name-4 UCS-4 or UTF-8) is a legal operand (SR17 c2: the ordinal exists in the IN set), it is one character (SR17 c4 speaks of national LITERALS only), and outside a THROUGH phrase its two UTF-16 code units are members of the class; but under a THROUGH phrase GR12 expands "the contiguous characters in the native character set" between the bounds, and a character that needs two code units has no position in the native set's run — the specification says nothing for that pair, so this implementation REFUSES it, under its own message naming GR12 (never under c4), rather than invent a run over code points the national substrate cannot hold (implementor-defined, kb/Work PB1091). | `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/l1_alphabet_ucs4_utf8_utf16_correspondence` |
| DOC-A.1-189 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, device-name (names available, restrictions on use)**, ISO 12.3.7.3 SR7 and SR8, **optional** + documented-if-provided | **Provided. The device-names are `CONSOLE`, `SYSIN`, `SYSOUT` and `SYSERR`**: `CONSOLE` = the process standard input (ACCEPT) and standard output (DISPLAY); `SYSIN` = standard input only; `SYSOUT` = standard output only; `SYSERR` = standard error, output only. SR8 - "The implementor shall specify the names that are available for switch-name-1, feature-name-1, and device-name-1" - is answered by ONE table, `ImplementorNames` (`src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/ImplementorNames.cs`), which is also the answer to items **190** and **191**; a SPECIAL-NAMES entry naming anything else is **COBOL2241** (kb/Work PB862), whose message lists the available names FROM the table. ⛔ Before that table `SPECIAL-NAMES. WIBBLE WOBBLE.` compiled and registered a mnemonic naming nothing, and a misspelled `CONSOEL IS PRT` surfaced only at the DISPLAY that used it, as a device 'CONSOEL' that "is not capable of receiving data". **Restrictions on use** (SR7's "additional restrictions"): a device's mnemonic-name-3 may be the FROM operand of ACCEPT only when the device has input capability and the UPON operand of DISPLAY only when it has output capability (`COBOL0817`, §14.9.1.3 SR2 / §14.9.11.3 SR2); by SR7 itself it may appear in no other statement - `SET` refuses it (`COBOL1757`, §14.9.39.3 SR5) and `WRITE ... ADVANCING` refuses it (`COBOL2243`, §14.9.51.3 SR16). Item **2** and item **59** state the default devices. | `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb862_implementor_names`; `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb862-unavailable-device-name`; `unit:ImplementorNamesDriftTests.EveryTableName_IsDocumented_AndNamedByTheDiagnostic` |
| DOC-A.1-190 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, feature-name (names available, any positioning rules, any restrictions on use)**, ISO 12.3.7.3 SR6 and SR8, **optional** + documented-if-provided | **Provided. The feature-names are `C01` and `CSP`**, and their only use is as the ADVANCING operand of a WRITE statement (SR6; §14.9.51.3 SR16). **Positioning rules** (§14.9.51.4 GR25 d - item **222**): `C01` - skip to channel 1, the top of the next page, which is exactly the `ADVANCING PAGE` advance of the same statement; `CSP` - suppress spacing, a ZERO-line advance: exactly ADVANCING 0's overprint of the same statement, written as a bare carriage return (§3 "DETERMINATION — ADVANCING 0 is an overprint"). ⚖ Surveyed (owner-decision protocol, `follow_gnucobol_on_split_latitude`): IBM Enterprise COBOL, Micro Focus and GnuCOBOL all spell both names with these meanings. Channels 2-12 (`C02`-`C12`) are **not** provided: each names a stop on a physical carriage-control tape, and a line-sequential print file has no forms-control model to position against. **Restrictions on use**: none beyond SR6 - a feature's mnemonic in ACCEPT or DISPLAY is `COBOL0817`, in SET `COBOL1757`; a WRITE whose file has a LINAGE clause may not name one (§14.9.51.3 SR13). A name outside the table is **COBOL2241** (item **189** carries the one-table rule). The NIST SQ207M placeholder `XXXXX073` is supplied as `CSP` by the NIST preprocessor, preserving the zero-line advance its golden encodes. | `conformance-test:FileIoDifferentialTests.WriteAdvancingC01_IsThePageAdvance`; `conformance-test:FileIoDifferentialTests.WriteAdvancingMnemonic_ZeroLineAdvance_RecordAlwaysReleased`; `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb862-write-advancing-device-mnemonic` |
| DOC-A.1-191 | **SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, switch-name (names available, which switches may be referenced by the SET statement, scope of, and external facility for modification)**, ISO 8.3.2.3.11 and 12.3.7.3 SR8, 12.3.7.4 GR2-GR4, **optional** + documented-if-provided | **Provided. The switch-names are `SWITCH-0` through `SWITCH-36` (GnuCOBOL's set) and `UPSI-0` through `UPSI-7` (IBM's User Program Status Indicators).** Every one may be referenced by the SET statement (GR3). The **scope** of every switch is the RUN UNIT - one switch shared by every runtime element (GR4 and its NOTE 1). The **external facility** that supplies a switch's initial status is the process environment variable `COBOL_<SWITCH-NAME>` with hyphens as underscores (`SWITCH-1` -> `COBOL_SWITCH_1`): `ON`, `1` or `TRUE` (any case) means on, anything else or absent means off; the value is read at the first interrogation and a later SET governs for the rest of the run unit (`SwitchStore`; an absent or empty variable is read as off and latched exactly like a present one, so a change to the environment after the first interrogation never changes a switch-status condition, and the closed name set is written once, `SwitchStore.Names`). Only a switch-name may carry ON STATUS / OFF STATUS condition-names, in either order, each at most once (§12.3.7.2 choice indicators, §5.2.6.4); a device-name or feature-name written with one is **COBOL2241**, because a system-name belongs to exactly one type (§8.3.2.3.1). A name outside the table is COBOL2241 too (item **189** carries the one-table rule). ⚖ Before kb/Work PB862 ANY word was accepted as a switch-name - a determination that could not stand beside a device-name set, since §8.3.2.3.1 forbids a name belonging to two types. | `conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb862_implementor_names`; `conformance-test:AlterSwitchesDifferentialTests.Switch_EnvironmentVariableSuppliesInitialState`; `unit:ImplementorNamesDriftTests.EveryTableName_IsAccepted_InTheArmItsKindAllows`; `unit:SwitchStoreTests.AnAbsentVariable_LatchesOff_AtTheFirstInterrogation` |

The page is advanced per the feature-name's row in `ImplementorNames`: `C01` advances exactly as `ADVANCING PAGE` does in the same position (BEFORE or AFTER); `CSP` advances zero lines. | `conformance-test:FileIoDifferentialTests.WriteAdvancingC01_IsThePageAdvance`; `conformance-test:FileIoDifferentialTests.WriteAdvancingMnemonic_ZeroLineAdvance_RecordAlwaysReleased` |
| DOC-A.1-123 | **Native arithmetic — techniques used, intermediate data item**, §8.8.1.3 / §11.9.5 / §14.7.7, required (the internal procedure need not be documented) | **The native intermediate data item is a scaled `Int128`** — a 128-bit two's-complement integer holding the unscaled value with a compile-time decimal scale (magnitude bound ≈ 1.7 × 10^38; every ≤ 31-digit operand and every aligned sum of them is exact). Any expression with a floating-point operand — or whose resultant identifiers are all floating-point — evaluates entirely in IEEE binary64 instead (that binary64 intermediate IS the arithmetic value §14.7.4.3 rounds into a floating-point resultant: a binary64 resultant holds it unchanged under every ROUNDED mode, a binary32 one takes the mode's neighbour, and an exact scaled or SDIDI value is rounded into either format ONCE — kb/Work PB1196); **a nested quotient carries its operands' precision plus 14 guard fraction digits, truncated, and rounds once, at the final transfer** (§14.7.7 rule 3 NOTE 1). The precision is the receiver's scale or the fraction digits the quotient's operands carry, whichever is larger, and never the guard digits an earlier quotient added, so it is the same at every depth of the expression (kb/Work PB3538: the guard used to be added to the dividend's SCALE, which for a nested quotient already held 14 guard digits, so `COMPUTE R = A / B / B / B / B` compounded it 14, 28, 42 until a value of 0.5 ended the run unit with EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW). The quotient is on the scaled `Int128` while its digit bound (the dividend's integer digits, plus the divisor's fraction digits, plus the working scale) fits the carrier, and the SAME truncated quotient on the exact 256-bit form (`CobolWide.DivTruncated`) while that bound fits 77 digits, so the lane is a representation and never changes the value (kb/Work PB3538's review finding R1-1: a dividend of unknown bound, an intrinsic's value, took the SDIDI's round-to-odd and `FUNCTION INTEGER(X) / 7 * 7` stored 2.000000 where `X / 7 * 7` stores 1.999999; `pb3538_unbounded_operand_quotients`). Past 77 digits, and beside an operand the SDIDI carries (a product of two intrinsic values, 39 + 39 digits; a floating-point literal; a power), the quotient is STILL that truncated quotient, held to the SDIDI's 34 significant digits by round-to-odd (`CobolDec.DivTruncatedToOdd`), so one of at most 34 digits is exact and equal to the other lanes' (review finding R2-1: the SDIDI's own quotient of the exact value, rounded at 34 digits, made the product above it round back up, and `FUNCTION INTEGER(X) * FUNCTION INTEGER(Y) / 7 * 7`, `FUNCTION INTEGER(X) * Y20 / 7 * 7` and `2.0E0 / 7 * 7` stored 2.000000; `pb3538_sdidi_lane_quotients`). Every lane also carries its operands' fraction digits, so the working scale of the next quotient does not depend on the lane either. **An operand's fraction digits are the places it is WRITTEN or DECLARED at, whatever its notation**, never the 0 of a scale an SDIDI value does not have and never a count that depends on its value (review findings R3-1 and R4-1): an item's are its declared scale, a fixed-point literal's and a floating-point literal's their written scale (a floating-point literal's significand places less its exponent, known at compile time: `2.50E0` has the 2 of `2.50` and of a `PIC 9V99` item, `1.0E-15` the 16 of `0.0000000000000010`), a NUMVAL-family value's its argument's written places (`NUMVAL ("2.50")` has 2), and a value an operation formed (a power formed on the SDIDI, a function's returned value) the places its result is held at (an exact sum or product keeps its operands', a ZERO operand's places and a zero result's included, as §8.8.1.5.3's ISO/IEC 60559 5.4.1 operations hold every exact result at the preferred exponent, so `FUNCTION ABS (Z + FUNCTION NUMVAL ("2.5"))` with `Z PIC 9V999 VALUE 0` has the 3 places it has when Z is 0.001 (review finding R5-1: the sum with a zero term was held at the other operand's places, and the outcome of a relation over it flipped on Z's value; `pb3538_zero_operand_precision`); a result the SDIDI rounded holds its 34 significant digits; a binary64 approximation, such as a floating-math function's value or NUMVAL-F's under native arithmetic, the places of its shortest round-trip decimal). The last two are known only at run time and are carried with the value through the sums, differences, products, negations and quotients above it (`CobolDecWithPrecision`), so `IF FUNCTION NUMVAL ("0.000000000000001") / 2 > 0`, `IF 10 ** -15 / 2 > 0` and `IF 1.0E-15 / 2 > 0` are GREATER (they were truncated at 14 places, to zero), `2.50 / 3 * 1000000000000000`, `2.50E0 / 3 * 1000000000000000` and `FUNCTION NUMVAL ("2.50") / 3 * 1000000000000000` are equal and GREATER than 833333333333333 (counting significant digits dropped the trailing zero and made the last two equal to it), and the working scale is the same at every depth (`pb3538_runtime_precision_quotients`, `pb3538_float_literal_precision`, `pb3538_written_precision`). As for a fixed-point operand, the written scale decides: `2.5E0 / 3 * 1000000000000000` is truncated one place sooner than the `2.50` spelling and equals 833333333333333. The working scale is one rule, `CobolNum.NestedQuotientScale`, applied at compile time and at run time alike. So a nested quotient raises the size error condition only for a zero divisor, or for a VALUE outside the range where it lands. The truncating quotient follows GnuCOBOL (CLAUDE.md rule 1), whose `cob_decimal_div` truncates and whose products and sums above it are exact: `2 / 7 * 7` into `PIC S9(9)V9(6)` is 1.999999 (`pb60_nested_configuration_inheritance`'s ARITH2 leg), where the SDIDI of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL gives 2.000000. Pinned by `pb3538_chained_division_native` (`A / B / B / B / B` with and without ON SIZE ERROR, three quotients multiplied, a relation, depth-10 chains), `pb3538_chained_division_standard_decimal` `pb3538_unbounded_operand_products` and `pb3538_unbounded_operand_quotients`, and held depth-independent by `NestedQuotientPrecisionDriftTests`. **A floating-point operand means a floating-point ITEM, a floating-point carrier literal or a floating-point receiver** — a floating-math function's returned value and a non-integer native power are engine-produced approximations (item 92), not operands "described with" a float usage, so beside non-float operands they join the arithmetic through their shortest-round-trip decimal and the SDIDI lane (kb/Work PB1641; `pb1641_function_result_beside_decimal_operands`). **The scaled `Int128` is used for a product only where the operands' DIGIT BOUNDS prove it fits** (the PICTURE's digit count for an item — a COMP-5 item owns its whole container range — and the digit count of a literal; the exact sum, difference and product of bounded operands are bounded in turn): N unscaled digits times M unscaled digits is below 10^(N+M), so N+M ≤ 38 is a bare multiply, N+M > 38 forms the exact 256-bit product — **and when that product IS the final transfer to a resultant (a single-receiver COMPUTE, MULTIPLY BY, MULTIPLY GIVING, and each receiver of a several-receiver MULTIPLY GIVING or COMPUTE whose right-hand side is a product) it is rounded ONCE, at that resultant's scale with that resultant's own mode (`CobolDec.MulAtScale`)**, whatever width the resultant is: a 16-byte COMP-5 item owns a 38-digit container (A.1 item 208), so its ROUNDED phrase — PROHIBITED included — must see every digit of a 38-digit product, and the SDIDI's 34 would hide them (kb/Work PB1143's review finding N1: `COMPUTE R5 = E * F` of two 20-digit operands into `PIC S9(31) COMP-5` stored …5370000 for …5361999). A product past the Int128 carrier at that scale is, checked, the size error EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION (§14.7.5 case 3; the receiver is unchanged) and, unchecked, keeps the low-order 38 digits a store can use — the same two dispositions as an SDIDI value's final transfer. **A product NESTED in a larger expression** (`A * B - C * D`, a relation operand) is not a transfer, and it keeps EVERY digit (kb/Work PB1900): it is formed EXACTLY as a 256-bit scaled integer (`CobolWide`) whenever the operands' digit bounds prove the exact value fits 77 decimal digits, the sums, differences and negations above it stay exact on that form, and the value is rounded ONCE, at the final transfer into the resultant — with that resultant's scale and mode, whatever its width — or, where there is no such transfer (a receiver-less operand, a floating-point resultant), lowered to the SDIDI by ROUND-TO-ODD (an inexact value keeps an odd last digit, so a receiver of at most 32 digit positions, which every PICTURE-limited one is (§13.18.40.3 SR14 caps them at 31), rounds it in every ROUNDED mode and PROHIBITED exactly as it would round the exact value). A relation compares two such operands exactly (§8.8.4.2.4 compares algebraic values), and a several-receiver COMPUTE's one initial evaluation is kept exact and rounded per receiver. This follows GnuCOBOL (CLAUDE.md rule 1), whose `cob_decimal_mul`, `cob_decimal_add` and `cob_decimal_sub` are exact over an arbitrary-precision integer (libcob/numeric.c): `COMPUTE R = A * B - C * D` over `PIC 9(21)` operands is exactly 1, where the 34-digit intermediate it replaced stored 10000000 (`conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb1900_nested_product_cancellation`). **An arithmetic expression that is a FUNCTION ARGUMENT keeps the same exact wide form, and the exact function family evaluates on it (kb/Work PB3953).** Under native arithmetic the standard fixes no width (§8.8.1.3: native arithmetic is "an implementor-defined method of evaluating … all integer and numeric functions"; §15.4.1: "the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor"), so for that latitude CLAUDE.md rule 1 makes GnuCOBOL's behaviour the answer, and its function-argument temporary is arbitrary-precision (the PB3514 `cobc` 3.2.0 probe of `ABS (BIG * BIG * BIG)` ends `…2999999999999999999`, and so does this compiler). An argument whose digit bound passes the `Int128` window reaches the function as the exact 256-bit intermediate (`IntrinsicRenderer.RawWideArg`, a registered settling site of `ExactWideSettlementDriftTests`), and ABS, SIGN, INTEGER, INTEGER-PART, FRACTION-PART, MOD, REM, MAX, MIN, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, SUM, RANGE, MEDIAN and MIDRANGE evaluate on it (`IntrinsicRenderer.RenderWide`, `CobolIntrinsics.*Wide`) whenever the arguments' digit bounds prove the work fits 77 digits (each argument aligned to the common scale, plus a digit per tenfold argument count for SUM, nine for a table(ALL) argument, one for RANGE and INTEGER, two for MEDIAN's and MIDRANGE's exact halving); a §15.3 type-6 argument takes its integer on the same form (`CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArgWide`), so MOD and REM see every digit of the dividend. The value they return is itself a wide value where it can be as wide as an argument, settled like a nested product: rounded once into a fixed-point resultant, compared exactly by a relation, kept by a function above it, shown whole by DISPLAY (`FunctionValueField.OfWide`, whose MAX, MIN and MEDIAN order two values exactly where their 34-digit images agree), transferred at the receiver's scale by a MOVE (`NumericRenderer.TransferWide`, whose high-order truncation keeps the value's own low-order digits, §14.6.8.2 4), and sent whole as text by a MOVE to an alphanumeric item or a STRING (`OperandText`, `CobolNum.FormatWideFunctionText`). With `BIG PIC 9(18)` holding 999999999999999999 and `K3 PIC 999` 999, `FUNCTION ABS (BIG * BIG * K3)` shows `998999999999999998002000000000000000999`, `FUNCTION MOD (BIG * BIG * K3, 1000)` is 999, `FUNCTION MAX (BIG * BIG * K3, BIG * BIG * K3 + 1)` is the second argument, and `MOVE FUNCTION INTEGER (BIG * BIG * K3) TO R` stores `9999999998002000000000000000999` into `PIC S9(31)` (`pb3953_function_argument_int128_window`). An SDIDI or binary64 argument beside it keeps its own lane (the wide argument then enters as its round-to-odd image, as beside a nested product in an expression). MEAN divides the EXACT wide sum once, on the SDIDI (`CobolIntrinsics.MeanWide`; §15.60.4 1, the SDIDI quotient in every mode, kb/Work PB3860): `FUNCTION MEAN (BIG * BIG * K3, 1)` shows `499499999999999999001000000000000000000`, one rounding of the exact `…000500`, where the image divided afterwards rounded twice (kb/Work PB4075). The binary64 family takes the exact wide value wherever its body is ill-conditioned: SIN, COS and TAN reduce the 39-to-77-digit angle itself modulo π/2 (`CobolIntrinsics.SinWide`; `FUNCTION SIN (BIG * BIG * K3)` is 0.9325597113900649…, not the sine of the image, which is some 999 radians away), and LOG, LOG10, ACOS and ASIN form x − 1 and 1 − abs(x) on the exact value, so a wide argument 10^−34 from 1 or −1 keeps its distance. EXP, EXP10 and SQRT take the image, because a 34-digit relative error cannot reach the last bit of a result whose condition number is at most 709, 709 and ½ (`pb4075_wide_argument_consumers`). Under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` the 34-digit SDIDI IS the value, rounded by the intermediate rounding mode (the same ABS shows `998999999999999998002000000000000000000`; §8.8.1.5.2: "a maximum precision of 34 decimal digits"; §15.4.1 1: the returned value equals that of the equivalent arithmetic expression). The DETERMINATION'S LIMITS: a nested product whose digit bound passes 77 is formed on the SDIDI (reduced to 34 significant digits by round-to-odd — a compound expression whose intermediates exceed 34 digits there is this item's determination, never a claim of exactness), a nested quotient whose digit bound passes 77 is the truncated quotient held to 34 digits by round-to-odd, a final-transfer quotient above a wide value is formed on the SDIDI by round-to-odd (GnuCOBOL's own divide is inexact: `shift_decimal` then a truncating `mpz_tdiv_q`, numeric.c:2259-2261), and an exponentiation enters on the SDIDI; and an operand of unknown bound (an intrinsic's value, a windowed view) is bounded by the `Int128` that carries it, 39 digits, the bound a 16-byte container already has, so its product takes the same exact arms; the checked multiply it used to take at the summed scale raised the size error condition when the SCALE left the carrier, not the value (three `FUNCTION MEAN` values of scale 18, 5.36 at scale 54, kb/Work PB3538) — a native product never wraps (kb/Work PB1143; `PIC 9V9(30)` times `PIC 9V9(30)` is legal because §14.7.7 r2 a) caps the COMPOSITE, not the unscaled product, and GnuCOBOL's arbitrary-precision decimal gives the exact product). The DIVIDE kernel's radix alignment never wraps either: a dividend that scales up past the carrier is formed on the exact 256-bit numerator and the quotient rounds ONCE by its true remainder (`CobolDec.QuotientAtScale`, so a 38-digit quotient reaches a 16-byte COMP-5 receiver whole — `pb1143_quotient_into_wide_receiver`); only a divisor scaled past the carrier, or an alignment past 10^38, takes the SDIDI (34 digits, round-to-odd); and a quotient past the carrier is EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW. The statistics functions SUM / RANGE / MEAN / MEDIAN / MIDRANGE align their arguments to a common scale; when the arguments' digit bounds show that alignment can leave the carrier the function is evaluated on the SDIDI instead (kb/Work PB621; `pb621_statistics_beyond_the_aligned_carrier`), so a value the receiver holds is never refused for the carrier's width — an argument of unknown bound keeps the escape-checked native arm (item 179), and MOD / REM keep it too (their value is a difference of nearly equal magnitudes that the 34-digit SDIDI cannot always carry, so they refuse loudly rather than answer an approximation). One value — the maximum of an unsigned 16-byte COMP-5 item, 2^128−1 — exceeds the intermediate range while being storable in an item; see item 179 for what an arithmetic reference to it does. | `conformance:cases/11.9.5-ARITHMETIC/l1_native_arithmetic_intermediate`; | DOC-A.1-70 | **Fatal exception condition — whether execution continues, and how a numeric receiving operand is affected, when checking for the condition is NOT enabled: the arithmetic size error condition without a SIZE ERROR phrase (EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, §14.7.5 no-phrase rule 4) and a non-finite value in a fixed-point landing (EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE)**, §14.6.13.1.3 item 8, required + documented (this row discharges the numeric-store family; other fatal conditions' dispositions are documented with their statements) | **Execution continues with the next statement, and the resultant identifier receives the LOW-ORDER digits of the result aligned at its scale** — the classic high-order truncation (`CobolNum.Store`), for EVERY value carrier: the standard-decimal intermediate (`CobolDec.ToUnscaled`, kb/Work PB74), the native scaled-`Int128` lane (`CobolNum.RescaleStoreCap` — the widening `CobolNum.Store` and `CobolEdit.Format` take, and the unchecked arm of the exact family's `CobolIntrinsics.Rescaled`, and the §14.2.3 GR9/GR10 CALL-argument landing `CobolArgAdapt.Land`; kb/Work PB288, whose crossing IS "a COMPUTE statement without the ROUNDED phrase" into a record of the formal's description and so takes this same no-phrase disposition, where it used to wrap the `Int128` intermediate in binary; and the same crossing into a FLOATING-POINT formal, which lands through `FloatResultant` — `CobolArgAdapt.LandFloat`, kb/Work PB1114 — under implied TRUNCATION, a value past the format's range landing at its largest finite value unchecked and raising EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION under checking), and a binary64 (`CobolFloat.ToScaledUnchecked` / `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble`'s unchecked form — the exact decimal expansion past the Int128 carrier; kb/Work PB77, 2026-08-18), and the unsigned-wide `UInt128` carrier of a 16-byte unsigned COMP-5 item, whose full container value lands in a numeric-edited receiver through `CobolNum.RescaleStoreCapU` (its low-order 38 digits at the receiver's scale, which the edit then truncates to the picture; kb/Work PB2163, golden `pb2163_unsigned_wide_into_edited`). Before PB77 a value past the carrier landed the saturation SENTINEL and the store kept its low digits: `COMPUTE X5 = D40` (a COMP-2 holding 1.0E+40, PIC 9(5)) stored 03715 — the low digits of `Int128.MaxValue` — where the result's are 90752. A non-finite binary64 (NaN, ±Infinity) landing in a fixed-point receiver with checking off stores ZERO. "Low-order digits" is a DECIMAL statement for a DISPLAY / COMP / PACKED receiver and the CONTAINER's two's-complement residue for a BinaryCapacity one (COMP-5 / the BINARY-CHAR family, A.1 item 208 / §13.18.60.4 GR12); it is never the Int128 carrier's own binary wrap taken modulo the picture. Until kb/Work PB639 (2026-09-05) the inline arithmetic store and the MOVE composed exactly those two — the alignment multiplied inside the carrier and only THEN met the decimal capacity — so `COMPUTE WC = 1000000000000000000000000000000` into `PIC S9(9)V9(9)` stored −123822295.304634368 where 10^39's low-order 18 digits are all zero; the determination and the code had disagreed on this row's own primary path since it was written. The other resultant identifiers of a multiple-receiver statement are stored normally. **A statement written with ONLY a NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase** goes to the same no-phrase rules (§14.7.5: with a size error condition and no SIZE ERROR phrase "processing proceeds as specified in 14.6.13.1.3 ... If a NOT SIZE ERROR phrase is specified, it is ignored"), so its NOT imperative does not run on a size error and runs when none occurred (the clause's closing paragraph). How its receivers are affected, and whether execution continues, is item 8's latitude, and here WiseOwl COBOL follows GnuCOBOL (CLAUDE.md rule 1): GnuCOBOL 3.2 keeps a resultant that would overflow UNCHANGED whenever the statement carries a SIZE ERROR or a NOT SIZE ERROR phrase (`cobc/typeck.c`: "There is a [NOT] ERROR/OVERFLOW/EXCEPTION" sets `COB_STORE_KEEP_ON_OVERFLOW`; the one exception is a COMP-5, COMP-X or COMP-N receiver of a NOT-only statement, which GnuCOBOL stores as if no phrase were written (its `build_store_option` sets the flag for those usages only with ON SIZE ERROR), an optimization that contradicts GnuCOBOL's own rule; WiseOwl COBOL keeps those receivers too, by the owner's decision that the exemption is GnuCOBOL's error, kb/Work PB3989), and the CCVS85 programs NC106A, NC170A-NC173A, NC175A-NC177A, NC202A, NC203A, NC251A and NC253A expect the same. So with checking off such a statement continues, every resultant that meets a size error keeps its value (the others store as they would have, §14.7.5 rule 2), a zero divisor leaves the resultants unchanged and continues, and the NOT imperative is skipped: `ADD 1 TO X NOT ON SIZE ERROR ...` with X `PIC 9 VALUE 9` keeps 9 (kb/Work PB3869, retired: the fuzz finding read "ignored" as fixing the receivers too, and the merge queue's CCVS run refuted it). **DIVIDE ... GIVING identifier-3 REMAINDER identifier-4 after a QUOTIENT size error** (kb/Work PB3975): §14.9.12.4 6) c) develops the subsidiary quotient and stores the remainder only "If the size error condition is not raised". With an ON SIZE ERROR phrase, or EC-SIZE checking enabled, identifier-4 is therefore unchanged (ISO decides; GnuCOBOL 3.2 stores it even then). With checking off and NO SIZE ERROR phrase the condition is item 8's, and WiseOwl COBOL follows GnuCOBOL 3.2 (libcob `cob_div_quotient` / `cob_div_remainder`): the quotient stores its low-order digits and the remainder IS stored, formed from the quotient truncated at identifier-3's decimal point location with EVERY integer digit (`DIVIDE 1003 BY 4 GIVING B REMAINDER R`, B `PIC 99`, R `PIC 999`: B = 50, R = 003, never 1003 - 50 x 4 = 803; the subsidiary quotient carries no digit cap, `ArithmeticEmitter.SubsidiaryShape`). A statement with ONLY a NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase keeps every receiver of the size error as the ON phrase does (above), and its remainder takes that same disposition: unchanged, where GnuCOBOL stores 003 exactly as it does under its ON phrase. ⛔ **THE NOT-ENABLED DISPOSITION IS PER CONDITION NAME** (kb/Work PB4092, PB4093; §14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3: "An exception condition is set to exist only if checking for that condition is enabled"). Checking enabled for ONE EC-SIZE name is checking for THAT name: every size condition the statement does not enable takes the disposition above — in an arithmetic statement, in a condition, an argument or a subscript, and in a report compose (whose enablement is the PRESENTING GENERATE's or TERMINATE's). With EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, -UNDERFLOW, -ZERO-DIVIDE, -EXPONENTIATION or -ADDRESS enabled alone, a result further from zero than its receiver holds is no-phrase rule 4's EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, which is not enabled, so the receiver receives the low-order digits (`COMPUTE C = A * A`, A = 100, C `PIC 999` holding 7: 000; it used to stay 007, the disposition of a statement with a SIZE ERROR phrase). With EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION enabled alone, a binary64 intermediate past its range (`IF D * D > 0`, D COMP-2 holding 1.0E200) is EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, which is not enabled, so the intermediate is the IEEE value (+Infinity; 0 for a nonzero result that rounds to zero, EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW) and execution continues; it used to raise EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW and end the run unit. A zero divisor and an exponentiation-rule violation are raised by every kernel, checked or not, so with their own name not enabled they terminate the run unit exactly as with checking off (below). A statement WITH a SIZE ERROR phrase takes every condition (§14.7.5). The table is `SizeChecks` (`EcState.SizeCheckRows`, pinned by `SizeChecksDriftTests`): the checked operators (`CobolFloat.AddChecked` and its siblings, `CobolNum.AddChecked` / `SubChecked`) take the conditions enabled, and the checked LANDING (`TryStore`, `RescaleChecked`, `ToScaled`) is chosen only where EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION is. **An INTERMEDIATE that cannot be formed at all** — a standard-decimal intermediate past decimal128 (§14.7.5 case 7 / no-phrase rule 3, `10 ** 100000`), a native value past the Int128 escape boundary in a value-semantics position (case 5, item 179 (3)), an exponentiation-rule violation (case 1), a zero divisor (case 2) — **has no result to store: with checking not enabled execution does NOT continue; the run unit terminates abnormally** ("abnormal run-unit termination: EC-SIZE-… (fatal): …", exit 1 — kb/Work PB75, 2026-08-18; it used to be an unhandled .NET stack trace, exit 127), whether the raise came from an arithmetic statement without a phrase or from a condition / argument / subscript. ⛔ **The zero divisor is raised by EVERY value lane's quotient kernel, checked or not** (kb/Work PB1605): `CobolNum.Divide` (the scaled `Int128` carrier), `CobolFloat.Div` (binary64 — the unchecked arm of `NumericRenderer.CombineReal`) and `CobolDec.Div` (the standard-decimal intermediate) all throw the one `CobolSizeError.ZeroDivide()`, because §14.7.5 case 2 is the condition whether or not checking is enabled and checking decides only its disposition. Until PB1605 the first two answered with checking off — `COMPUTE A = B / Z` stored 000 and `COMPUTE FR = FL / FZ` stored +Infinity (NaN for 0 / 0), and the run went on — so the code contradicted this row on the scaled and binary64 lanes while the SDIDI lane already terminated. Survey under the owner's precedence (ISO → GnuCOBOL → IBM / Micro Focus; §14.6.13.1.3 item 8 is the latitude): GnuCOBOL 3.2 continues with the resultant unchanged (its decimal divide marks the quotient not-a-number and the store skips it), but its own source flags that handling as a known defect whose intended behaviour is to abort on the fatal condition — so that rung offers no settled model, and this row's family determination (termination, which the SDIDI zero divisor and the exponentiation-rule violation already took) stands for the zero divisor on every lane. Pinned by `SizeErrorDispositionTests.ZeroDivisor_CheckingOff_TerminatesNamingEcSizeZeroDivide` (both native lanes, COMPUTE / DIVIDE INTO / DIVIDE GIVING REMAINDER / a nested quotient / a condition, and the SDIDI lane), its phrase-path control, and `ZeroDivisorLaneTests`. With checking enabled the §14.6.13.1.3 #4/#5/#7 path applies to those statements exactly as to arithmetic ones (golden `pb75_sdidi_overflow_outside_arithmetic`, `SizeErrorDispositionTests`). With the phrase or with EC-SIZE checking enabled the disposition is §14.7.5's own — the receiver is left unchanged and the size error condition is processed — because the CHECKED landing raises the size error past the carrier (item 179, kb/Work PB13, PB2967). ⛔ **The §14.2.3 GR9/GR10 ARGUMENT CROSSING takes that checked disposition IN THE ACTIVATING ELEMENT** (kb/Work PB640): GR9's second branch and GR10 allocate the linkage record "by the activating runtime element during the process of initiating the activation", so the crossing's COMPUTE runs under the ACTIVATING element's `>>TURN EC-SIZE` state — with checking on, a value further from zero than the formal's description permits raises EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION there (`CobolArgAdapt.LandForFormal` → `CobolNum.StoreOrRaise`), the activating element's USE declaratives run, and §14.9.4.4 GR3 g) does NOT transfer control, so the callee never executes. With checking OFF the low-order digits above stand. The same rule and the same two dispositions cover the INVOKE lane (§14.2.3 GR9's "a method"; §14.8.2.3.3 rule 2 a)), whose landing was already caller-side but unconditionally the unchecked one. ⛔ **ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED is asked by every final transfer's own rounding decision** (kb/Work PB647, PB3990): a final transfer lands AT the resultant identifier's scale, so the store's rescale is the identity and only the landing sees the discarded fraction; the scaled carrier's `CobolNum.BumpsMagnitude`, the SDIDI's `CobolDec.RoundFromRemainder`, `FloatResultant` and `CobolEdit`'s floating-point store raise `CobolSizeError.ProhibitedInexact` (EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION) there, or a Try form answers false, in the checked and the unchecked form alike. Before PB647 the condition depended on the receiver's SCALE rather than on the transfer's exactness: the same statement raised into `PIC 9V9` and stored silently into `PIC 9V9(9)`. ⛔ **ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED with checking NOT enabled and no SIZE ERROR phrase** (kb/Work PB3990, reversing PB1196's truncation): §14.7.4.3 rule 7 — "the EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION exception condition is set to exist, the size error condition exists, and the content of the resultant identifier is unchanged" — keeps the resultant whether or not checking is enabled, and with checking off §14.6.13.1.3 item 8 leaves only whether and how execution continues to the implementor. WiseOwl COBOL's determination, for a fixed-point AND a floating-point resultant alike, every usage and every arithmetic statement: execution CONTINUES with the next resultant identifier and then the next statement, and the resultant that met the condition keeps its value (`COMPUTE N ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED = -2.5` into `PIC S9` and 0.1 into a FLOAT-SHORT both leave the receiver as it was; GnuCOBOL 3.2 keeps a fixed-point receiver the same way, and CLAUDE.md rule 1 would follow it even if rule 7 were read as item-8 latitude). The emitted statement catches that one condition around the receiver's compute-and-store (`ArithmeticEmitter.KeepsOnProhibitedInexact`), and a report printable item's implicit COMPUTE (§13.18.53.4 GR2 / §13.18.54.4 GR4, which has no SIZE ERROR phrase and takes the checking of the GENERATE or TERMINATE that prints the item, kb/Work PB4031) takes the same one catch (`ReportWriterEmitter.FieldImage`) while that statement does not enable EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION: the item keeps its unchanged content, which is SPACES because each presentation composes the line from a space-filled buffer (§13.8.6.2.3: the item's value "is determined solely by a SOURCE, SUM, or VALUE clause"), and the presentation continues (`SOURCE IS WS-F ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED` with WS-F = 1.55 into `PIC 9(3)` prints three spaces; golden `13.18.53-SOURCE/pb3990_report_source_prohibited_keeps_the_item`); a value that is exact but too big is §14.7.5 case 3 alone and keeps the low-order digits above (`COMPUTE N ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED = 150` into `PIC 99` stores 50), and one both inexact and too big is rule 7's (unchanged). With the phrase or with checking enabled the receiver is left unchanged too, and the phrase or the EC-SIZE handling runs. **A floating-point resultant** (`FloatResultant`, kb/Work PB1196) has no low-order digits to keep: a value past the format's largest finite magnitude after the mode's rounding (§14.7.5 case 3 / no-phrase rule 4, EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION) stores, with checking off, ISO/IEC 60559's overflow result for the mode — the largest finite magnitude when the mode rounds toward zero (TRUNCATION, PROHIBITED, TOWARD-LESSER on a positive value, TOWARD-GREATER on a negative one), ±Infinity otherwise; a NaN or ±Infinity VALUE transfers unchanged and is never that condition.
