| DOC-A.1-128 | **OCCURS clause — range of values allowed in the index**, §13.18.38.4 GR2, required + documented | **The full signed 64-bit interval, −9 223 372 036 854 775 808 through +9 223 372 036 854 775 807.** In this data model an index IS its 1-based occurrence number, held in a C# `long` (each INDEXED BY name is an `IndexDeclaration` owning its own `long` cell, minted by `DataBinder.RegisterIndexes`; DATA_MODEL_DESIGN D3), so the allowed range is that carrier's range — `CobolIndex.MinIndex` / `CobolIndex.MaxIndex`. §13.18.38.4 GR2 requires the range to include at least occurrence numbers (1 − integer-2) through (2 × integer-2); integer-2 cannot exceed this implementation's maximum occurrence count (`CobolDynTable.MaxOccurrences`, 2^30−1), so the required interval is contained with more than thirty bits to spare. ⛔ **A value inside the range but outside the TABLE is not out of range**: §14.9.39.4 GR2 a) 1. c and GR4 b) each end "even if that occurrence is not a valid occurrence within this table", so an index pointing past its own table is legal and must not raise — a table-bounds test here would reject conforming programs. GR2's own three statements enforce the range (kb/Work PB459): a SET amount lands through `CobolIndex.TryAmount` and a SET / PERFORM VARYING augment through `CobolIndex.Augment`, each of which sets EC-RANGE-INDEX and leaves the index unchanged on a value or result outside it (GR2 b's "undefined unless the value of the index is specified by the rules of that statement" — §14.9.39.4 GR2 a) 1. b and GR4 a) specify it, so it is not undefined). A SEARCH cannot reach the boundary at all: §14.9.37.4 GR4's initial-index guard leaves the scan only when the index is within the table's occurrence count, so its `+= 1` is bounded by that count. | `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb459_set_index_amount_guards`; `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb459_set_index_amount_ec`; `conformance:cases/13.18.38-OCCURS/pb459_set_index_range_ec`; `conformance:cases/14.9.39-SET/pb459_set_index_overflow_unchanged` |
| DOC-A.1-179 | **Size error condition — whether the intermediate data item's value range is checked**, §14.7.5 item 5, required + documented | **Checked, in five places.** (1) Whenever size-error checking is ENABLED for the statement — an ON SIZE ERROR phrase, or EC-SIZE checking turned on by `>>TURN` / an exception-checking PERFORM (kb/Work PB91, 2026-08-18: this now includes every arithmetic expression the statement evaluates, in a condition, a function argument, a subscript, a SET amount, not only the arithmetic statement's own operands) — addition and subtraction are overflow-checked at the `Int128` intermediate boundary (`AddChecked`/`SubChecked` → `CobolSizeError`, the size error condition, §14.7.5 case 5; a zero divisor in a divide operation → EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE, case 2), disposed per the phrase or per §14.6.13.1.3 (golden `pb91_native_overflow_outside_arithmetic`); with checking NOT enabled an addition and a subtraction wrap unchecked, exactly as §14.7.5's "if … the implementor defines that the range … is to be checked" conditions the case on the implementor's determination — **and a native PRODUCT never wraps in any statement** (kb/Work PB1143): a product whose operands' digit bounds prove it fits is a bare multiply, and one that may leave the carrier is formed exactly (item 123), an operand of unknown width being bounded by the `Int128` that carries it (kb/Work PB3538), so a product, like a nested quotient, raises the size error condition only for a VALUE outside the range where it lands. Reachable: `HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC` of `PIC S9(19) COMP-5` is exactly `Int128.MaxValue`, where `ADD 1` overflows the intermediate itself. **"Enabled" is per condition name** (kb/Work PB4092; §14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3): the checked operators are chosen, and raise, only for the conditions the statement enables or its SIZE ERROR phrase takes — EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW for the `Int128` sum's wrap and a binary64 result of ±Infinity, EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW for a nonzero binary64 result rounded to zero — and a range condition not enabled is the unchecked operator's value (A.1 item 70). (2) An arithmetic OPERAND whose value exceeds the intermediate range — possible only for an unsigned 16-byte COMP-5 item holding a value above 2^127−1 — raises the size error condition on reference (`CobolNum.Widen`), never a silent wrap: with ON SIZE ERROR the phrase takes it, without it the run fails loudly naming the operand. The value-preserving paths (MOVE, DISPLAY, relation conditions) are NOT arithmetic and carry the full container range. Pinned by `highest_algebraic_comp5_unsigned` (the `S19-ADD1=SIZE` / `W19-ADD1=SIZE` legs). **The same boundary binds a function's returned value** (kb/Work PB2698): FUNCTION ABS of a signed 16-byte item holding −2^127 has the value 2^127 (§15.7.4 r1 b's equivalent expression `(- (argument-1))`), past the intermediate, so it raises the size error condition like every other exact-carrier step (`CobolIntrinsics.SizeEscape`) and never returns the negative number the negation wraps to; and the unary exact functions (ABS, SIGN, INTEGER, INTEGER-PART, FRACTION-PART) take an UNSIGNED-WIDE operand on its own lane (`SignOfU`, `IntegerPartU`, `FractionPartU`; ABS of an unsigned operand is the operand) instead of narrowing it, so none of them raises a size error for a value whose result is in range (golden `2023/pb2698_unary_functions_unsigned_wide_and_minimum`). **(3) An SDIDI-carried value entering the Int128 carrier as an INTERMEDIATE** — an intrinsic argument, an aligned arithmetic operand, a subscript, an integer argument (kb/Work PB69, 2026-08-18) — whose magnitude the carrier cannot hold at the required scale raises **EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW** (`CobolDec.ToUnscaledIntermediate`), never the modular low-order digits; under native arithmetic such a value arises only from an integer power past the carrier (the documented double approximation — an intrinsic with such an argument computes on its SDIDI body instead, a relation compares it exactly, an arithmetic operation with it evaluates on the SDIDI; a store of it is the checked §14.7 transfer, SIZE ERROR). Pinned by `2023/pb69_native_power_past_the_carrier` and `CobolDecDivisionTests`. **The carrier's bound is `Int128`'s own range, not 38 digits, and the SDIDI lift of a wider operand is a rounding, not a size error** (kb/Work PB2918): a 16-byte binary container owns 39 digits, so an operand lifted into the SDIDI (`NumericRenderer.DecOperand`) whose digit bound passes the intermediate's 34 is ROUNDED once under the INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING mode (§8.8.1.5.2 r1; PROHIBITED ⇒ EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, §11.9.11.2 r3d) — `COMPUTE R = S + 1` with S = −2^127 in `PIC S9(19) COMP-5` is the SDIDI −170141183460469231731687303715884100000 and is stored, where it used to take ON SIZE ERROR — in standard-decimal arithmetic and in a native statement that carries a Dec operand (item 82) alike, where the native lane's bound is its 38-digit exact scratch rather than 34 (a native 36-digit product is carried exactly and reduced once at the result, and a native relation compares it exactly, so only a 16-byte container's 39th digit or an unknown bound rounds at the lift); and the checked landing of an SDIDI value into the carrier (`CobolDec.ToUnscaledChecked` / `ToUnscaledIntermediate`) tests whether the value FITS `Int128` (`CobolNum.WideningFits`) and no longer counts digits, so a 39-digit value below 2^127 lands. The same rule routes the unary functions that HAVE an equivalent arithmetic expression (ABS §15.7.4, SIGN §15.81.4, INTEGER-PART §15.49.4, FRACTION-PART §15.42.4) to their SDIDI bodies under STANDARD-DECIMAL when the argument's lift would round (kb/Work PB2965; §15.4.1 r1 makes the returned value equal the expression): `FUNCTION ABS(S)` with S = −2^127 in `PIC S9(19) COMP-5` is the rounded 170141183460469231731687303715884100000 and is stored, not the size error of the magnitude of −2^127, and `FUNCTION FRACTION-PART` of a 39-digit scaled container is the SDIDI's fraction (−0.8841 for −2^127 at scale 9). INTEGER (§15.44.4 r1) and MAX / MIN (§15.59.4 r1, §15.63.4 r1) have no equivalent expression, return the argument's own value, and stay exact (the determination D3 records: an exact result past 34 digits keeps its precision). An UNSIGNED-wide operand (above 2^127−1) lifted for a relation or a function argument is rounded the same way (`CobolDec.FromUnsigned`); as an operand of an arithmetic expression on the SDIDI lane (every standard-mode expression, and a native one carrying a Dec operand) it is rounded the same way (kb/Work PB2966), and only on the native `Int128` lanes does it still raise the size error condition (2). The SDIDI RESULT lands in an unsigned 16-byte receiver through `CobolDec.ToUnscaledMagnitude` (kb/Work PB2966): a value in [2^127, 2^128) is inside the receiver's container (A.1 item 208) and is stored (`COMPUTE Q = W + 0` with W = 2^128−1 in `PIC 9(19) COMP-5` stores 340282366920938463463374607431768200000, the operand rounded to 34 digits), where it used to be §14.7.5 case 3; a result past 2^128 remains that size error. Pinned by `2023/pb2966_sdidi_unsigned_wide_operand_and_landing`. **The binary64 twin of (3)** (kb/Work PB3019): a floating-point value entering the `Int128` carrier as an INTERMEDIATE (`NumericRenderer.Align` / `AlignRoundedUp` - an alignment, an argument, a count) whose magnitude the carrier cannot hold at the required scale raises **EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW** too (`CobolFloat.ToScaledIntermediate`), where it used to saturate to `Int128.MaxValue` - a value that a comparison or a selection takes for a number, that cannot be told from 1E301 against 1E300, and that a 16-byte receiver accepts as legal. The formatted-time seconds argument alone keeps a sign-saturating screen of its own (10^19 seconds or more is "out of the standard numeric time form", the SDIDI lane's bound, `CobolDate.SecondsOfReal`). **DIVIDE ... GIVING ... REMAINDER** takes the lane of the statement (kb/Work PB3017): under STANDARD / STANDARD-DECIMAL its quotient, subsidiary quotient and remainder are SDIDI values formed from the operands' §8.8.1.5.2 lifts (§14.9.12.4 GR1, GR6 c), GR7), so an unsigned 16-byte dividend in [2^127, 2^128) or a floating-point dividend of 1E30 are no size error when the quotient fits the receiver; under native arithmetic the exact `Int128` kernel stays for two scaled operands (an unsigned-wide one past the carrier is case 5 as above), while a binary64 or SDIDI operand is divided as it is, by the same division DIVIDE GIVING without REMAINDER performs, and its quotient past the carrier is the resultant's size error (kb/Work PB3829); and the subsidiary quotient's digit cap is the digits the receiver's store KEEPS (a PICTURE-truncating item's digit positions; no cap for a binary-capacity item, which holds its whole container). Pinned by `2023/pb3017_sdidi_divide_remainder_beyond_the_int128_carrier` and `2023/pb3019_native_float_intermediate_past_the_carrier_is_a_size_error`. **(4) The receiver-bound radix-point ALIGNMENT of a result, under checking** (kb/Work PB639, 2026-09-05). This is §14.7.5 case 3, not case 5 — a RECEIVER overflow "after radix point alignment" — but it shares the carrier, and the alignment multiply wraps: a widening the `Int128` carrier cannot form was aligned first and capacity-checked afterwards, so a wrap that landed back inside the picture read as fitting. `CobolNum.WideningFits` is now consulted BEFORE the multiply by all three siblings (`TryStore`, `RescaleChecked`, `RescaleEscape`) and by `CobolEdit.TryFormat`: a value the carrier cannot align is further from zero than ANY fixed-point receiver permits, so it is the size error condition and storing rule 2 leaves the receiver unchanged. Before this, `COMPUTE WC = 340282366920938463463374607432 ON SIZE ERROR` into `PIC S9(9)V9(9)` — a legal 30-digit literal that is ceil(2^128 / 10^9) — ran NOT ON SIZE ERROR and stored +0.231788544, and the same statement under `>>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON` raised nothing at all. **(5) The binary64 intermediate** (kb/Work PB1566, 2026-09-24; PB1581 + PB1147, 2026-09-26). Under native arithmetic an expression with a floating-point operand, or whose resultants are all floating-point, evaluates in binary64 (item 123), and the §15.4.1 float family's returned value IS a binary64 (item 92), so binary64's range is that intermediate's range and a result outside it is this case: **EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW** when farther from zero, **EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW** when a nonzero exact result rounds to zero (§14.7.5's no-phrase rule 3 names both; a subnormal is in range) — raised by the ONE `CobolFloat.InBinary64Range` check as the same `CobolSizeError` FACTORIAL raises past the Int128 intermediate. It covers (a) the native binary64 OPERATORS where size-error checking is enabled — `+ - * /` (`CobolFloat.AddChecked` / `SubChecked` / `MulChecked` / `DivChecked`) and `**` (`CobolIntrinsics.PowNativeRealChecked`), the floating arm's twins of the scaled lane's `MulChecked` / `AddChecked` / `DivideOrThrow`, including §14.7.5 case 2's zero divisor (EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE) — and, like that lane, the bare IEEE operators where checking is not enabled; and (b) the float family's returned values unconditionally, as FACTORIAL's is: EXP / EXP10 on every carrier (e^x is never zero, so a finite argument's zero result is the underflow), every SDIDI-evaluated list body's narrowed result (VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION / PRESENT-VALUE over an exact list, kb/Work PB1565), and the binary64 list bodies over a floating argument (SUM, MEAN, RANGE, MIDRANGE, MEDIAN, VARIANCE, STANDARD-DEVIATION, PRESENT-VALUE — each operation of the equivalent arithmetic expression, so `MIDRANGE(1.5E308 1.5E308)`'s sum overflows). A NON-FINITE operand or argument is not an operation leaving the range and keeps item 70's disposition. Before it `DISPLAY FUNCTION EXP(1000)` printed `Infinity`, `COMPUTE F = C * C ON SIZE ERROR` over a COMP-2 holding 1.0E+300 took NOT ON SIZE ERROR and stored `Infinity`, and `COMPUTE FR = FL / FZ ON SIZE ERROR` with a FLOAT-LONG zero divisor did the same. Enforced by `DateTimeFormatGrammar.MaxFractionDigits`, which the §15.3 format recogniser consults, so a format with a longer fraction is rejected at COMPILE time (`COBOL1631`) instead of fabricating a value. | `conformance:cases/A.1-Implementor-defined-language-element-list/l1_time_fraction_max_digits` |
| DOC-A.1-92 | **Characteristics and representation of a numeric intrinsic function's returned value, and its text image**, §15.4.1 + §14.9.11.4 GR1, required — documentation NOT required by A.1 (voluntary); partially addresses A.1-56 | §15.4 places a function's returned value in a **temporary elementary data item**, and under NATIVE arithmetic §15.4.1 makes "the characteristics and representation of the returned value … defined by the implementor"; §14.9.11.4 GR1 independently makes any conversion between a DISPLAY operand and the device implementor-defined. **DISPLAY SHOWS THE TEMPORARY BY ITS DESCRIPTION (kb/Work PB3514, adjudicated 2026-10-25).** §15.4 puts the returned value in a temporary elementary data item, DISPLAY shows a numeric data item by its description (A.1 item 56), and §15.4.1 leaves the description to the implementor under native arithmetic, so the precedence order gives it to GnuCOBOL 3.2.0, whose description of the temporary is a function of the function and its arguments. Under the default `--numeric-display decimal`, DISPLAY of a numeric or integer function therefore shows the temporary as it shows any item of that description: the decimal point at the scale, a signed item's leading `+` or `-`, the program's decimal separator. There are three shapes, and ONE catalog column (`IntrinsicSig.DeviceForm`) says which a function has, defaulting to the third so that a function added tomorrow needs no edit. **(1) A copy of an argument's item** (`FunctionDeviceForm.Argument`): ABS (§15.7.1 "returns the absolute value of the argument"), MAX (§15.59.4 1) "the returned value is the content of the argument-1 having the greatest value"), MIN (§15.63.4 1) "the content of the argument-1 having the least value"), MEDIAN of an odd count (§15.61.1 "returns the content of the argument whose value is the middle value"; equal values keep their written order) and MEAN of one argument return the CONTENT of an argument, so the temporary has THAT argument's description: a field's PICTURE, USAGE and SIGN (a COMP-5's container digits, a SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE sign trailing); a numeric literal's field, one digit position for every digit written (a leading zero too), the fraction digits written and a sign position when a sign was written (`MAX(005 3)` is `005`, `MAX(+5 3)` is `+5`, `MAX(3 -14 0 8 -3)` is the literal `8`); an arithmetic expression or a nested function the temporary it was made as (shapes 2 and 3, signed exactly when its value was negative THEN). ABS holds the magnitude in a copy of that item: with `S PIC S9(5)V99` holding -12.5 and `U PIC 9(5)V99` holding 12.5, `ABS(S)` is `+00012.50`, `ABS(U)` `00012.50`, `ABS(FUNCTION INTEGER(S))` `+000000013`, `MAX(U S)` U's `00012.50`, `MIN(U S)` S's `-00012.50`; `MAX(I S2)` over `PIC 9(3)` 7 and `PIC S9(3)` -14 is `007`. **(2) An unsigned DISPLAY integer of fixed width** (`FixedDigits`): DATE-OF-INTEGER eight digits, DAY-OF-INTEGER seven (`16010101`; `00000000` for an invalid argument). **(3) The description the VALUE alone gives** (`Value`, every other exact function; `CobolNum.ReturnedValueProfile`): the trailing zeros of the fraction are dropped; a value of under 2**31 (2**32 unsigned) with at most 9 fraction digits is a 9-position item, one of under 2**63 (2**64) with at most 18 fraction digits a 20-position item, any other exactly its own digits (at least its fraction digits); the item is signed exactly when the value is negative. `FUNCTION INTEGER(-12.5)` is `-000000013`, `FUNCTION NUMVAL("12.50")` `00000012.5`, `FUNCTION ORD("A")` `000000066`, `FUNCTION SUM(U N)` `000000015`, `FUNCTION NUMVAL("0.000000001")` `.000000001`, `FUNCTION FACTORIAL(20)` `02432902008176640000`. Under a standard arithmetic mode the functions that are binary64 natively (SQRT, EXP, PI …) are exact SDIDI values and take this shape too (`SQRT(4)` is `000000002`, `PI` its 34 digits). **A call the binder FOLDS** shows as the literal when GnuCOBOL folds the same call (`FunctionDeviceForm.Literal`: LENGTH and BYTE-LENGTH of a fixed item, `7`) and as the value of the call it replaced otherwise (HIGHEST- and LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC, which GnuCOBOL evaluates at run time: `0099999.99`; SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, which it lacks, takes the same shape); the LENGTH of a run-time-length item is a computed value (`000000003`), and so is the LENGTH of a numeric function's value, which GnuCOBOL does not fold either (`LENGTH(FUNCTION ABS(S))` is `000000007`, below). **NOT COPIED**, because GnuCOBOL shows a figure the value does not have or an image no description gives: (a) its 4-byte temporary has 9 digit positions and cuts a 10-digit value's high-order digit (`NUMVAL("2147483647")` is `147483647` there; here `2147483647`); (b) its DISPLAY temporary takes its digit count from a GMP size estimate that may exceed the true count by one (`-09223372036854775808` there; here `-9223372036854775808`); (c) the 100-digit PI and the other binary64 images: a **binary64 result** (the §15.4.1 float family natively, and any function given a COMP-1 or COMP-2 item) keeps the shortest round-trip image a floating-point item has (kb/Work PB3505), so `SQRT(4)` is `2` where GnuCOBOL shows `000000002` and `ABS` of a COMP-2 holding -0.1 is `0.1` where it shows `0.09999999999999999`; a selection over a floating-point item picks the winner's own image (`MAX(F B)` with `B PIC 9(9) COMP-5` holding 5 is B's `0000000005`). **Measured, not argued:** `cobc -x -std=default` 3.2.0 was run over the PB3514 probe matrix (the selecting, rounding, statistical, date, parsing and mathematical functions over unsigned, signed, COMP-3, COMP, COMP-5, BINARY-DOUBLE, SIGN SEPARATE, P-scaled and floating-point items, literals, expressions and nested calls), and the goldens `pb3514_function_result_device_form`, `…_abs` and `…_comma` are the lines on which it and this compiler agree; `…_not_copied` pins the rows above, `…_standard_decimal` the SDIDI lane and `pb3514_function_result_digits_form` the option's other value. **A function's DISPLAY and its MOVE differ** exactly as an item's do, because §14.9.25.4 GR6 fixes what a MOVE sends: `MOVE FUNCTION ABS(S) TO PIC X(10)` is `12.50` while `DISPLAY FUNCTION ABS(S)` is `+00012.50`, as `MOVE S TO` and `DISPLAY S` differ. `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION …)` is a separate question (below). **WiseOwl COBOL's determination for every OTHER use of the value as TEXT — a MOVE to a character receiver, STRING, INSPECT, a text comparison, and DISPLAY under `--numeric-display digits` — is that a numeric function result renders in the LITERAL form of its value** — the significant digits with **no leading-zero padding**, a leading `-` when negative (never a zoned over-punch, because this is not a stored item), and a decimal point followed by exactly the result's scale in fraction digits when the value is scaled. **THE DECIMAL POINT IS THE PROGRAM'S DECIMAL SEPARATOR (kb/Work PB2507).** The literal form is the form a numeric literal has (the DISPLAY conversion row, A.1 item 56), and §12.3.7.4 GR14 a) makes the comma "the character written in numeric literals to represent the decimal separator" under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, so under that clause `DISPLAY FUNCTION NUMVAL("1,5")` prints `1,5`, `FUNCTION MAX(1,5 2,25)` prints `2,25` and `FUNCTION ABS(N)` over an `S9V99` item holding −1,5 prints `1,50`; a contained program inherits the clause (§12.3.4 GR1). The standard leaves the character image to the implementor (§14.9.11.4 GR1), so the precedence order decides and GnuCOBOL 3.2 prints the comma. The spelling is the EVALUATING unit's on every lane that writes this text: the native scaled-integer call, the SDIDI call under a standard arithmetic mode, the compile-time FOLD (HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC and its siblings, whose folded literal carries the separator) and the materialized §15.4 temporary (`DataItem.FunctionValueSeparator`). Without the clause the period is unchanged. Pinned by `85/pb2507_function_result_decimal_comma`, `2023/pb2507_function_result_decimal_comma_native`, `2023/pb2507_function_result_decimal_comma_standard_decimal`, `FunctionTextImageTests` and `FunctionTextDecimalPointTests`. A FLOAT-valued function (SQRT, trig, financial) renders through the same shortest-round-trip `CobolFloat.Display` a COMP-2 item does, so the function and an item holding its value agree. **The §15.4 temporary a statement materializes the value into** (the MOVE multi-receiver hoist of §14.9.25.4 GR1, an EVALUATE subject, an INVOKE argument) **has the same text image**: it is flagged as the function's returned value and described at scale 0 for an INTEGER function (§15.2 item 5), so `MOVE FUNCTION INTEGER(N) TO A B` stores in each character receiver what `MOVE FUNCTION INTEGER(N) TO A` does (kb/Work PB1007; a NUMERIC function's temporary read as TEXT in a character formal keeps the implementor scale 9, which only `--permissive` can move to a character receiver). **THE INTERMEDIATE IS DESCRIBED FOR THE VALUE AND ITS USE, NOT AS THE RETURNED-VALUE ITEM (kb/Work PB3268).** §14.9.25.4 GR1's `temp` is "an intermediate result item provided by the implementor" and §15.4.1 makes the returned value "the same for all instances of a given function within a single execution of the runtime element", so `MOVE FUNCTION PI TO Q1 Q2` stores in both receivers what `MOVE FUNCTION PI TO Q3` stores (3.141592653589793 into `PIC 9V9(15)`; the fixed S9(21)V9(9) intermediate stored 3.141592653000000, and cut a 25-integer-digit NUMVAL to its low 21 digits, a COMP-2 receiver to 3.141592653 and an EVALUATE subject to nine places). **WiseOwl COBOL's determination:** a value the renderer returns as a binary64 (`ReceiverContext.FloatLanding`) is held on a COMP-2 intermediate and each receiver's own float landing quantizes once, at its own scale; which functions those are is the renderer's dispatch asked at bind time (`FunctionValueLane.ReturnsBinary64`): under NATIVE arithmetic the §15.4.1 floating-math family, and any numeric-argument function given a binary64 argument (a COMP-1/COMP-2 item, another function's binary64 value), EXCEPT a function with an SDIDI body given an SDIDI-carried argument (a floating-point literal such as `0.1E0` in `VARIANCE`, `ANNUITY`, `PRESENT-VALUE`, `SUM`, `MAX`, …), whose value is an SDIDI. Any other value whose EVERY receiver is floating-point of ONE binary format is held on an item of that format, a COMP-1 for an all-binary32 set (so an exact value is rounded once, as A.1 item 81 states; a binary64 narrowed into it rounded `2**60 + 2**36 + 1` to `2**60` where the correctly rounded binary32 is `2**60 + 2**37`) and a COMP-2 for an all-binary64 set; any other value whose every receiver is a numeric or numeric-edited item, at least one of them floating-point (a floating-point numeric-edited item, a binary32 beside a binary64, a floating-point item beside a fixed-point one), is held on the widest floating-point numeric-edited item the PICTURE admits, `+9.9(35)E+9999` (§13.18.40.3 SR15, §13.18.40.4 GR13 b), a 36-digit decimal floating-point item: an edited receiver truncates the sender's decimal value to its own significand (§14.6.8.4 2), a fixed-point one to its own digit positions (§14.6.8.2 4), a binary one converts it once, and truncating to 36 digits first changes nothing, where a binary64 intermediate cut `NUMVAL ("1.2345678901234567890123")` into `PIC +9.9(20)E+99` to 17 digits (kb/Work PB370) and a fixed-point one cut a floating-point receiver, which keeps its digits at any magnitude: `MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL ("1234567890123456.5") TO S C` (S `PIC S9(3)V99`, C FLOAT-LONG) stored 567890123456.5 in C through a 12-integer-digit window, and a FLOAT-SHORT beside a FLOAT-LONG stored 1.234E-21 as 0 in both (kb/Work PB3268). Every other value is held on a fixed-point item described by the receivers of the MOVE (the widest fixed-point receiver's scale and integer digits, the integer digits kept first; a floating-point receiver reaches it only beside a character receiver under `--permissive`, and takes the fraction digits the 38 of the `Int128` carrier leave), unless every receiver is fixed-point and their integer and fraction digits together pass the carrier's 38 (a `PIC 9(31)` beside a `PIC V9(28)`), when no fixed-point window is exact for all of them (capping the scale cut `MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL ("1234567890123456789012.123456789") TO X Y`'s `Y` to seven fraction digits) and the value is held on the 36-digit decimal item above (kb/Work PB370), and 21 integer + 17 fraction digits for a value read as an operand (an EVALUATE subject, a function argument frozen for §8.4.3.2.4 GR2's left-to-right order). An INTEGER function's value is held at the carrier's 38 digits at scale 0, so a 31-digit `INTEGER(N)` or `SUM` reaches every receiver whole (a 31-digit value is a DISPLAY temporary of 31 digits, and that is what `FUNCTION LENGTH` measures), unless it is a binary64, or every receiver is numeric with a floating-point one among them, when it is held as any other numeric function's value is: `INTEGER` of a FLOAT-LONG holding 1.5E50 is a 51-digit integer (pinned by `cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_integer_float`; the binary32 sets by `cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_binary32_receivers`). A NESTED function is classified by the carrier the renderer returns it on, an INTEGER function included (§15.2 item 5 fixes the value's type, not its carrier): `ANNUITY(INTEGER(1.5E0) 3)` computes on `INTEGER`'s SDIDI value, and only SIGN, ORD-MAX and ORD-MIN, whose SDIDI bodies return an exact integer, hand their caller an exact value. **Residual:** a value that needs more digits than the `Int128` carrier holds, an exact-family NUMVAL text of more than 17 fraction digits as an EVALUATE subject, is held at the carrier's digits where the un-hoisted reference would keep the SDIDI's, and a value of more than 36 significant digits on the 36-digit decimal item is cut to 36 (only the `Int128` scaled lane carries one, a 37- or 38-digit `SUM` beside a floating-point receiver); both need an SDIDI-carried intermediate item. Pinned by `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_one_evaluation`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_pi_and_wide_integers`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_float_receivers`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_mixed_float_set`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_standard_decimal`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_lane_matrix` (353 function x argument-shape x receiver-set cells, each a multi-receiver MOVE against the single-receiver one), `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_nested_lane`, `conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb3268_function_value_integer_nested`, `FunctionValueIntermediateDriftTests` and `FunctionValueLaneDriftTests`. **AND ITS LANDING IN A FIXED-POINT ARITHMETIC RECEIVER TAKES THE STATEMENT'S ROUNDING MODE, ONCE, AT THAT RECEIVER'S SCALE (kb/Work PB647).** The quantizer used to round NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO at a working scale whatever the statement said, while the MOVE channel took the receiver's mode at the receiver's scale, so one returned value landed two ways in one receiver: with `S PIC 9V9(9)`, `MOVE FUNCTION SQRT(3) TO S` gave 1.732050807 and `COMPUTE S = FUNCTION SQRT(3)` gave 1.732050808, and `FUNCTION SQRT(0.9999999999)` into `PIC 9V9` split across a whole tenth. §15.4.1's identity sentence forbids that outright, and §8.8.1.3's native latitude reaches the INTERMEDIATE, not the transfer into a resultant identifier, which §14.7.4.1 puts "relative to the size provided for the resultant identifier" and §14.7.4.3 rule 2 makes TRUNCATION when no ROUNDED phrase is written. **The determination is therefore: the float family's returned value is a binary64, and its transfer into a fixed-point resultant identifier is the SAME transfer a MOVE of that value performs** — the receiver's scale, the statement's mode, one rounding (`ReceiverContext.FloatLanding`; the same rule governs native `**`). A nested float operand is not that transfer: it stays the same binary64 value (kb/Work PB653) and, as an OPERAND, it is an **engine-produced approximation, not a floating-point item** (kb/Work PB1641) — §14.9.2.4 GR4 / §14.9.44.4 GR4 (ADD and SUBTRACT; for the other statements and conditions the native lane is this compiler's determination under §8.8.1.3, item 123) require "enough places" except for operands "described with usage binary-char, binary-short, binary-long, binary-double, float-short, float-long, or float-extended", and §14.7.7 r2 lists an intrinsic function, those usages and a floating-point literal as three separate bullets. Beside operands that are NOT floating-point the approximation therefore enters the arithmetic through its shortest-round-trip decimal (the SDIDI, §8.8.1.5.1's conversion — the same VALUE) and the operation runs on the decimal lane, so `13.2 + FUNCTION SQRT(16)` is 17.2 (it stored 17.1 when 13.2 was dragged into binary64 as 13.199999999999999) and `0.1 + FUNCTION SQRT(0.04) = 0.3` is TRUE; beside a floating-point ITEM or into a floating-point receiver the expression stays in binary64 (item 123), exactly as before. The same holds for a native non-integer `**`. Where the ISO text is silent about the intermediate's representation, GnuCOBOL (which evaluates every intrinsic result as a decimal) is the precedent. Pinned by `pb1641_function_result_beside_decimal_operands`. The retired rationale — that rounding at the working scale is the better approximation of the returned VALUE — was true of the value and irrelevant to the transfer; the visible gain is that ROUNDED now does something on this family at all, where `COMPUTE S ROUNDED` and no-phrase `COMPUTE S` used to answer alike. A nested float operand carries no working scale at all, so the expression over a float FUNCTION and the same expression over a COMP-2 holding the identical value agree to the digit (`FUNCTION SQRT(3) * 2` into `PIC 9V9(9)` gives 3.464101615 either way). Pinned by `pb647_float_landing_mode` at 2002/2014/2023 and `FloatLandingModeDriftTests`. Examples of the literal form: `MOVE FUNCTION ORD("A") TO PIC X(10)` → `66` left-justified, space-filled (§14.9.25.4 GR6; §15.70.1 — ordinal position, lowest is 1); `DISPLAY FUNCTION ORD("A")` under `--numeric-display digits` → `66` (under the default, `000000066`); `DISPLAY FUNCTION MIN(3 -14 0 8 -3)` → `-14` in both (the literal argument's own field). **⛔ The literal form exists to make the compile-time FOLD unobservable in the TEXT channels** (MOVE, STRING, INSPECT, comparisons, DISPLAY under `digits`). An intrinsic over constant arguments folds to a numeric literal and a literal renders as its own text (`DISPLAY 42` → `42`); had a computed result been given a padded fixed width instead, a MOVE of `FUNCTION LENGTH(X)` and of `FUNCTION ORD(C)` would produce visibly different formats for no reason a COBOL programmer could see. One rule, both paths. In DISPLAY's default form the fold is observable only where GnuCOBOL's own is, LENGTH and BYTE-LENGTH (`7` of a fixed item against `000000003` of a run-time length), because a selection function copies a literal argument's own field: the fold/compute pairs of the golden `da2_function_as_text` (`MAX(3 7)` and `MAX(FIVE 7)`) still print alike. **The Table-16 consequence (kb/Work PB73, adjudicated 2026-08-18):** the function's §15.2 TYPE is its §14.9.25.3 Table-16 row as a MOVE sender — an INTEGER function (ISO §15.2 item 5, "no digits to the right of the decimal point": LENGTH, ORD, INTEGER-OF-DATE, ABS/MAX/MIN over integers, …) is the Integer row and moves to an alphanumeric or national receiver in this text form (`MOVE FUNCTION ORD("A") TO PIC X(10)` → `66`); a NUMERIC function (item 4 — SQRT, NUMVAL, RANDOM, MAX over a non-integer, …) is the NONINTEGER row and moves only to a numeric or numeric-edited receiver, whatever a particular reference's value (the principle §8.4.3.2.3 SR11 states for the integer-operand positions) — COBOL0819. `--permissive` keeps the pre-adjudication admission with a warning, rendering the same literal text. Pinned by `2023/pb73_table16_function_type_and_boolean_view`, the negatives `pb73-move-numeric-function-to-alphanumeric` / `pb73-move-numval-function-to-national`, and `MoveTable16FunctionTypeTests`. This is the TEXT channels' determination; DISPLAY's default form follows GnuCOBOL (above), whose zero-padding of a computed `ORD` and minimal print of a folded `MAX` are both its temporaries' descriptions (a literal argument's field, a value-described item). **NUMVAL and NUMVAL-C HAVE NO NATIVE WORKING SCALE, BECAUSE §15.4.1'S LATITUDE DOES NOT REACH THEM (kb/Work PB251, rows RV-15.4.1-2 / RV-15.4.1-L2.2).** §15.4.1's closing sentence is a CONDITIONAL — "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined **unless otherwise specified in the function definition**" — and §15.67.4 r1 / §15.68.4 r1 are exactly such a specification, written once with no arithmetic-mode qualification: "The returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1". Neither function has an equivalent arithmetic expression, so the latitude is withdrawn and **the native returned value is the parsed value EXACTLY**; only the *characteristics and representation* stay the implementor's. **WiseOwl COBOL's determination: that representation is the SDIDI, in every arithmetic mode** — the one representation that holds every conforming argument (§15.67.3 r3's 31 digits native, r4's 34 standard) with no working scale at all, since its exponent is carried at run time. No compile-time scale can do the job: a scaled `Int128` temporary needs *i* + *ws* digits for an argument with *i* integer digits and r3 permits *i* = 31, so the only *ws* safe for every conforming argument is 7 — while `NUMVAL("0.123456789")` needs 9. The former `max(context scale, 6)` rule made a function's value depend on the SHAPE of its receiver and truncated wherever no receiver scale was inherited: `DISPLAY FUNCTION NUMVAL("0.1234567")` printed 0.123456, and a receiver was no protection either — it bounds the STATEMENT's result, not an OPERAND's precision, so `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION NUMVAL("0.1234567") * 10000000` stored 1234560 into `PIC 9(9)`. Pinned by `pb251_numval_native_value_fixed`, whose native lines are the SAME lines `pb60_numval_standard_decimal` prints for the same references. **NUMVAL-F HAS ONE VALUE IN EVERY ARITHMETIC MODE, EVERY CHANNEL AND EVERY RECEIVER: THE EXACT PARSE (PB60 / RV-15.69.4-2, re-determined by kb/Work PB3839, owner 2026-10-26).** §15.69.4 r2 makes the native (and standard-binary) returned value "an approximation of the numeric value represented by argument-1" and r3 gives standard-decimal arithmetic "the numeric value represented by argument-1"; §15.4.1 leaves "the characteristics and representation of the returned value" under native arithmetic to the implementor, and nothing in the standard says WHICH approximation. The precedence for such latitude is the ISO text, then GnuCOBOL, then self-consistency, and the first two are silent or agree: GnuCOBOL 3.2 rounds an exact decimal once at the receiver (`COMPUTE R ROUNDED MODE AWAY-FROM-ZERO = FUNCTION NUMVAL-F("0.12340000000001")` into `PIC 9V9(4)` stores 0.1235, as it does for NUMVAL). **WiseOwl COBOL's determination: the approximation IS r3's value** — the exact parse, significand × 10^(exponent − fraction digits), carried as an SDIDI exactly as NUMVAL's is (`IntrinsicCarrierRules.ReturnsExactParse`: NUMVAL and NUMVAL-C by §15.67.4 r1 / §15.68.4 r1, NUMVAL-F by this determination). The earlier determination, the float family's (a binary64 wherever no fixed-point scale governed, an `Int128` parse truncated at the receiver-capped `max(receiver scale, 9)` for a fixed-point receiver), gave ONE reference several values and rounded a fixed-point receiver's value twice: `DISPLAY FUNCTION NUMVAL-F("0.12340000000001")` printed the full value, a COMP-2 received a binary64, and `ROUNDED MODE AWAY-FROM-ZERO` into `PIC 9V9(4)` truncated at nine places and then rounded the truncation, storing 0.1234 where the rule (§14.7.4.1 "relative to the size provided for the resultant identifier", §14.7.4.3 rule 3) owes the one rounding of the exact value, 0.1235 — the receiver-shape dependence this paragraph's NUMVAL sibling rejects. **Every channel now reads the same value:** a DISPLAY or STRING operand renders the item-92 text form of the exact value at its own scale (`NUMVAL-F("5E+30")` is `5000000000000000000000000000000`, `NUMVAL-F("1.5E-12")` is `0.0000000000015`, a 20-digit significand keeps all 20); a relation compares the exact values (`NUMVAL-F("0.12345678901234567891") = NUMVAL-F("0.12345678901234567892")` is FALSE, where binary64 made it TRUE); an operand, an argument and a subscript carry it exactly; a fixed-point receiver (any scale, a trailing-P item, any ROUNDED mode) rounds it ONCE with the statement's own rule, and a MOVE truncates it per §14.6.8.2 rule 4; a floating-point receiver converts the exact decimal once and lands it as it lands any decimal sender (item 81: a MOVE rounds to nearest, a COMPUTE with no ROUNDED phrase truncates, so `COMPUTE F = FUNCTION NUMVAL-F("1.5E-12")` stores what `COMPUTE F = 0.0000000000015` stores). **The range of the representation:** a conforming native argument whose magnitude passes decimal128's (exponent beyond +6144, or below −6176; `FUNCTION NUMVAL-F("1E+7000")`) is outside the SDIDI that carries the value, and is the size-error condition of the implementor-defined intermediate range (§14.7.5 case 5, item 179: EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW / EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW, the receiver unchanged under ON SIZE ERROR), exactly as every other SDIDI-carried native value (a floating-point literal, an integer power) and as the same argument under standard-decimal arithmetic, where TEST-NUMVAL-F already reports it (§15.95.4 r1 b 6); a binary64 that read it as ±Infinity or zero is gone. The ACCEPT device transfer into a floating-point receiver is not a function reference: it converts the record, which IS the NUMVAL-F argument format, once into the receiver's own format (`CobolIntrinsics.NumvalFDouble` / `NumvalFSingle`, item 81). Pinned by `pb3839_numval_f_one_value` (every ROUNDED mode at scale 4 in both signs, scales 0, 9 and 12 and a trailing-P receiver, an operand, DISPLAY, the 10**-20 relation, the COMP-2 landings), `pb60_numvalf_native_channels`, `pb251_numval_native_value_fixed`, the SIZE ERROR witness `pb3839_numval_f_beyond_the_sdidi` and `ReceiverShapeReaderDriftTests`. **NUMVAL-F's value no longer differs by mode:** under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (and 2002's STANDARD) §15.69.4 r3 fixes it ("the numeric value represented by argument-1") and the SDIDI temporary carries the parsed value exactly at its own scale in every channel (`NUMVAL-F("1.23456789012345E-3")` renders 0.00123456789012345; a 34-digit significand is exact) — pinned by `pb60_numval_standard_decimal`; what the three NUMVAL functions still do differently by mode is their digit cap (31 native, 34 standard-decimal), and nothing else. **THE SELECTION FUNCTIONS FOLLOW THE SAME RULE (kb/Work PB3839).** MAX and MIN return "the content of the argument-1 having the greatest [least] value" (§15.59.4 r1 / §15.63.4 r1), so the selected value reaches a receiver with every digit it has: a receiver-bound result lands at the common argument scale, widened to the receiver's own scale and capped at its `Int128` headroom (`ReceiverContext.WorkingScale`), never at a coarser receiver's scale alone, where it was truncated first and the receiver's ROUNDED phrase then rounded the truncation (`MAX(0.12345 0.1)` into `PIC 9V99` ROUNDED MODE AWAY-FROM-ZERO stored 0.12 where §14.7.4.3 rule 3 owes the one rounding of 0.12345, 0.13). Pinned by `pb3839_max_min_round_once`. **THE RETURNED VALUE'S CAPACITY — WHAT A CLASS CONDITION ASKS OF A FUNCTION-IDENTIFIER (kb/Work PB1401 / PB1466).** §8.5.2.12 items 6–7 make a numeric or integer function a category-numeric data item, so §8.8.4.4.4 GR3 g) / m) ("the numeric value farthest from zero" / "the nonzero numeric value nearest to zero that may be contained in that data item") need the temporary's extremes, and they follow the representation fixed above: a **binary64** result (the float family) has binary64's, asked on its own bits exactly as a COMP-2 item is; an **SDIDI** result (NUMVAL / NUMVAL-C in every mode, every function under a standard arithmetic mode) has the SDIDI's (±9.999…E+6144 at 34 digits, nearest 1E-6176); every other result has the extremes of a NOMINAL item — **S9(30)** for an INTEGER function (nearest nonzero value 1, §15.2 item 5) and **S9(21)V9(9)** for a NUMERIC one — because the temporary DISPLAY shows and LENGTH measures has a description that follows the value, so no one item's extremes exist for the condition to read (kb/Work PB3951). `FUNCTION ABS(-1) IS NEAREST-TO-ZERO` is therefore TRUE and `FUNCTION SQRT(4) IS NEAREST-TO-ZERO` FALSE. A function-identifier `IS NUMERIC` is GR3 n) 1. — the function is category numeric (§15.2 items 4–5), so its VALUE is tested, never its text: true for every fixed-point or SDIDI result and for a finite binary64 (`FUNCTION NUMVAL("1.5") IS NUMERIC` and `FUNCTION INTEGER(-5.5) IS NUMERIC` are TRUE; n) 2.'s all-digits test used to answer them FALSE on the text "1.5" / "-6"); `IS IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE` compares the value's magnitude with the mode's intermediate extremes (GR3 l)). Every one of these tests evaluates the function ONCE (`CobolValueClass`), so RANDOM's seed advances once per written reference. Pinned by `conformance:cases/8.5.2.12-Numeric-category/pb1401_computed_numeric_class` and `conformance:cases/8.5.2.12-Numeric-category/pb1401_computed_numeric_numeric`. **THE LENGTH OF A FUNCTION'S RETURNED-VALUE ITEM (kb/Work PB1398).** A function-identifier is a data item (§8.4.3.2.1), so `FUNCTION LENGTH` and `FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH` (§15.50.3 r1 / §15.14.3 r1, "a data item of any class or category") measure the item its §15.2 type describes. **The determination (kb/Work PB3951): an INTEGER or NUMERIC function's returned value is measured as the SAME §15.4 temporary DISPLAY shows, by BYTE-LENGTH in bytes (§15.14.4 r1) and by LENGTH in character positions (§15.50.4 r2, r3; the two are one number for every temporary but the copy of a USAGE NATIONAL argument, item (1) below), so it is GnuCOBOL 3.2.0's size of its temporary by the precedence of CLAUDE.md rule 1, because §15.4.1 leaves the representation to the implementor.** The first implementation gave every numeric function the fixed S9(30) or S9(21)V9(9) item, 30 bytes (`LENGTH(FUNCTION ABS(S))` was 30); that item is a description nobody else uses, and it was a second answer to the question the three shapes above already answer. (1) A copy of an argument's item is the bytes of THAT item: `LENGTH(FUNCTION ABS(S))` is 7 over `S PIC S9(5)V99`, 5 over `PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3`, 2 over `PIC S9(4) COMP`, 8 over a SIGN SEPARATE `PIC S9(5)V99`, 4 over a COMP-1 item; `MAX(PK S)` is the size of whichever argument is greater; a numeric literal's field is its digits written plus a sign position when a sign was written (`ABS(-12.50)` 5, `ABS(12.50)` 4). A copy of a USAGE NATIONAL argument has the item's positions for LENGTH and its bytes for BYTE-LENGTH (`MIN(NN NU)` over `PIC S9(5) USAGE NATIONAL` is 5 and 10; 6 and 12 with SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE), because the compiler states both from the argument item (`ItemLength.Positions`, `DataItem.ByteWidth`); GnuCOBOL, whose national support is unfinished, answers 10 to both (the same departure it makes for the item itself). (2) DATE-OF-INTEGER is 8 and DAY-OF-INTEGER 7. (3) Every other exact function is the item its VALUE describes (`CobolNum.ReturnedValueProfile`): 4 bytes for the 9-position temporary, 8 for the 20-position one, otherwise its DISPLAY digits (`INTEGER(S)` 4, `NUMVAL("12345678901234567890123")` 23). The size follows the value, so the call is evaluated at run time, as GnuCOBOL evaluates it, and DISPLAY shows it as a computed value (`000000007`). `FunctionValueField.Length` and `FunctionValueField.ByteLength` are the one answer: the binder sends the argument to the renderer (`IntrinsicBinder.FunctionResultLength`) and the renderer reads the field `FunctionDeviceText.Field` builds for DISPLAY, so the item DISPLAY shows and the item LENGTH measures cannot differ, and a function added tomorrow needs no edit. **NOT COPIED**, as for DISPLAY: a binary64 result (the float family natively, `SQRT`, `PI`, `ANNUITY`) is the 8 bytes of a binary64 item where GnuCOBOL gives it a DISPLAY temporary of 38 to 96 digits (`LENGTH(FUNCTION SQRT(I))` is 96 there); a DISPLAY temporary is its true digit count where GnuCOBOL's is a GMP size estimate that may exceed it by one (`NUMVAL("-9223372036854775808")` is 19 here, 20 there); and a call the binder folded into a literal (`FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION LENGTH(X))`, which GnuCOBOL refuses) is measured as that literal's own field, one byte per digit written. The IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE extremes of §8.8.4.4.4 GR3 g) / m) cannot come from this item, whose description follows the value, so they read the nominal S9(30) / S9(21)V9(9) below. An INDEX function's item is the index carrier, 8 positions and 8 bytes. An ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL or BOOLEAN function has a run-time length: LENGTH counts its positions (§15.50.4 r1–r3); BYTE-LENGTH counts 1 byte per alphanumeric position, 2 per national position (D-N1) and — a boolean function having "an implicit usage bit" (§15.2 item 2) — 8 boolean positions to the byte rounded up (§15.14.4 r4: `BYTE-LENGTH(BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 16))` is 2, with 9 positions 2, with 8 positions 1). | DOC-A.1-92b | **Evaluation of an exact-family intrinsic whose ARGUMENT is floating-point**, §15.4.1, required — documentation NOT required by A.1 (voluntary) | §15.4.1 makes the characteristics and representation of a returned value "defined by the implementor" under native arithmetic, and each of these functions is defined by an equivalent arithmetic expression over its own operands. **WiseOwl COBOL's determination: when ANY argument renders as floating-point (USAGE COMP-1 / COMP-2 / FLOAT-SHORT / FLOAT-LONG / FLOAT-EXTENDED), the function's equivalent arithmetic expression is evaluated in IEEE binary64** and the result is then delivered to the receiver by the ordinary rules — unquantized into a floating receiver, quantized through `FromDouble` into a fixed-point one — at the resultant identifier's own scale with the statement's ROUNDED mode when the value IS the transfer, at the working scale with truncation when it is a nested operand (kb/Work PB647). With an all-fixed-point argument list the function stays base-10 and takes the exact carrier its arguments need: scaled `Int128` while the aligned arguments and the sum of what the function adds fit it, and — for SUM, MEAN, RANGE, MEDIAN and MIDRANGE only (kb/Work PB621) — the SDIDI, whose 34 significant digits are NEAREST-rounded, once they could leave it. The latter is the "implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression" §15.4.1 licenses under native arithmetic (cite.py-verified), not an exact value: the receiver's single rounding sees the 34-digit nearest value, so a 35th-or-later digit that decides a carry is already rounded (the double rounding A.1 item 123 states, and which a product avoids only because §14.9.26.4 owns its transfer, not a function's). The determination is forced rather than chosen: a floating-point argument is a legal class-numeric argument (§8.5.2.12 item 2 + §8.5.2.1 Table 2), and once an operand arrives as binary64 there is no exact value left for an exact evaluation to preserve. Sign discipline is the spec's, not the carrier's — MOD floors and REM truncates (§15.64.4 / §15.77.4), INTEGER floors and INTEGER-PART truncates (§15.44 / §15.49) — so `MOD(-7,3)` is 2 and `REM(-7,3)` is -1 in binary64 exactly as in `Int128`. Pinned by the golden `pb2_float_argument_exact_family`. Before this was implemented, such a program did not merely compute differently: it failed to compile, surfacing a raw Roslyn `CS1503` from the generated C#. | `conformance:cases/15.63.4-Returned-value-rules/da2_function_as_text`; `conformance:cases/8.4.3.3-Reference-modification/pb73_table16_function_type_and_boolean_view`; `conformance:cases/15.67.3-Argument-rules/pb60_numval_one_scan`; `conformance:cases/15.7.4-Returned-value-rule/pb2_float_argument_exact_family` |
| DOC-A.1-33 | **Computer's coded character set — correspondence between alphanumeric and national characters**, §14.9.25 MOVE GR6 · §8.8.4.2.11 locale-based comparison · §15.26.4 r1/r3 (DISPLAY-OF) · §15.66.4 r1/r3 (NATIONAL-OF), required + documented | Both native repertoires are **UTF-16, one code unit per character position** (item 188's substrate — note 188 itself answers a DIFFERENT question, §12.3.7.4's ALPHABET-phrase correspondence; THIS row is the character correspondence item 33 demands), so the correspondence is the **TOTAL IDENTITY, both directions**: every alphanumeric character's national correspondent is the same code unit, and vice versa. Consequences, each deliberate: **(1)** DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF **argument-2 is accepted and vacuous** — §15.26.4 r2 / §15.66.4 r2 substitute only for a character "that has no corresponding" representation, and under a total correspondence no such character exists (the §15.26.3 r2 / §15.66.3 r2 class and one-position screens still bind the argument); **(2)** the r3 **EC-DATA-CONVERSION is unreachable by declaration** from any character pathway — a conforming determination (r1 grants the correspondence to the implementor), not an accidental dead branch; **(3)** §14.9.25.4 GR6's alphanumeric→national MOVE conversion is the same identity (the reverse direction is not a MOVE at all — §14.9.25.3 SR10 / Table 16 forbid a national sender into an alphanumeric receiver, COBOL0819, and DISPLAY-OF is the sanctioned conversion); **(4)** CONVERT's NAT→ANUM and ANUM→NAT character legs (§15.19.4 r1/r3, whose NOTES name DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF as "the same facility") likewise never substitute. ⚠ The 8-bit BYTE serialization of usage DISPLAY (CONVERT's ANUM→HEX/BYTE legs) is a **separate** §8.1.2 NOTE 2 determination (item 209's one byte per DISPLAY position), and it is PARTIAL: a code unit above 0xFF has no one-byte image. **Decided disposition (2026-08-09, RV-15.19.4-2): the serialization substitutes `'?'` (0x3F) and sets EC-DATA-CONVERSION** — §15.19.4 r2 carries no substitution sentence because the standard's model assumes a total serialization; where ours is partial, the r1/r3-analogous substitution+EC is the smallest extension of the standard's own machinery, visible under checking and never silent (`StorageByte.ImageByte`, the one run-time storage-image reader, which CONVERT's `RawBytes` and every REDEFINES view share, item 31; pinned by `Convert_ByteSerializationSetsDataConversion_WhenChecked_2023`). CONVERT's ANY source reads an item's RAW STORAGE bytes per the documented representations themselves (items 205/208/209/215, D-N1 UTF-16BE for national — `OperandText.AsStorageImage`, the one storage channel). Implemented in `CobolIntrinsics.Repertoire` (the identity, both directions); pinned by the golden `pb59_repertoire_identity` and the re-derived `national_intrinsics`. | `conformance:cases/15.26.4-Returned-value-rules/pb59_repertoire_identity`; `conformance:cases/15.2-Types-of-functions/national_intrinsics` |
| DOC-A.1-93 | **Function returned values — returned value length exceeds implementor-defined limits**, §15.4 Returned values, required + documented (the value returned on excess shall be documented) | The maximum length of a returned value is **1,073,741,791 character positions** (`0x3FFFFFDF`, `CobolIntrinsics.ReturnedValueMaximum`): the CARRIER's own ceiling, since a returned value is a native .NET `System.String`, and the same number A.1 item 62 documents for a dynamic-length item. The standard leaves the number to the implementor, so CLAUDE.md rule 1's precedence takes GnuCOBOL's answer, and GnuCOBOL 3.2 imposes no smaller bound (measured, kb/Work PB2631: a 10,000-position UPPER-CASE, REVERSE, CONCAT and SUBSTITUTE each return all 10,000 positions). It is NOT the 8,191-position literal maximum (§8.3.3.4.3 SR1, `CobolLiteral.MaxLiteralPositions`): that bounds what source text can write, and a returned value is sized by run-time data. When a function's returned value would exceed the maximum, **EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is set to exist** exactly as §15.4's own sentence prescribes, and **the value returned is the §15.3 checking-off default — a zero-length value** (with checking enabled the raise is fatal and no value is returned). ONE guard asks it, `CobolIntrinsics.ReturnedValueOverMaximum`, at every function whose returned value can outgrow its arguments, before the value is allocated where its length is known first: `Concat` (the sum of the argument lengths), `Substitute` (an argument-3 longer than its argument-2, asked as the value grows), `Convert` (two hexadecimal digits per byte, two bytes per national position), `BaseConvert` (the base-2 re-expression of a base-16 input is four digits per input digit) and `BooleanOfInteger` (argument-2 itself — a §15.4 rule, NOT §15.13.3 r2's argument rule, which any positive length satisfies; conflating the two was kb/Work PB383). A function whose returned length follows an argument (UPPER-CASE, LOWER-CASE, REVERSE, TRIM, DISPLAY-OF, NATIONAL-OF) cannot pass it, because no item is longer than the carrier. Every guard returns through the one `ExceptionState.ArgumentErrorZeroLength` mechanism. §15.12.3 r3's input-side maximum has no separate A.1 number: it is bounded by this determination, and the row says so rather than inventing one. | `conformance:cases/A.1-Implementor-defined-language-element-list/l1_returned_value_length_limit`; `conformance:cases/A.1-Implementor-defined-language-element-list/l1_returned_value_limit_boolean_repro`; `unit:ReturnedValueMaximumTests.TheMaximum_IsTheNumberRowDocA193Publishes`; `unit:ReturnedValueMaximumTests.OnePastTheMaximum_IsTheZeroLengthValue`; `unit:ReturnedValueMaximumTests.PastTheLiteralMaximum_ReturnsTheWholeValue` |
| DOC-A.1-50 | **DELETE FILE statement — validation of fixed file attributes**, §14.9.10.4 GR19, required + documented | **The validated set is EMPTY.** GR19 requires the implementor to *define* which of the §9.1.6 fixed file attributes DELETE FILE validates; it nowhere requires the set to be non-empty, and an empty definition is as complete a definition as any other. WiseOwl COBOL validates **none** of them — not the organization, prime or alternate record keys, SUPPRESS WHEN attribute, code set, logical or physical record sizes, record type, key collating sequence, or record delimiter — **uniformly across every organization and storage medium** (GR19's second sentence permits the set to vary by organization or medium; ours does not, which is the simpler determination to state and to rely on). **The consequence, stated so nobody re-derives it as a defect:** GR18 sets '39' when the connector's attributes and the physical file's do not match, so with nothing validated there is nothing to mismatch and **'39' is unreachable from DELETE FILE BY DEFINITION, not by omission** — a DELETE FILE through a connector that contradicts the physical file succeeds with GR20 a)'s '00'. This is the determination the standard asks for, and it replaces the deferral ("documented non-support until a physical-attribute store exists") that stood in §3 until 2026-08-31; a deferral is not a definition. Implemented at `FileRegistry.DeleteFile`, pinned by `2023/delete_file_attribute_set_empty` (organization AND record size contradicted; still deletes). ⚠ **This says nothing about OPEN.** A.1 item **129** (§14.9.27.4 GR10) is a SEPARATE required obligation with a DIFFERENT answer — its validated set is not empty — discharged by the row below (kb/Work PB193). | `conformance:cases/9.1.13.6-Permanent-error-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/delete_file_attribute_set_empty` |
| DOC-A.1-71 | **FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause — TO phrase meaning and rules**, §12.4.5 SR5 and SR6, required + documented | §12.4.5.1 prints the TO phrase as a LIST — `ASSIGN [TO] {device-name-1 \| literal-1} …`, the ellipsis on the inner brace pair in every format — and §12.4.5.2 SR5 makes "the meaning and rules for the allowable specification of device-name-1 and the value of literal-1" the implementor's. **The determination (CLAUDE.md rule 1: ISO leaves it open → GnuCOBOL, whose documented form is a device word followed by one file name): the TO phrase is EITHER one operand, which names the physical file, OR a DEVICE CLASS — `DISK` or `PRINTER` — followed by one operand, which names the physical file.** Both device classes denote a file of the host file system, so the class word selects nothing further: `ASSIGN TO DISK "a.dat"` and `ASSIGN TO "a.dat"` name the same file. Every other list — two file names, three or more operands, a literal before another operand, or a leading word that is not a provided class (a console device such as `KEYBOARD` is not: a file connector here is always a host file) — is refused BY NAME, **COBOL2256**, citing SR5 and this row. **What an operand names:** literal-1's value, or device-name-1's spelling, is mapped to a host path by `CobolFile.ResolveHostPath` — a target already carrying a `.`, `/` or `\` is used verbatim; any other is lowercased and given a `.txt` extension in the current directory — the same mapping item 73 applies to data-name-1's content. The host path is then made ABSOLUTE against the current directory at the association, and that absolute spelling is the physical file's identity to the run unit: Table 19's arbitration and the keyed record stores compare it case-insensitively on Windows and macOS and case-sensitively elsewhere (`HostFile.PhysicalFileComparer`, kb/Work PB2748), so `data.dat` and `./data.dat` are one physical file and, on Linux, `Cust.dat` and `cust.dat` are two; a symbolic or hard link remains a second spelling. **A word that is BOTH a declared constant-name and a device-name-1 (kb/Work PB2500):** §12.4.5.1 admits `{device-name-1 \| literal-1}` at one position, §13.10.3 SR2 admits a constant-name wherever a format specifies a literal, §8.3.2.1 4) lets one word be a system-name and a user-defined word, and §12.4.5.2 SR5 leaves the meaning of both to the implementor, so the standard does not say which reading wins. ⚠ DETERMINATION (ISO leaves it open → GnuCOBOL, which substitutes the declared constant): **the program's own declaration of the word wins** — the same answer the LOCALE clause's external-locale-name-1 (item 181) and the ALPHABET clause's code-name (item 184) already give. A word that names a constant entry is literal-1 "as if … written" (§13.10.4 GR1) and meets §12.4.5.2 SR4 as a written literal does (an alphanumeric literal, not zero-length; a numeric, national, boolean or zero-length constant is **COBOL2645**, naming the constant), a constant whose own entry was refused reports at the entry only, and a word that names no constant is device-name-1, its own spelling. In a two-operand list the leading word is read as the device class when it spells one even if the program declares a constant of that spelling (the only allowable two-operand list is class + name, and the constant reading would be a list of two names); the second operand is read as any single operand is. The word reaches `AssignTargetRule.WordText` through `LiteralEnvironment.ReadConstant`, the one constant lookup the SPECIAL-NAMES and AS-phrase positions already use. **SR6 (the syntactical combinations with data-name-1):** all three are allowed — the TO phrase alone, `ASSIGN USING data-name-1` alone, and both together, in which case §12.4.5.3 GR3 b) lets the content win (item 10). The list is read in ONE place, `AssignTargetRule.Resolve`; the grammar (`CobolIO.g4#assignClause`, `assignTarget+`) takes the whole general format and used to answer a second operand with the parse error COBOL0308 (kb/Work PB829). | `conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb829_assign_device_class`; `conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb829-assign-target-list`; `conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb2500_assign_constant_name`; `conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb2500-assign-constant-numeric`; `conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb2500-assign-constant-below-2002`; `conformance-test:AssignConstantNameTests.ConstantOfTheWrongShape_IsRefusedUnderSR4` |
| DOC-A.1-72 | **FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause — consistency rules for external file connectors**, §12.4.5 GR1, required + documented | §12.4.5.3 GR1 b) requires the file control entries that reference one external file connector to have *"A consistent specification for data-name-1, device-name-1, and literal-1 in the ASSIGN clause"* and leaves the rules to the implementor. **WiseOwl COBOL's rule: the entries must name the same file target and the same data-name-1, and nothing more.** (1) **The TO phrase is compared by the operand that names the file** (item 71), not by every word written: a leading device class is dropped, a literal is compared by its value and a device-name by its spelling. So `ASSIGN TO DISK "xa.dat"`, `ASSIGN TO PRINTER "xa.dat"` and `ASSIGN TO "xa.dat"` are consistent, and a device-name and a literal with the same spelling are the same name, so `ASSIGN TO XADAT` and `ASSIGN TO "xadat"` are consistent. Item 71's host-path mapping is NOT applied before the comparison: `ASSIGN TO XADAT` and `ASSIGN TO "xadat.txt"` are NOT consistent, although both open the host file `xadat.txt`. The comparison ignores case, so `"Data.txt"` and `"data.txt"` are consistent, even though on a case-sensitive host they name different physical files; the file opened is the one named in the program that executes the OPEN. An entry with a TO phrase and one without are not consistent. (2) **The USING data-name-1 is compared by spelling, qualifiers included, ignoring case.** `IN` and `OF` are the same, so `FNAME IN G` and `FNAME OF G` are consistent; `FNAME` and `FNAME OF G` are not, and neither are an entry with a USING phrase and one without. The check runs only when checking for EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH is enabled. It happens when a second program that describes the external file is activated: the two ASSIGN fields are part of the `SelectFingerprint` each program registers with `ExternalStore.Describe` (built in `OoEmitter.SelectFingerprint`, the one §12.4.5.3 GR1 identity — kb/Work PB1079), and a difference raises **EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH** (§14.8.4.4), which is fatal. **⛔ The two programs still hold SEPARATE STORAGE for an identically-spelled data-name-1, and that is deliberate.** §12.4.5.3 GR3 b) associates the connector with the file named *"in the runtime element that executes the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement"*, which only makes sense if the entries MAY name different data items. GR1 i) shows how the standard words it when it wants the opposite (FILE STATUS: *"where data-name-4 shall reference the same corresponding external data item"*), and §13.4.5.4 GR2 c) 2. does the same for LINAGE; GR1 b) says neither. Implemented at `FileConnector.Associate`, called with the executing program's own rendered specification (kb/Work PB673). | `conformance:cases/A.1-Implementor-defined-language-element-list/l1c09_external_assign_consistency` |
| DOC-A.1-73 | **FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause — USING phrase meaning and rules**, §12.4.5 GR4, required + documented | **The content of data-name-1, with leading and trailing SPACES removed, IS the assign target, and it is then mapped to a host path by exactly the rule that maps literal-1** (`CobolFile.ResolveHostPath`: a target already carrying a `.`, `/` or `\` is used verbatim; any other is lowercased and given a `.txt` extension in the current directory). So `PIC X(20) VALUE "  data/in.dat  "` names `data/in.dat`, and `VALUE "CUSTMAST"` names `custmast.txt`. **The removal of spaces is the determination that makes the feature usable at all** — data-name-1 is an alphanumeric item, so its content is space-padded to its declared size, and an unstripped name would ask the operating environment for a file whose name ends in blanks. **The association is made at every OPEN, SORT and MERGE and at no other statement** (§12.4.5.3 GR3's own timing sentence): one connector reaches different physical files during a run unit (§9.1.21), and a DELETE FILE before the first of those three finds no associated file and takes §14.9.10.4 GR14's successful '05'. **A sort-merge file's own `ASSIGN USING` is associated at its SORT or MERGE exactly as a file's is at its OPEN** (kb/Work PB1097; §12.4.5.3 GR3 names the sort-merge file-name in the same rule): the statement checks the content first, before any phase, and when the association cannot be made "the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement is unsuccessful" — which §3.176 defines as an attempt that "does not result in the execution of all the operations specified by that statement", so nothing is released, sequenced or returned and no USING or GIVING file is touched. A sort-merge file entry has no FILE STATUS clause (§12.4.5.1 Format 4), so the failure has no I-O status to carry; the statement's effect is the observation. **Content that is empty after the space removal, or that carries a character below U+0020, names no physical file**: the association cannot be made, so the statement is unsuccessful with §9.1.13.6 item 2's '31' — the status the standard reserves for exactly this failure. Everything the operating environment rejects beyond that is an ordinary open failure ('30'/'35'/'37'), never an escaping exception: a target the host cannot make absolute (a path longer than the host allows, a NUL) is its own host path (`CobolFile.ResolveHostPath` is total, kb/Work PB2848), so the OPEN meets the host's refusal and reports '35' or '30'. Implemented at `FileConnector.AssociationFailure`, the ONE rule (a pure function of the specification), which `FileConnector.Associate` — the ONE writer of a connector's host path — and `CobolSort.AssociationMade` (the sort-merge file, which has no connector) both ask; §12.4.5.2 SR7's own limits on data-name-1 (alphanumeric, not subordinate to the file's FD) are compile-time, `COBOL1810`/`COBOL1811`. (kb/Work PB324) | `conformance:cases/9.1.13.6-Permanent-error-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb324_assign_using_dynamic`; `conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb746_assign_using_2002`; `conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb1097_sort_merge_assign_using_content`; `unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests.Open_ADynamicTargetTheHostCannotMakeAbsolute_IsAnIoStatus` |
| DOC-A.1-10 | **ASSIGN clause, USING phrase — consistency rules between data-name-1's content and device-name-1 / literal-1**, §12.4.5 GR4, optional + documented if provided | **There are NONE.** §12.4.5.3 GR4's second sentence asks for "the consistency rules, **if any**, that apply between the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1 and either the specification of device-name-1 or the value of literal-1", and "if any" makes the empty set a complete answer. WiseOwl COBOL requires no relationship whatever: where a file control entry writes BOTH phrases — `ASSIGN TO "pb324mix.dat" USING WS-NAME` — GR3 b) applies "when the USING phrase of the ASSIGN clause is specified" with no condition on the TO phrase, so the content wins outright, literal-1 is never used to identify a file, and an entirely unrelated content is accepted rather than diagnosed. **The consequence, stated so nobody re-derives it as a defect:** the inconsistency branch of §12.4.5.3 GR3's closing sentence is unreachable BY DEFINITION, and the '31' this implementation does report comes from the CONTENT rule of item 73 (empty, or a control character) rather than from any comparison with device-name-1/literal-1. There is likewise no device-name-1 vocabulary to be consistent with: the TO phrase's operand is a file-name mapping (item 71), not a device. | `conformance:cases/9.1.13.6-Permanent-error-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb324_assign_using_dynamic` |
| DOC-A.1-129 | **OPEN statement — validation of fixed file attributes**, §14.9.27.4 GR10, required + documented | **The validated set is exactly what each organization's PHYSICAL FORMAT ENCODES.** ⛔ **Owner decision 2026-09-07 (question 24), verbatim: _"Let's match GNUCobol's implementation in spirit. No sidecar of any type."_** (kb/Work PB802) — it REPLACED the `.cbattr` catalog sidecar this determination previously named, and NTFS alternate data streams were considered and rejected with it. WiseOwl COBOL writes and reads NOTHING beside a data file, so a physical file's fixed file attributes are whatever ITS OWN BYTES record. GR10 grants exactly that latitude: "The implementor defines which of the fixed-file attributes are validated during the execution of the OPEN statement. The validation of fixed-file attributes may vary depending on the organization or storage medium of the file." **Three organizations, three answers, each derived from that one rule rather than listed.** **(1) Record sequential with FIXED-length records, and line sequential — NOTHING is validated.** §9.1.7.2: "In record sequential files the length of each record is determined by any information the implementor may add to the record on the physical storage medium (such as record length headers)" — WiseOwl COBOL adds none to a fixed-length one, which is plain bytes — and "In line sequential files the length of each record is determined by the number of characters between the preceding line delimiter and the following line delimiter or the end of file if no line delimiter is present", where the delimiters encode no attribute either. The standard answers every disagreement such a re-read can produce with a SUCCESSFUL completion rather than a refused OPEN: §9.1.13.2 item 3's '04' ("A READ statement is successfully executed but the physical record from the file is shorter than or longer than the minimum or maximum length of records allowed for the fixed file attributes for that file"), item 5's '06' and item 7's '09'. Writing a print, report or extract file and reading it back under a different record description is exactly the idiom those three statuses exist for — measured, a validated record size broke six conforming programs on this repository's own corpus, one into an infinite READ loop — so a '39' there would reject legal source. `RecordLayoutNotice` remains the stderr notice for the arithmetic case and leaves the I-O status alone. **(2) Record sequential with RECORD VARYING — the record-length header must PARSE, and nothing more.** §9.1.7.2's "such as record length headers" is precisely what this processor adds here: a 4-byte little-endian length prefix per record (`RecordFraming`), whose method §12.4.5.11.4 GR5 grants ("If the RECORD DELIMITER clause is not specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record is specified by the implementor") and whose GR1 it obeys ("Any method used shall not be reflected in the record area or the record size used within the function, method, or program"). A first prefix naming more bytes than the file holds is not a framed file at all, so the connector's declared VARIABLE **record type** — a §9.1.6 fixed file attribute — contradicts the medium and the OPEN is unsuccessful with '39'. A prefix that parses but falls outside the RECORD clause's bounds is NOT a conflict: that is item 3's '04' on the READ, which a '39' at the OPEN would make unreachable. A file shorter than one prefix states nothing and is not a conflict. **(3) RELATIVE and INDEXED — whatever the keyed store's COMMITTED META PAGE carries** (the paged store format 6 of `docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-runtime-library.md` 2.2.1.4, read from pages 0 and 1 by `MetaPage.Describes`): the **organization**, the **record type** (fixed or variable), the **minimum and maximum logical record size in bytes**, and the **key table** — each key's byte windows (one per data-name-2 of a SOURCE phrase, kb/Work PB1099), DUPLICATES phrase, SUPPRESS WHEN value and collating-sequence fingerprint (the sequence identified by its weights, not by the alphabet-name that produced them). Those two organizations live in an implementor-defined store whose STRUCTURE is those attributes — an indexed file has one B+ tree per key, ordered under that key's sequence — and the meta page is where that structure is written down — IN THE FILE, as GnuCOBOL's ISAM key definitions are in the file. A file whose meta pages are absent or unreadable is not a store this build can interpret — a whole-store file of an earlier build (format 5 and below, its magic at offset 0) included: '39', loud, rather than a silent misread. **The format's own limits are part of the set** (2.2.1.4): a key is stored as one byte per character position in a B+ tree leaf that holds at most 1 016 key bytes, so a prime key longer than 1 016 character positions, or an alternate key longer than 1 008 (its tree's entry key carries the 8-byte release ordinal after it), and a key table whose descriptors do not fit the meta page (3 927 bytes, at least 50 keys of 64-byte descriptors) are declarations the physical format cannot hold, refused with '39' at the OPEN in every mode, OUTPUT included, before any file is touched (GR25). Under an active APPLY COMMIT clause the prime key is also the identity of a transaction's holding, which carries a kind byte before it (docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-runtime-library.md 2.2.1.10; kb/Work PB3337), so the bound there is 1 015. A ZERO-BYTE file is the one tolerated exception — it holds no records, so it can misread nothing, and it states no attribute to contradict. **(4) A SEQUENTIAL description over a RELATIVE or INDEXED store — the store's ORGANIZATION, when the OPEN would let the sequential connector WRITE.** The keyed store's meta page records the file's organization, and §12.4.5.10.3 GR1 says what that attribute means: "The file organization is established at the time a physical file is created and cannot subsequently be changed." A sequential connector opened I-O over a keyed store read the header as its first record and its REWRITE overwrote it, after which the file opened only with '39' under its own RELATIVE or INDEXED description; one opened EXTEND appended records that follow the frames as bytes no store can parse. So an OPEN I-O or OPEN EXTEND of any sequential organization (record, varying or line) whose physical file is a keyed store (its meta pages describe a store, damaged or not: `MetaPage.Describes`) is the file attribute conflict, '39' (`SequentialConnector.FixedAttributeConflict`; kb/Work PB1098). OPEN INPUT changes nothing and stays unvalidated (below), and OPEN OUTPUT is a creation that establishes a new organization (§14.9.27.4 GR18). ⛔ **THE KEY CHECK HAS A DOCUMENTED RUNTIME OPT-OUT — `WISEOWL_COBOL_KEYCHECK=OFF`**, GnuCOBOL's `COB_KEYCHECK=OFF` under this repository's own naming (`WISEOWL_COBOL_`, never `COBOL_`, which is the external-switch family's prefix). It is read ONCE per run unit, in `FileRegistry`'s constructor, and is registered in `RuntimeConfig` like every other variable the runtime honours. It is part of this determination rather than an escape from it: with it OFF the key table leaves the validated set for that run and the organization, record type and record sizes stay in it. With it OFF the FILE'S key table is still the trees' (one tree per key its meta page records): a connector whose description declares a different key table drives those trees by key NUMBER — a declared alternate key the file has no tree for provides no access path (a READ or START under it is '23', a WRITE gives it no entry), and a tree the description does not declare is not maintained by that connector's statements (a record it writes has no entry there; an entry naming a record it deleted or replaced is passed over, never delivered, because the record no longer carries the entry's release ordinal under that key). ⚖ **Surveyed, not assumed** (the standing latitude rule): GnuCOBOL's own testsuite shows exactly two status-39 cases — `variable-length SEQUENTIAL data integrity` (a RECORD VARYING FD over a file whose record-length header does not parse → `OPEN ERROR: 39`) and `INDEXED undeclared keys` (three FDs on one physical file declaring three, two and one keys; the one whose key table disagrees answers '39', and `COB_KEYCHECK=OFF` opens it) — which is the behaviour reproduced above, organization for organization. ⚠ **This REPLACED a catalog, and the change is owner-visible in two ways.** The keyed store's format is a FORMAT CHANGE: a relative or indexed file written by an earlier build carries no meta pages this build can read and is refused with '39' rather than silently misread.
