| DRV-GR-8.1.3.2-5 | unpopulatable-antecedent | the set of COBOL-repertoire characters this implementation cannot represent graphically is empty: source text and every alphanumeric and national item are held as UTF-16 (ISO/IEC 10646), which encodes every Table 1 basic character and every Annex B extended letter (§7's A.1 item 25) | **§8.1.3.2 GR5**: *"When an implementation does not provide a graphic representation of all characters of the COBOL character repertoire, substitute graphics may be specified by the implementor to replace the characters not represented."* (`cite.py --check 8.1.3.2` → OK, rule 5). | DRV-GR-13.18.16.4-6 | definitional | defines a constraint on the USER's run unit (a CONTROL operand shall not reference a group whose length at run time is zero), and no rule gives its violation a consequence, so §4.4 2) leaves the result undefined and obliges the implementation to nothing | **§13.18.16.4 GR6**: *"Data-name-1 shall not reference a zero-length group item."* (`cite.py --check 13.18.16.4` → OK, rule 6). A zero-length item is a RUN-TIME state (§8.5.4: *"whose length at runtime is zero"*). The group forms §8.5.4 lists are items 1, 2, 5 and 7. Items 1 and 7, and item 2 built on them or on a DYNAMIC LENGTH item, are refused at compile time by **§13.18.16.3 SR5 and SR7** whatever their length (`--check 13.18.16.3` → OK 5), 7)), and those rules are pinned by the pb177 negatives. Item 5, a variable-length logical record with zero character positions (`--check 8.5.4` → OK 5)), is REACHABLE. Measured on the pinned build: an FD with `RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 0 TO 4 DEPENDING ON RL`, a zero-length record read back (`RS=0000`), and `RD … CONTROL IS F-REC`, then INITIATE/GENERATE/TERMINATE, run with no diagnostic and no exception condition. GR6 therefore states what a conforming program may not do, names no exception condition and no result, and **§4.4 2)** supplies the rest: *"The results of violating the formats or rules of standard COBOL are undefined unless otherwise specified"* (`--check 4.4` → OK 2)). Any behaviour conforms, so a golden would pin an implementation choice. | owner: 2026-10-08 |
| DRV-GR-7.2.3.4-4 | unpopulatable-antecedent | the set of source listings this compiler produces is empty: §7's A.1 item 117 (the cobol command has no listing option, and a compilation writes only the assembly, its .runtimeconfig.json and the generated .g.cs) | **§7.2.3.4 GR4**: *"If the SUPPRESS phrase is specified, library text incorporated as a result of COPY statement processing is not listed. If a listing is being produced, the COPY statement itself is listed."* (`cite.py --check 7.2.3.4` → OK, rule 4). | DRV-GR-7.2.3.4-5 | unpopulatable-antecedent | the set of source listings this compiler produces is empty: §7's A.1 item 117 (the cobol command has no listing option, and a compilation writes only the assembly, its .runtimeconfig.json and the generated .g.cs) | **§7.2.3.4 GR5**: *"At the completion of copying the library text into the compilation group, the LISTING directive that is in effect for the COPY statement itself is considered to be in effect, regardless of any LISTING directives in the library text."* (`cite.py --check 7.2.3.4` → OK, rule 5). To observe it, a statement would have to reference the item after its instance ended. **§9.3.14.3** (*"An instance object is destroyed either when it is determined that the object cannot take part in the continued execution of the run unit, or when the run unit terminates, whichever occurs first."*, `--check 9.3.14.3` → OK) makes that set empty by definition. Unlike events 2, 4, 5 and 6, which are pinned by goldens because a later activation or re-growth can see storage restored, event 1 has no later reference. | DRV-GR-14.9.51.4-16 | unpopulatable-antecedent | the set of resources a WRITE needs that another run unit can hold locked is empty: the record being written does not yet exist, so no connector holds its lock (the invalid key condition for an existing key is decided regardless of locks, §14.9.51.4 GR33 and GR42); file-level contention is decided at OPEN by Table 19; and the implementor defines no other locked-record circumstance (§7's A.1 item 152, condition absent) | **§14.9.51.4 GR16**: *"The RETRY phrase is used to control the behavior of the WRITE statement for files opened for file sharing for the case where resources needed to write a record are locked by another run unit. The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase."* (`cite.py --check 14.9.51.4` → OK, rule 16). The antecedent needs a WRITE resource held locked by another run unit. The record a WRITE creates exists only after the WRITE succeeds, so no file connector can hold its lock beforehand. An existing key is the invalid key condition, decided *"regardless of any locks that are associated with the record being accessed"* (`--check 14.9.51.4` → OK 33)) and with locks *"ignored"* (`--check` → OK 42)). File sharing conflicts arise only at OPEN and DELETE FILE (§9.1.13.9 1) and 2), statuses 61/62: *"because an OPEN statement is attempted on a physical file"*, `--check 9.1.13.9` → OK 1)). The only other source, *"circumstances other than a locked logical record"* (`--check 9.1.16` → OK), is A.1 item 152, whose determination is "Condition absent", pinned by `LockedRecordStatusProducersDriftTests`. The lock ceiling (53/54, kb/Work PB707) is this run unit's own count, not another run unit's lock. §14.7.9.3 GR4's retry path (*"If the I/O operation is unsuccessful on the first attempt"*, `--check 14.7.9.3` → OK 4)) is therefore never entered by a WRITE. ⚠ CONTINGENT on §7's A.1 item 152: re-adjudicate if an implementor-defined locked-record circumstance is added. | owner: 2026-10-08 |
| DRV-GR-12.4.6.4.4-3 | definitional | defines a constraint on the USER's run unit (which files one SAME RECORD AREA clause may name while an APPLY COMMIT clause names them), with no consequence given for a violation, so §4.4 2) leaves the result undefined and obliges the implementation to nothing | **§12.4.6.4.4 GR3**: *"The file and record area of a file subject to commit and rollback may not be shared with another such file or record area unless it has been closed, a commit or a rollback has been executed and the APPLY COMMIT clause for the file has been deactivated."* (`cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4` → OK, rule 3). The rule's subject is the program's files and record areas. It names no exception condition and no result, and Annex A.2 does not list it, so **§4.4 2)** supplies the rest: *"The results of violating the formats or rules of standard COBOL are undefined unless otherwise specified"* (`--check 4.4` → OK 2)), and a run unit that allows the situation is *"a conforming run unit, although the resultant execution is not defined by standard COBOL"* (`--check 4.4` → OK 2)). WiseOwl COBOL neither refuses nor checks the SAME RECORD AREA and APPLY COMMIT clause pair: a compile-time refusal would reject source the standard requires an implementation to accept (§4.2.2), and the owner chose to leave the violation undefined and document it (kb/Work PB3539, option (i), 2026-10-23). A violation therefore behaves as an ordinary SAME RECORD AREA, and ROLLBACK restores only what §14.9.36.4 GR3 names: *"All files and data-items referenced in active APPLY COMMIT clauses are restored to the state they were in at the execution of the last COMMIT statement"* (`--check 14.9.36.4` → OK 3)). Any behaviour conforms, so a golden would pin an implementation choice. | owner: 2026-10-23 |
| DRV-GR-12.4.5.9.4-2 | unpopulatable-antecedent | the set of file connectors for which this processor does not support record locking is empty: every organization (sequential, the LINE SEQUENTIAL extension among them, relative and indexed) sets and honours record locks through PhysicalFileTable.LockRecord and PhysicalFileTable.HolderOf, answering '51' to another connector in the same run unit and in a different one, and every host carries the cross-run-unit half (HostRegionLocks.HostOfThisProcess: HandleRegionLocks on Windows and Linux, SidecarRegionLocks on every other host) | **§12.4.5.9.4 GR2**: *"If the processor does not support record locking, record locks have no effect for the associated file connector."* (`cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4` → OK, rule 2). The antecedent is a property of the processor, and this processor supports record locking on every connector it can open. §9.1.16's *"While locked by a given file connector, a record is not accessible to another file connector in the same or a different run unit"* (`cite.py --check 9.1.16` → OK) holds within a run unit (goldens pb683_open_sharing_read_only and l1_lock_mode_omitted_sets_no_lock, whose C2 control answers '51') and across run units (CrossRunUnitKeyedStoreDriftTests and CrossRunUnitSequentialLockDriftTests, each under both region-lock hosts). A connector sets no record lock only where §12.4.5.9.4 GR1 or GR3 says so (FileRegistry.LocksEffective); those rules govern a processor that supports locking, so they never populate GR2's antecedent. GR2's consequent is therefore never reached, and a golden could pin nothing. | owner: 2026-10-23 |
